signals.title: [Bug]: MTP speculative decoding crash with illegal memory access on long sequences (Qwen3.6-27B-FP8, v0.19.1)
signals.text:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Your output of `python collect_env.py` here ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Description When using MTP speculative decoding (num_spec_tokens=5) with the FP8‑quantized Qwen3.6‑27B model as both target and draft model, the engine crashes on long requests. Environment vLLM version: 0.19.1 Model: Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 TP size: 4, fp8 quantization, prefix caching + chunked prefill enabled Speculative config: method=mtp, model=same as target, num_spec_tokens=5 Symptoms The crash occurs after the request has accumulated ~26 k total tokens and has generated >1200 output tokens. Just before the crash, spec metrics become abnormal: accepted tokens equal drafted tokens, acceptance rate jumps to 100%, and the scheduled draft tokens are all -1. All worker processes then fail with torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered in gpu_model_runner.py line 1706 (prev_common_req_indices_tensor = torch.tensor(...)). Excerpt from logs SpecDecoding metrics: Mean acceptance length: 6.00, ..., Avg Draft acceptance rate: 100.0% scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={...: [-1, -1, -1, -1, -1]} ... torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered File "gpu_model_runner.py", line 1706, in _prepare_input_ids prev_common_req_indices_tensor = torch.tensor( To reproduce Serve Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 with MTP speculative decoding using --num-speculative-tokens 5. Send a conversation that grows to 25k+ tokens total. The crash typically happens after 1000+ tokens have been generated. Expected behavior Generation should continue without invalid draft tokens or illegal memory access. Additional notes GPU memory usage was low (~5.4% KV cache), so it’s not an OOM issue. The problem is reproducible; disabling speculative decoding avoids the crash. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Feature]: granitemoe loader should accept FP8_DYNAMIC expert weight_scale tensors
signals.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch ### Summary The `GraniteMoeForCausalLM` weight loader in `vllm/model_executor/models/granitemoe.py` does not route `.block_sparse_moe.input_linear.weight_scale` or `.block_sparse_moe.output_linear.weight_scale` tensors into FusedMoE expert slots. Its expert branches in `load_weights` only match on `.weight`; tensors ending in `.weight_scale` fall through to a generic pass-through that has no mapping for them, so loading raises `KeyError` on `params_dict[name]` in `_load_weights` once it tries to look up the unrecognized name. As a result, FP8-quantized Granite MoE (non-hybrid) checkpoints cannot be served. This issue is scoped to the **`FP8_DYNAMIC`** scheme (compressed-tensors `weights.strategy="channel"`, per-output-row weight scales; dynamic per-token activation scales computed at runtime; no `input_scale` tensor on disk). Producer-side tooling (e.g. `llm-compressor`'s `GraniteMoeHybridParallelExpertsLinear` helper, adapted for the plain `GraniteMoeParallelExperts` module) emits fused expert weight scales with shape `[num_experts, 2*intermediate_size, 1]` on `input_linear` and `[num_experts, hidden_size, 1]` on `output_linear`, which matches exactly what the existing `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8MoEMethod` channel-strategy branch expects for `w13_weight_scale` / `w2_weight_scale`. `FP8_BLOCK` (2D block-shaped weight scales) is explicitly out of scope here; see "Follow-ups". ### Motivation With a producer-side helper that reshapes the 3D fused expert tensor to 2D for quantization and then restores 3D on save (analogous to `llm-compressor`'s existing `GraniteMoeHybridParallelExpertsLinear` for the hybrid architecture), `compressed-tensors` emits `input_linear.weight_scale` and `output_linear.weight_scale` with the correct 3D shapes listed above. The sibling loader for the hybrid variant (`granitemoehybrid.py`) already handles both `.weight` and `.weight_scale` on the fused-expert path. The plain `granitemoe.py` loader is the only piece missing. Without this, FP8 quantization of Granite MoE models (e.g. the G5 family: 20B / 120B / 230B) has no working serving path in vLLM — any attempt to load such a checkpoint will fail at the expert-scale load step. ### Current behavior `vllm/model_executor/models/granitemoe.py` `load_weights()`: ```python if n.endswith(".block_sparse_moe.input_linear.weight"): for e in range(p.size(0)): w1_name = n.replace(".block_sparse_moe.input_linear.weight", f".block_sparse_moe.experts.{e}.w1.weight") ... w1_param, w3_param = p[e].chunk(2, dim=0) new_weights[w1_name] = w1_param new_weights[w3_name] = w3_param elif n.endswith(".block_sparse_moe.output_linear.weight"): ... ``` Only `.weight` matches on the expert branches. A tensor ending in `.weight_scale` falls into the `else` branch at line 481 (`new_weights[n] = p`), is handed off to `_load_weights`, and there: 1. `stacked_params_mapping` (for `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj`) doesn't match. 2. `expert_params_mapping` (from `fused_moe_make_expert_params_mapping` with `ckpt_{gate,down,up}_proj_name = "w1"/"w2"/"w3"`) searches for `f"experts.{id}.w1."` / `w2.` / `w3.` substrings. The unprocessed name `...input_linear.weight_scale` contains none of these, so no mapping matches. 3. The fallthrough calls `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name(name, params_dict)`, which only handles `.k_scale` / `.v_scale` / `.q_scale` / `.kv_scale` suffixes; for `.weight_scale` it returns the name unchanged. 4. `params_dict[name]` then raises `KeyError` because `model.layers.N.block_sparse_moe.input_linear.weight_scale` is not a registered parameter. So the current behavior on an FP8-with-expert-scales checkpoint is a hard `KeyError` at load time, not a silent skip. The fix pattern is straightforward: extend the expert branches in `load_weights` to also match `.weight_scale`, split the 3D tensor per expert the same way the weight is split, and rename to per-expert per-shard names (e.g. `...experts.{e}.w1.weight_scale`). Those rewritten names will then be matched by `expert_params_mapping` in `_load_weights` via the `w1.` / `w2.` / `w3.` substring search, which routes them into the correct `w13_weight_scale` / `w2_weight_scale` FusedMoE slots without any further changes to `_load_weights`. ### Proposed behavior Extend the two fused-expert branches in `granitemoe.py::GraniteMoeModel.load_weights` to match both `.weight` and `.weight_scale`: - `input_linear`: change `if n.endswith(".block_sparse_moe.input_linear.weight"):` to also accept `.weight_scale`. For each expert `e`, slice `p[e].chunk(2, dim=0)` and store under `...experts.{e}.w1.weight_scale` / `...experts.{e}.w3.weight_scale` in `new_weights`. The `n.replace(".block_sparse_moe.input_linear.weight", f".block_sparse_moe.experts.{e}.w1.weight")` call already works for both suffixes because `.weight` is a prefix of `.weight_scale` — the replacement produces the correctly-suffixed name by string-prefix match, the same subtlety the hybrid loader already relies on. - `output_linear`: same pattern, for `...experts.{e}.w2.weight_scale`. Downstream, `_load_weights`'s existing `expert_params_mapping` dispatcher matches on `.w1.` / `.w2.` / `.w3.` substrings and routes the rewritten names into `w13_weight_scale` / `w2_weight_scale` FusedMoE slots via the per-scheme method class (`CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8MoEMethod`). No changes are needed in `_load_weights` itself or in FusedMoE. This differs slightly from the hybrid loader's structure — hybrid's fused-expert branch calls `_load_expert` directly with manually-constructed `experts.w13_weight_scale` names, while the plain loader's two-stage structure (rewrite into `new_weights`, then dispatch in `_load_weights`) hands the per-expert per-shard names through the existing Mixtral-style dispatcher. Both end up in the same FusedMoE slot; the plain loader's fix is a minimal extension of its existing branches. ### Acceptance - A `compressed-tensors` checkpoint for a `GraniteMoeForCausalLM` model with `quantization_config.format = "float-quantized"`, 8-bit float weights (`weights.num_bits=8`, `weights.type="float"`, per-channel `weights.strategy="channel"`), and dynamic per-token activation scales (`input_activations.dynamic=true`), whose experts carry 3D `input_linear.weight_scale` of shape `[num_experts, 2*intermediate_size, 1]` and `output_linear.weight_scale` of shape `[num_experts, hidden_size, 1]`, loads cleanly in vLLM. - Output token quality matches a reference path (e.g. the same model served with attention-only FP8 quantization, or the BF16 baseline ± expected FP8 drift). - No warnings about unused weights or missing scale parameters. ### Scope / non-goals - **In scope:** `FP8_DYNAMIC` only — per-output-row weight scale tensors sliced per expert the same way the weight is (`p[e].chunk(2, dim=0)` for `input_linear`, `p[e]` for `output_linear`). `FP8_DYNAMIC` has no on-disk `input_scale`; activation scales are computed per-token at runtime, so no activation-scale plumbing is needed. - **Out of scope (tracked as follow-ups):** - `FP8_BLOCK` — 2D block-shaped weight scales (after producer-side 2D flatten, or an equivalent 3D layout). The hybrid loader's per-row `chunk(2, dim=0)` slicing does not apply cleanly to block-scale shapes; this needs its own design and will be filed as a separate issue (or rolled into Issue 2 during implementation, since block scales are closer in shape to FP4 sidecar tensors than to per-channel FP8 scales). - FP4 / W4A16-packed sidecars (`weight_packed`, `weight_global_scale`, `weight_shape`, `weight_zero_point`, `weight_g_idx`) — tracked in Issues 2 and 3. - Static FP8 activation quantization (`FP8_STATIC` with an on-disk `input_scale`) — would require a separate branch that does not exist in the hybrid loader today either. ### Alternatives _No response_ ### Additional context ### Affected files - `vllm/model_executor/models/granitemoe.py` ### Reference - Mirror implementation already in `vllm/model_executor/models/granitemoehybrid.py` `load_weights()`. ### Follow-ups - **`FP8_BLOCK` expert support for Granite MoE loaders.** To be filed once this issue lands. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug][XPU] Mamba align-mode prefix caching crashes: "Overflow when unpacking long long" storing state.data_ptr()
signals.text:
### Your current environment
Environment (vllm collect_env, abridged) ``` vLLM version : 0.23.1rc1.dev920+gdd127d82e (main @ dd127d82), VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=xpu PyTorch version : 2.12.0+xpu (XPU build 20250302) Python version : 3.12.3, glibc 2.39, Linux 7.0.0 x86_64 Intel GPU : Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B70 Graphics (Battlemage / Xe2), 32 GB Level Zero driver : 26.18.38308.1-0 Intel Graphics Compiler : 2.34.4 oneAPI compiler : 2025.3.3 vllm-xpu-kernels : 0.1.10.1 triton-xpu : 3.7.1 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug Serving a hybrid GDN/Mamba model (Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6 MoE) with `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align` on the XPU backend initializes fine, then the **engine dies on the first request**: ``` ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long File "vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py", line 626, in initialize_from_forward_context self.state_base_addrs[idx] = state.data_ptr() ``` **Root cause:** `state_base_addrs` is allocated as `dtype=torch.int64` (`mamba_utils.py`, ~line 534). On XPU, Level Zero USM device pointers exceed 2^63, so assigning `state.data_ptr()` into a **signed** int64 tensor overflows. Works on CUDA because device pointers there fall in the signed range. **Repro:** ```bash vllm serve \ --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align \ --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --dtype bfloat16 # XPU backend; send one completion → crash ``` **Suggested fix:** preserve the 64-bit pattern rather than assigning the raw Python int — e.g. signed reinterpret `ptr - 2**64 if ptr >= 2**63 else ptr` (keeps the `int64` buffer the Triton copy kernel already consumes; its address arithmetic is modular two's-complement so it resolves to the correct pointer), or switch the buffer to `uint64`. `--mamba-cache-mode align` prefix caching is marked experimental; this int64 overflow is the first blocker to exercising it on XPU at all. Searched existing issues — none on XPU mamba prefix caching.

signals.title: [Feature] Support `extract_hidden_states` on Model Runner V2
signals.text: ### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch ### Feature Add Model Runner V2 support for `extract_hidden_states`, so the existing hidden-state extraction path works when MRv2 is enabled (ideally via an `ExtractHiddenStatesSpeculator` registered in `init_speculator()`), with the same core semantics as Model Runner V1: - extract configured intermediate-layer `aux_hidden_states` - write them into `HiddenStateCache` through the cache-only extract model - remain compatible with hidden-states KV connectors (e.g. `ExampleHiddenStatesConnector`) - return sampled tokens as draft tokens so verification always accepts ### Motivation `extract_hidden_states` is already supported on Model Runner V1 (`ExtractHiddenStatesProposer`) and documented for draft-model data generation / analysis. MRv2 is becoming the default path for more models, but today MRv2 `init_speculator()` does not register extract and raises: ```python NotImplementedError(f"{speculative_config.method} is not supported yet.") ``` ### Pitch Porting extract to MRv2 would: 1. keep feature parity with MRv1 as MRv2 adoption grows 2. avoid long-lived out-of-tree forks just to preserve an already-supported speculative method 3. reuse the existing extract model / cache-spec / connector stack, mainly adding the missing MRv2 Speculator wiring ### Alternatives 1. **Maintain an out-of-tree / backend-specific MRv2 Speculator** Unblocks local users quickly, but risks divergence from upstream semantics and higher maintenance cost. 2. **Build a separate non-speculative hidden-state export API** Cleaner long-term API maybe, but much larger scope than porting the already accepted extract method to MRv2. 3. **Do nothing / wait without tracking** Leaves a growing MRv1/MRv2 feature gap with no clear roadmap signal for downstream projects. ### Additional context #### Current status on recent `main` - **Model Runner V1**: supported in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` via `ExtractHiddenStatesProposer`, with `use_aux_hidden_state_outputs = True`. - **Model Runner V2**: `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/__init__.py` `init_speculator()` currently registers only `dflash` / `dspark` / Gemma4 MTP / `mtp` / eagle-family (`use_eagle()`). Other methods, including `extract_hidden_states`, fall through to `NotImplementedError`. - There is no `ExtractHiddenStatesSpeculator` (or equivalent) under `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/`. So with MRv2 enabled, a config like: ```python speculative_config = { "method": "extract_hidden_states", "num_speculative_tokens": 1, "draft_model_config": { "hf_config": { "eagle_aux_hidden_state_layer_ids": [1, 2, 3, 4], }, }, } ``` fails at speculator initialization instead of using the existing V1 extract path. #### Related prior art I searched existing issues/PRs for an MRv2 port of `extract_hidden_states` and did **not** find a dedicated tracking issue/PR. Closest related work: - Original RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33118 - Initial feature: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/33736 - Docs: `docs/features/speculative_decoding/extract_hidden_states.md` - Follow-up MRv1 / connector / hybrid work (not MRv2 port), e.g.: - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39949 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43869 - https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49301 There are active MRv2 speculative-decoding efforts (Eagle/MTP/draft-model, etc.), but none appear to cover `extract_hidden_states` specifically. #### Why this matters As MRv2 becomes the default for more models, lacking extract support creates a feature gap for draft-model data generation and for out-of-tree backends that are migrating users to MRv2 while still needing hidden-state export. #### Questions for maintainers 1. Is it correct that MRv2 does not support `extract_hidden_states` yet? 2. Is there already a tracking issue/PR that I missed? 3. Is there a rough priority or timeline for an MRv2 port (e.g. an `ExtractHiddenStatesSpeculator`)? Happy to help prototype or review an in-tree MRv2 implementation if that matches upstream direction. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_vllm ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary Long-running vLLM engine processes leak host memory (VmRSS/VmData) on paths where a libtorch stable-ABI custom op with a `str` argument is dispatched **eagerly** in the hot loop. Each such call leaks ~48 bytes; over hours this grows unbounded and can OOM the engine (~0.5 GB/hour under continuous load in our reproduction). The root cause is **not in vLLM** — it is a bug in PyTorch's stable ABI, which heap-allocates a `std::string` when unboxing a `str` argument and never frees it. **Upstream issue:** https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191340 ## Where it hits vLLM `reshape_and_cache_flash` is registered as a stable op with a `str kv_cache_dtype` argument: - schema: `csrc/libtorch_stable/torch_bindings.cpp` (`reshape_and_cache_flash(Tensor key, ... str kv_cache_dtype, ...) -> ()`) - impl: `csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu` (`void reshape_and_cache_flash(..., const std::string& kv_cache_dtype, ...)`) - bind: `ops.impl("reshape_and_cache_flash", TORCH_BOX(&reshape_and_cache_flash))` On most paths this op is captured into a CUDA graph and replayed, so it is not re-dispatched per step and the leak does not accumulate. But on the **Voxtral/Whisper realtime streaming** path it is dispatched eagerly — once per attention layer per decode step — so every KV-cache write leaks and the process grows without bound. Any other eagerly-dispatched stable op with a `str` argument is affected the same way. ## Symptoms - Steady, linear host-memory growth (VmRSS/VmData) proportional to decode steps, not to batch size or sequence length. - Invisible to `tracemalloc` (the allocation is C++-side, not Python). - Not reclaimed by `malloc_trim(0)` — the memory is live, not fragmentation. - glibc `mallinfo2().uordblks` grows in lockstep with RSS. - Present only on eager (non-CUDA-graph) dispatch paths. ## Root cause (upstream) In PyTorch's `torch/csrc/stable/stableivalue_conversions.h`, the `str` → `std::string` unboxing (`ToImpl<std::string>::call`) does: ```cpp auto strptr = new std::string(data, length); // heap-allocated TORCH_ERROR_CODE_CHECK(torch_delete_string(handle)); return *strptr; // returns a COPY; *strptr is never deleted ``` Each unbox orphans one heap-allocated `std::string` control object (~48 bytes: `sizeof(std::string)` + allocator overhead; the value's characters are irrelevant since short strings like `"auto"` fit small-string optimization). Fix is upstream: construct the string on the stack instead of with `new`. See https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191340 for details and the patch. ## Impact on vLLM - Realtime/streaming ASR paths (Voxtral, Whisper) that dispatch KV-cache writes eagerly leak continuously and can OOM long-running servers. - Standard batched/CUDA-graph serving is largely unaffected because the op is replayed, not re-dispatched. ## Fix / mitigation - **Real fix:** upstream PyTorch (https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191340). The fix is header-only in the stable ABI, so vLLM's custom-op `.so` must be recompiled. - **Possible vLLM-side mitigations** while waiting for an upstream release: - Avoid re-dispatching stable ops with `str` arguments in eager hot loops (e.g. pass the dtype as an enum/int rather than a `str`, if a non-`str` schema is feasible). - Ensure the affected streaming paths use CUDA-graph capture/replay where possible. ## Reproduction Minimal, self-contained (CPU-only) reproduction of the underlying leak — two no-op stable ops identical except one takes a `str` — is in the upstream issue: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191340 ## Environment ``` torch: 2.11.0+cu130 CUDA: 13.0 OS: Linux (x86_64) ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

Low-frequency: 1 occurrence in ~10 days of continuous multi-user operation. Not reproducible on demand. Docker's restart policy recovered the service automatically. ## Serving configuration - Model: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4 - MoE backend: MARLIN (W4A16 path; native FP4 / CUTLASS FP4 unavailable on sm_121) - Speculative decoding: MTP, num_speculative_tokens=3, draft moe_backend=triton - kv_cache_dtype=fp8, mamba_ssm_cache_dtype=float16 - max_model_len=131072, max_num_seqs=8 - async_scheduling, chunked prefill, VLLM_COMPILE (mode 3), CUDAGraph PIECEWISE Full launch command: ``` vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --served-model-name chat-model --max-model-len 131072 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.70 --trust-remote-code --async-scheduling --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-seqs 8 --moe-backend marlin --mamba_ssm_cache_dtype float16 --quantization fp4 --reasoning-parser super_v3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"moe_backend":"triton"}' ``` ## Crash context From the engine's `dump_input` at crash time: - Crash occurred mid-decode on a single active request: `num_computed_tokens=8192`, 790 tokens scheduled in the failing step - `kv_cache_usage=0.042` — **not** a KV exhaustion / OOM condition - `num_running_reqs=1, num_waiting_reqs=0` - The error surfaced in `async_copy_ready_event.synchronize()` (`gpu_model_runner.get_output`), consistent with an asynchronous kernel fault reported at a later sync point rather than at the faulting kernel itself ## Traceback

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## What happens Since the auto backend resolution started defaulting to `mnnvl` (#47219 / #47589), startup on non-fabric multi-node clusters attempts mnnvl workspace creation, which: 1. Stalls ~30s per workspace attempt (up to 2: non-quant + quant), then logs: - `Failed to initialize FlashInfer All Reduce workspace: [fd_exchange] timed out connecting to /tmp/cuda_fd_xchg_...` - `Failed to initialize FlashInfer Allreduce norm fusion workspace with backend=mnnvl` 2. I'm not sure why but we subsequently hit OOM on worker nodes. Disabling the pass avoids both: `--compilation-config '{"pass_config": {"fuse_allreduce_rms": false}}'` On "vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k3" this did not occur because the mnnvl workspace was not attempted on this topology. ## Expected vLLM should pre-check fabric support before attempting multi-node mnnvl workspace creation, and skip cleanly on IB-only topologies instead of relying on a 30s timeout inside flashinfer. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: draft_model speculative decoding crashes at init under TP>1 when draft hidden_size > target (TRT-LLM fused allreduce+RMSNorm workspace sized from target only)
signals.text: ### Summary With `draft_model` speculative decoding under tensor parallelism (`TP>1`), the engine crashes at init when the **draft model's `hidden_size` is larger than the target model's**. The `fuse_allreduce_rms` compilation pass builds the FlashInfer TRT-LLM fused allreduce+RMSNorm workspace with a token budget derived from the **target** model's `hidden_size` only. When the draft model then runs its own forward under TP, its larger `hidden_size` overflows that workspace and `check_trtllm_allreduce_fusion_workspace_metadata` raises, aborting startup. `draft_hidden < target_hidden` and `TP=1` both work; the crash is specific to **`draft_hidden > target_hidden` AND `TP>1`**. ### Environment - vLLM `v0.27.1`, V1 engine, `dtype=torch.bfloat16` - 2×H100 PCIe (80GB), `tensor_parallel_size=2` - `compilation_config.pass_config.fuse_allreduce_rms: True` (default), FlashInfer allreduce backend - Full raw server logs for all arms (`collect_env` included): https://github.com/seongyun1104/depthchart/tree/39b1557/draft_model_tp_bug ### Reproduction | Arm | target (TP) | draft | draft_hidden vs target_hidden | result | |-----|-------------|-------|-------------------------------|--------| | A | Qwen3-30B-A3B (**TP=1**) | Qwen3-4B | **2560 > 2048** | OK (acceptance 83.8%, normal) | | B | Qwen3-30B-A3B (**TP=2**) | Qwen3-4B | **2560 > 2048** | **CRASH** at init | | C | Qwen3-30B-A3B (TP=2) | Qwen3-0.6B | 1024 < 2048 | OK (acceptance 73.1%, coherent) | Arm A vs B isolates the trigger to **`TP>1`**: same `draft_hidden > target_hidden` pair, only the parallelism differs. Arm C shows the same TP=2 target is fine when `draft_hidden < target_hidden`. Arm B command (greedy): ``` vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --override-generation-config '{"do_sample": false}' \ --speculative-config '{"method": "draft_model", "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-4B", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}' ``` (Qwen3-4B `hidden_size=2560` as draft; Qwen3-30B-A3B `hidden_size=2048` as target.) ### Traceback (arm B, verbatim) ``` File ".../vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/allreduce_rms_fusion.py", line 265, in call_trtllm_fused_allreduce_norm ... check_trtllm_allreduce_fusion_workspace_metadata( File ".../flashinfer/comm/trtllm_ar.py", line 1026, in check_trtllm_allreduce_fusion_workspace_metadata raise ValueError(error_msg) ValueError: Workspace validation failed: - token_num (8192) * hidden_dim (2560) exceeds workspace max_token_num (8192) * hidden_dim (2048). This may cause Illegal Memory Access. ``` `hidden_dim (2560)` is the draft (Qwen3-4B); the workspace budget `hidden_dim (2048)` is the target (Qwen3-30B-A3B). ### Where it comes from The fused-allreduce workspace token budget is `max_token_num = max_size // (hidden_dim * element_size)`, and `hidden_dim` is taken from the target model config in the pass. The draft model's forward under TP issues the same fused allreduce with its own (larger) `hidden_size`, exceeding the target-sized budget. Note (not a proposed fix): patching the pass `__init__` to use `max(target_hidden, draft_hidden)` did **not** resolve it — the run still reports `hidden_dim (2048)` in the validation error, so the workspace metadata that is actually checked is created upstream of that pass field. A correct fix has to reach the workspace **creation** site so its stored `hidden_dim` accounts for the draft model. ### Relationship to #50877 / #50932 Same theme (FlashInfer allreduce workspace/buffer under a draft model that adds allreduce traffic), but a **distinct backend**: - #50877 / PR #50932 — the **MNNVL** path (`trtllm_mnnvl_ar`, Lamport buffer rotation); #50932 touches `flashinfer_all_reduce.py` / `fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm.py` and adds an `is_buffer_size_sufficient` admission guard. - This report — the **TRT-LLM fused allreduce+RMSNorm** compilation-pass path (`allreduce_rms_fusion.py` → `flashinfer/comm/trtllm_ar.py`), which #50932 does not touch. Filing separately so the TRT-LLM path is tracked; happy to fold into #50877 if maintainers prefer a single tracking issue.

signals.title: [Bug]: OpenAI `strict` flag on tool definitions is rendered into the model-visible chat template, changing tool-call behaviour
signals.text: ### Your current environment vLLM 0.24.0, `Qwen3.6-27B-FP8`, TP=2 (2× RTX 3090), served via `/v1/chat/completions`. Requests below go **directly to vLLM** (no gateway/proxy in the path). ### Describe the bug The request-level `strict` flag on a function definition (`tools[].function.strict`, part of the OpenAI protocol) is passed through to `apply_chat_template()` and therefore serialized verbatim into the `<tools>` block that the model sees. `strict` is a **server-side decoding directive** — vLLM uses it in `vllm/tool_parsers/structural_tag_registry.py::_any_tool_strict()` to decide whether to attach structural tags. It is not part of the JSON Schema the model needs. Leaking it into the prompt makes it model-visible, and the model reacts to it. #### 1. The field reaches the prompt (minimal, fully reproducible) Same request, only `strict` differing, via `/tokenize`: | `tools[0].function.strict` | prompt tokens | |---|---| | absent | 411 | | `false` | 416 | | `true` | 416 | `return_token_strs: true` shows it rendered inside the tools block: ``` ..."required": ["city"]}, "strict": false} </tools> ``` #### 2. It measurably degrades tool calling With a realistic agent payload (24 tools, ~3.8 KB system prompt, a task where calling a tool is optional), `strict: false` causes the model to emit a **malformed tool call as plain text in `content`** — an arguments-only object with no function name and no `<tool_call>` wrapper — instead of a real tool call. `finish_reason` is `stop`, `tool_calls` is empty. Identical request, only `strict` differing, 5 trials each, non-streaming: | `strict` | `tool_calls` | malformed call leaked into `content` | |---|---|---| | absent | **5/5** | 0/5 | | `false` | 0/5 | **4/5** | Example of what lands in `content`: ```json {"command": "cat << 'EOF' > \"$(dirname '$WORKSPACE')/essay.md\"\n...", "description": "Write essay to file"} ``` #### 3. It is semantic, not prompt-length noise Adding a **neutral filler string of the same token cost** to every tool description, with `strict` absent, does *not* reproduce it: | variant (24 tools, 5 trials) | `tool_calls` | |---|---| | `strict` absent | 4/4 | | `strict: false` | **0/4** | | `strict` absent + equal-length filler text | 4/4 | So it is the *meaning* of `"strict": false` in the tools block, not the extra tokens. #### 4. `strict: false` and absent take the identical server-side path `_any_tool_strict()` returns `False` for both, so with `tool_choice="auto"` both skip structural tags: ```python if tool_choice == "auto" and not _any_tool_strict(tools): return None ``` The only difference between the two requests is therefore what the **model** sees. ### Expected vs actual **Expected:** `strict` is consumed by the server to select the decoding strategy and does not appear in the rendered prompt. `strict: false` and an absent `strict` should be behaviourally identical, as the structural-tag code already treats them. **Actual:** `strict` is rendered into `<tools>`, and `strict: false` measurably degrades tool-call formatting relative to omitting the field. ### Where it happens `vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py`: ```python tool_dicts = [tool.model_dump() for tool in request.tools] ... tool_dicts=tool_dicts, # -> apply_chat_template(tools=...) ``` `model_dump()` is called with no `exclude`, so the whole function object — including `strict` — is handed to the chat template, which serializes it into `<tools>`. ### Suggested fix Exclude `strict` from the dicts passed to `apply_chat_template()`. vLLM has already consumed it (`_any_tool_strict()`) before this point, and a chat template has no way to know which fields are protocol-level rather than part of the function schema. ### Notes / limitations - The behavioural degradation (#2) needs a large, realistic tool set. It did **not** reproduce with 2, 3, or 6 tools, nor with the first 16 or 20 tools of the same set — in those cases both variants behave identically. The prompt-leak itself (#1) reproduces minimally with a single tool. - I have not tested >0.24.0. Between v0.24.0 and v0.27.1 I could find no merged PR touching this path (#40894 and #42292 are both already ancestors of v0.24.0). - This may be as much a chat-template question as a vLLM one, but vLLM controls what is passed to the template.
signals.author: datanerdie

signals.title: [Bug] Streaming completions end with no finish_reason / no [DONE] — xgrammar "Failed to advance FSM" is one logged trigger, but some drops are fully silent (no engine error)
signals.text: ### Summary While serving a Qwen 3.8 27B NVFP4 checkpoint with `--enable-auto-tool-choice` (xgrammar FSM backend for tool-call constrained decoding), the engine logs a `Failed to advance FSM` ERROR for some requests, and the HTTP SSE stream for those requests terminates **without a final `finish_reason` chunk and without the `data: [DONE]` sentinel**. Downstream clients (e.g. an OpenAI-compatible SDK consumer) receive only partial content and cannot distinguish a normal completion from a truncated one. Importantly, the "no `finish_reason` / no `[DONE]`" symptom is **broader than the logged FSM error**: on the same instance we also observed client-visible mid-stream drops where the engine logs **nothing** — no `Failed to advance FSM`, no ERROR, no disconnect, no abort — while the engine is healthy and actively serving. The API-server layer logs no error, warning, or client-disconnect event for the affected request in either case. So the missing terminal chunk is the real user-facing bug; the FSM failure is one observed (logged) trigger, and a clean-engine occurrence suggests the failure path can be silent. Per the FSM error message itself ("Please file an issue"), filing here. ### Environment - vLLM: `0.26.1rc1.dev298+g1ea84d74b.d20260803` (pip inside container) - Image: `eugr/spark-vllm:latest` (sha256:1d335d4fb3d1c5dce6e79f87a4019a04e98fa9ceb7b894d50d413159382ab6c6) - Hardware: NVIDIA GB10 (Grace Blackwell, sm_121a), CUDA 13.x (eugr image) - Model: Qwen 3.8 27B NVFP4, `served-model-name qwen3.8-27b` - Single node, TP=1 ### Launch command ``` vllm serve /model \ --served-model-name qwen3.8-27b \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.45 \ --max-model-len 262144 \ --max-num-seqs 4 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}' ``` ### Observed engine logs (timestamps UTC) ``` (EngineCore pid=304) ERROR 08-18 23:06:09 [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request chatcmpl-ab4973be9a4cd69e-86178720 for tokens 271. Please file an issue. (EngineCore pid=304) ERROR 08-18 23:10:38 [backend_xgrammar.py:162] Failed to advance FSM for request chatcmpl-803065810e03ac9d-8173c9f7 for tokens 271. Please file an issue. ``` Additional distinct requests with the same error signature were observed within a 48 h window on the same instance (request IDs available on request): 2 further occurrences, all at token 271 or nearby. Note: both FSM failures reported "for tokens 271" — the FSM advance failure appears reproducible at a specific token position, which may indicate a particular token id / grammar state combination. ### Symptoms 1. Client receives a partial stream of content deltas, then the connection ends cleanly (no HTTP error, no 5xx). 2. No final chunk with `finish_reason`, no `data: [DONE]`. 3. Engine continues serving subsequent requests normally (KV cache ~4–6 %, 0–2 running requests, no preemptions, no OOM, no crash). 4. **Two observed variants**, both producing the identical client symptom: - (a) Logged trigger: the single `Failed to advance FSM` ERROR above, nothing else. The API server logs no error/warning/disconnect. - (b) **Silent trigger**: no engine log line at all — no FSM error, no ERROR, no disconnect, no abort — while the engine is healthy and actively serving (e.g. 00:43 and 00:48 UTC 2026-08-19, `Running: 1 reqs`, ~15–20 tok/s generation, clean 00:40–00:50 UTC window). ### Impact Clients cannot distinguish this from a benign early stop. An agent framework treating "no finish_reason + partial text" as an error will surface it as a truncated/incomplete response, causing user-visible failures and wasted retries. Frequency observed: ~18 client-visible drops over ~2 days on a moderately loaded single-node box (plus 2 more on 2026-08-19, one of which was the silent variant), and several of the affected completions were ordinary text turns (not tool calls). Because the silent variant logs nothing, operators cannot currently correlate a client-side truncation with any server event. ### Questions / hypotheses (for maintainers) - Is there a known fix for FSM advance failure in the xgrammar backend (the line in question: `vllm/v1/.../backend_xgrammar.py:162`)? - Should a failed FSM advance degrade gracefully (e.g. fall back to unconstrained decoding for the remainder of the sequence) and still emit a terminal `finish_reason` so clients get a clean stream end? - Is the "for tokens 271" repeat a clue to a specific grammar state (e.g. a token that is valid per the tokenizer but invalid in the FSM)? - **What causes the silent variant** — a `finish_reason` / `[DONE]` terminal chunk being dropped with no server-side error at all? Is there any code path where the API server closes the SSE stream for a healthy in-flight request without logging, and could a WARN/DEBUG be added so this is diagnosable? ### Minimal repro status No minimal prompt-level repro yet; the failure correlates with specific request content during normal chat/tool-call traffic. Happy to capture the full request payload for a failing request ID if maintainers want it (data contains private content — will redact or share via a secure channel).
signals.author: Duckmanjbr

signals.title: [Bug]: Kimi-K3 chunked prefill diverges from one-shot prefill under TP8/PP2
signals.text: ### Your current environment <details> <summary>Relevant environment</summary> ```text vLLM commit: aa9903490c616dc6871e5acc62cec7bb1e5e9434 Platform: Linux aarch64 GPU: NVIDIA GB200 CUDA: 13.0 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 Python: 3.12 Model: moonshotai/Kimi-K3 Tensor parallel size: 8 Pipeline parallel size: 2 Prefix caching: disabled CUDA graphs: disabled (--enforce-eager) ``` </details> ### 🐛 Describe the bug Kimi-K3 produces substantially different hidden states when the same 32,768-token request is evaluated as one prefill step versus four 8,192-token chunked-prefill steps. The comparison uses: ```text Model: moonshotai/Kimi-K3 Topology: TP8 / PP2 Input: identical 32,768 token IDs Control: --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 Candidate: --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 Other model/runtime settings: identical ``` We instrumented the model to capture activations at several one-based completed-layer boundary IDs. The instrumentation only observes/copies activations; the earliest mismatch occurs on the first PP stage, before the PP boundary. #### Expected behavior For an identical causal input, one-shot prefill and chunked prefill should produce numerically equivalent hidden states, within normal BF16/kernel tolerances. #### Observed behavior The first 8K chunk is bit-identical at every captured boundary. Boundary ID 2 also remains bit-identical for all four chunks. Starting at boundary ID 4, chunks 1-3 diverge, and the error grows through the network: | Boundary ID | Later-chunk relative L2 range | Later-chunk cosine range | |---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 0 | 1.0 | | 4 | 0.0167-0.0197 | 0.99981-0.99986 | | 5 | 0.0461-0.0615 | 0.99811-0.99894 | | 12 | 0.0664-0.0721 | 0.99741-0.99780 | | 13 | 0.0669-0.0730 | 0.99734-0.99777 | | 47 | 0.2414-0.2434 | 0.97039-0.97086 | | 93 | 1.2652-1.3944 | 0.04287-0.15671 | Boundary 47 is the PP partition boundary. Because the first mismatch is already present at boundary 4 on the first PP stage, PP transport does not appear to be the origin, although later residual mixing amplifies the error. The same one-shot-versus-4x8K divergence reproduces with both KDA prefill backends: - FlashKDA - Triton `chunk_kda_with_fused_gate` This makes a backend-specific FlashKDA numerical issue unlikely. The pattern instead suggests that some state used around the full KDA layer path is not equivalent across chunk boundaries. Candidate areas include causal-convolution state, per-layer state-cache binding/indexing, or recurrent-state gather/writeback. This is a hypothesis, not a claimed root cause. #### Why this is a correctness bug - The weights, token IDs, topology, and runtime settings are identical; only the prefill chunk size changes. - Chunk 0 is bit-identical through the entire model, while later chunks diverge. This is the signature expected from cross-chunk state continuity rather than ordinary batch-shape numerical variation. - The final-layer relative error exceeds 1.2 and cosine similarity falls as low as 0.043, far beyond reasonable BF16 tolerance. - The mismatch begins before the PP boundary and reproduces under two independent recurrent KDA prefill implementations. #### Related upstream work - #51039 investigates a different long-context Kimi-K3 corruption symptom. Its isolated KDA recurrent-kernel tests found one-shot/chunk-threaded recurrence to be exact, but those tests do not cover the full KDA layer wrapper, including Q/K/V causal convolutions and vLLM state-cache plumbing. - #51483 fixes a stateless one-token first chunk being classified as decode. The chunks in this reproduction are 8,192 tokens, so that trigger does not apply. A useful minimal regression test would compare one-shot and split execution of the complete Kimi-K3 KDA layer path while checking, in order: 1. Q/K/V causal-convolution outputs and stored conv states. 2. Gathered recurrent initial state. 3. Final recurrent state before cache writeback. 4. Layer output after residual mixing. ### Before submitting a new issue... - Searched existing and past vLLM issues. The related reports above do not cover this deterministic 32K one-shot versus 4x8K full-model mismatch.
signals.author: yubofredwang

signals.title: [RFC]: DeepSeek-V4 Performance Optimization on ROCm (Phase Two)
signals.text: ## Motivation. > Continue working on phase one: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/41820. DeepSeek-V4 introduces CSA (Compressed Sparse Attention, `compress_ratio=4`), HCA layers, and a large MoE backbone. A side-by-side trace comparison of the vLLM decode path against vLLM-ATOM on ROCm shows that vLLM still leaves measurable performance on the table. The gaps cluster into three areas: 1. **Unfused mHC kernels.** vLLM runs `mhc_post` and `mhc_pre` as separate kernels, and `mhc_pre_big_fuse` + `add_rmsnorm_quant` as two kernels, while ATOM fuses each pair into a single kernel (`mhc_fused_post_pre` and `mhc_pre_big_fuse_rmsnorm`). Every extra kernel launch on the decode critical path costs launch latency and cache/register thrash. 2. **Serial execution where overlap is possible.** ATOM forks auxiliary HIP streams to run compressor GEMMs (CSA pre-attention), SWA KV insertion (HCA), and the MoE router/shared experts concurrently with the main stream. vLLM executes all of these serially. 3. **Slower attention support kernels.** ATOM replaces the vLLM CSA top-k selection kernels and the post-attention batched GEMMs (`torch.mm` + `manual_unroll`) with dedicated optimized kernels (e.g., `batched_gemm_bf16_kernel`). An earlier attempt at closing gap #2 — PR #51794, which enables three-stream overlap for CSA pre-attention — is currently a draft: the overlapped region itself is faster when there is no bubble, but some ranks see a much slower tail all-reduce due to inter-rank latency jitter. The un-optimized kernels running in the parallel streams contend for hardware resources and desynchronize ranks. This suggests the correct order of work is: **replace the kernels with ATOM's optimized versions first, then enable stream overlap on top of them.** ## Proposed Change. Port the ATOM-optimized decode path into vLLM's ROCm DeepSeek-V4 implementation, using the ATOM trace as the reference for each change. The work is organized per module: ### 1. CSA - [ ] **Fuse mHC kernels**: merge `mhc_post` + `mhc_pre` into `mhc_fused_post_pre`, and `mhc_pre_big_fuse` + `add_rmsnorm_quant` into `mhc_pre_big_fuse_rmsnorm`. #52737 - [ ] **Pre-attention three-stream overlap**: Before the input GEMMs, fork three HIP streams: (1) **default stream**: fused wqa+wkv GEMM → q/kv RMSNorm → wq_b → qnorm/RoPE → SWA KV insert; (2) **aux stream 0**: main-compressor wkv_gate GEMM → compress kernels (compressed KV cache write); (3) **aux stream 1**: indexer-compressor wkv_gate GEMM → K-cache write. After the join, the indexer weights GEMM, the indexer q-side (wq_b + fused q RoPE+quant), the sparse indexer op (top-k selection), and the MLA attention run serially on the main stream. Each aux stream is a self-contained chain starting from `hidden_states`, so no fine-grained cross-stream dependencies are required. **This item stays disabled (draft) until the kernels in the parallel streams are replaced with ATOM's**. - [ ] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50866 - [ ] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51794 - [ ] **Replace top-k kernels**: between `gluon_deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle` and the core `sparse_attention`, replace the vLLM top-k implementation with ATOM's fused sparse-indexer kernels. #52882 - [ ] **Replace post-attention batched MM**: after `inverse_rope_gptj_kernel` (and before fp8 quant / `cross_device_reduce_2stage`), replace `torch.mm` + `manual_unroll` with `batched_gemm_bf16_kernel`. ### 2. HCA - [ ] **Pre-attention two-stream overlap**: for `c128a` layers (which have no indexer), run the main KV compression concurrently with SWA token insertion on an auxiliary stream. - [ ] **Kernel replacement**: port ATOM's HCA kernels (details to follow in a follow-up analysis). ### 3. MoE - [ ] **Router and shared-experts dual-stream overlap**: run the router computation concurrently with the shared experts on a second stream, then join before the routed experts. - [ ] **Kernel replacement**: port ATOM's MoE kernels (details to follow in a follow-up analysis). ## Feedback Period. _No response_ ## CC List. @Fangzhou-Ai @qli88 @tjtanaa @ChuanLi1101 ## Any Other Things. _No response_ ## Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: [Bug]: Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime permanent engine hang on a specific audio file via /v1/audio/transcriptions (empty multimodal embeddings)
signals.text: > **About this report**: This analysis was produced automatically by **Hermes (an autonomous AI agent)** on behalf of a user. Reproduction happened on a rented cloud GPU instance (vast.ai, RTX 3090 24 GB, CUDA 13.0.2) accessed via SSH — there is no local GPU involved. ### Your current environment ```text OS : Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm) (x86_64) — vast.ai cloud instance GPU : NVIDIA RTX 3090 (24 GB, sm_86) CUDA Version : 13.0.2 Python : 3.12 vLLM Version : 0.27.1 (official image vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1) VLLM Build Commit : 6e448d0ea9bf3d88d898b65449ca6dc2aec170ac Model : mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602 (snapshot 2769294da9567371363522aac9bbcfdd19447add) vLLM serve args : --tokenizer-mode mistral --config-format mistral --load-format mistral --trust-remote-code --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE"}' --max-model-len 16000 --max-num-seqs 1 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --served-model-name whisper-1 ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug Serving `mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602` with vLLM v0.27.1 (V1 engine), one specific WAV file sent to `/v1/audio/transcriptions` makes the **entire engine hang permanently**: - The log floods with `Realtime model received empty multimodal embeddings for 1 input tokens. Returning zero embeddings to avoid engine crash.` (`voxtral_realtime.py:305`). - The GPU stays at **100 % utilization** and VRAM at ~21/24 GB — the engine appears to decode indefinitely (zero embeddings never produce an EOS). - `/health` stops responding, the port stays open but no request is ever answered. The only way out is killing the vLLM process. - Reproduced **twice in a row** at exactly the same audio file (the first 150 requests of the same benchmark batch all succeeded, then this file hangs the server deterministically). The audio file is **not** silent or unusual: 16 kHz, mono, 16-bit WAV, 5.4 s, RMS −24.5 dBFS, peak −3.8 dBFS, 62 % silence. Its RMS/silence statistics are almost identical to 9 sibling files of the same batch that all transcribe fine. **Failing audio file (for reproduction):** https://drop.n0ne.de/u/NZsVNE.wav ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start vLLM as above (Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602, any GPU with ≥ 16 GB VRAM). 2. Wait for `/health` to return OK. 3. POST the attached WAV to `/v1/audio/transcriptions` (multipart `file`, `model=whisper-1` or any served name, `language=de`). A plain curl `-F file=@...` is enough. 4. Observe: the request never returns, `/health` stops responding, GPU stays at 100 %. Expected behavior: the request either returns a transcription (the reference text of this TTS sample is "Zug einfährt auf Gleis sieben, bitte zurücktreten von der Bahnsteigkante."), or the engine survives and continues serving. Actual behavior: permanent engine hang; the whole server becomes unresponsive and must be restarted. ### Logs Excerpt of `vllm.log` during the hang (repeated thousands of times): ```text (EngineCore pid=2044) WARNING 08-19 09:45:46 [voxtral_realtime.py:305] Realtime model received empty multimodal embeddings for 1 input tokens. Returning zero em (EngineCore pid=2044) WARNING 08-19 09:45:47 [voxtral_realtime.py:305] Realtime model received empty multimodal embeddings for 1 input tokens. Returning zero em (EngineCore pid=2044) WARNING 08-19 09:45:47 [voxtral_realtime.py:305] Realtime model received empty multimodal embeddings for 1 input tokens. Returning zero em ``` Meanwhile `nvidia-smi` reports `100 %, 21208 MiB, 24576 MiB` and `curl /health` times out / returns nothing. ### Related issues — checked, none explains this - **#38233** (closed, "Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime hangs/crashes on multiple sessions due to encoder_cache_usage saturation on 16GB GPU") — multiple `/v1/realtime` sessions and encoder-cache saturation on 16 GB. Ours: a **single** `/v1/audio/transcriptions` request, 24 GB GPU, no cache saturation, no sessions. - **#45022** (open PR, "fix boot-OOM / silent-hang / max-len crash on 16 GiB") — fixes boot-time failures on 16 GiB. Ours: boots fine on 24 GB, hangs after ~150 healthy requests at one specific file. - **#44461** (closed, "Fix token feedback timeout silent hang") — a timeout in the realtime `feed_tokens()` background task. Ours: plain transcription endpoint, no realtime session, no token feedback involved. - **#39229 / #39202** ("Fix Voxtral Realtime crash on mixed-batch transcription") — crash with mixed prefill+decode batches. Ours: `--max-num-seqs 1`, strictly one request at a time, no mixed batch. - **#50860** (open, "Resumable (realtime) sessions retain raw mm_feature.data...") — memory retention across realtime sessions. Ours: single short request, no sessions. The common denominator of the existing reports is that the *zero-embedding fallback* in `voxtral_realtime.py` is a known fragile spot; this report adds a concrete deterministic input that turns that fallback into a **permanent whole-server hang** instead of the intended "keep other requests alive".

signals.title: [Bug]: CUDA graph memory profiling estimation is too huge
signals.text: ### 🐛 Describe the bug I ran `Inferact/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-NVFP4` -tp2 -dp4 -ep on 4*4GB300 and saw ``` (Worker_DP1_TP1_EP3 pid=3585771) INFO 08-19 05:56:57 [gpu_model_runner.py:6936] Estimated CUDA graph memory: 118.65 GiB total ``` after such estimation I got fail for sure ``` (EngineCore_DP0 pid=3584999) ERROR 08-19 05:56:57 [core.py:1346] ValueError: No available memory for the cache blocks. Try increasing `gpu_memory_utilization` when initializing the engine (this flag also controls CPU memory reservation on the CPU backend, despite its name). See https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/configuration/conserving_memory/ for more details. ``` I had around a dozen of such standalone sweeps and every time got estimation 118.65 GiB. With `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0` and `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85` the endpoint ran successfully. I suspect that something is too pessimistic in CUDA graph memory profiling estimation. PS I saw similar pessimistic estimation on another tp/dp configs but here it is most outstanding.

signals.title: [Bug]: NemotronParseForConditionalGeneration does not tie lm_head.weight to decoder.embed_tokens.weight, produces garbage output
signals.text:
The output of python collect_env.py ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 Clang version : Could not collect CMake version : Could not collect Libc version : glibc-2.39 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.13.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A XPU used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-7.0.0-28-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 13.0.88 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada Generation Nvidia driver version : 580.173.02 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.16.post3 [pip3] numpy==2.2.6 [pip3] torch==2.13.0+cu130 [pip3] transformers==5.15.0 [pip3] triton==3.7.1 ============================== vLLM Info ============================== vLLM Version : 0.27.1 vLLM Build Flags: CUDA Archs: 7.5 8.0 8.6 8.9 9.0 10.0 12.0; ROCm: Disabled; XPU: Disabled ``` Also reproduced on vLLM v0.26.0 with the same result.
### 🐛 Describe the bug `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-2.0`'s checkpoint does not ship a materialized `lm_head.weight` tensor — its config sets `tie_word_embeddings=True` and the exported checkpoint expects the output head to be tied to `decoder.embed_tokens.weight` instead of duplicating it (a common compact-export convention, and the same convention the model's Transformers reference implementation follows). `NemotronParseForConditionalGeneration.load_weights` in [`vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_parse.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_parse.py) has no fallback for this case: ```python def load_weights(self, weights): lm_head_dict = dict(self.lm_head.named_parameters()) ... elif is_lm_head(name): trimmed_name = ".".join(name.split(".")[1:]) param = lm_head_dict[trimmed_name] with torch.no_grad(): default_weight_loader(param, w) ... ``` `self.lm_head` is only ever populated inside the `is_lm_head(name)` branch, which requires a weight name starting with `"lm_head"` to be present in the checkpoint. Since that name never appears for this model, `self.lm_head` is silently left at its random `nn.Module` init. There is no error, warning, or unloaded-weights report — the server boots and serves requests normally. **Minimal repro:** ```bash docker run --gpus '"device=0"' --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \ -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \ --entrypoint bash vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1-ubuntu2404 \ -c 'pip install -q albumentations timm open_clip_torch einops && \ vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-2.0 \ --dtype bfloat16 --max-num-seqs 8 \ --limit-mm-per-prompt "{\"image\": 1}" \ --trust-remote-code --port 8000' ``` ```python import base64, json, urllib.request with open("document.png", "rb") as f: b64 = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode() payload = { "model": "nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-2.0", "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "text", "text": ""}, {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": f"data:image/png;base64,{b64}"}} ] }], "max_tokens": 2048 } req = urllib.request.Request( "http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions", data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, ) print(json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120))["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]) ``` **Observed:** fluent-looking but semantically meaningless output interleaved with stray ``/`` bbox tokens, unrelated to the input document's actual content. Reproduced against two independent real document images (a rendered PDF page and a synthetic document PNG), ruling out a bad test input. **Expected:** structured markdown output in the model's documented format (`text`), matching the input document's actual content — which is exactly what's produced once `self.lm_head.weight` is manually tied to `self.decoder.embed_tokens.weight` after `load_weights` runs. ### Fix and verification Adding a tied-embeddings fallback to `load_weights` — tie `self.lm_head.weight = self.decoder.embed_tokens.weight` when `config.tie_word_embeddings` (or `config.decoder.tie_word_embeddings`) is set and no `lm_head.*` weight was seen in the checkpoint — resolves it. I verified this fix end-to-end: same request, same image, before/after — garbage output becomes correct structured markdown extraction. The model's own HF repo already ships a runtime monkeypatch that does exactly this ([`vllm_tied_patch/sitecustomize.py`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-2.0/blob/main/vllm_tied_patch/sitecustomize.py)), which suggests this was identified and worked around downstream rather than fixed in vLLM directly. Happy to submit a PR with the fix folded directly into `load_weights`. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the documentation page, which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signals.title: Gemma 4 E2B + LoRA: illegal memory access in lora_expand at engine init once max_model_len >= 87383
signals.text: ## Environment vLLM 0.27.1, flashinfer-python 0.6.16.post3, triton 3.7.1, torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.3 (driver 610.43.02). Reproduced on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, NVFP4 checkpoint) and H100 80GB (SM90, FP8 checkpoint). Also seen on 0.22.1. ## Problem With Gemma 4 E2B and `enable_lora=True`, `LLM(...)` dies during engine init once `max_model_len` crosses ~87.4k: ``` RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. ``` No request and no adapter are needed — the profile run alone triggers it. Chunked prefill is off, so `max_num_batched_tokens` equals `max_model_len` and the profile run runs at the full length. With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` the faulting launch is the LoRA expand kernel: ``` File "vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/lora_expand_op.py", line 248, in _lora_expand _lora_expand_kernel[grid](...) File "triton/runtime/jit.py", line 761, in run RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered ``` reached from the compiled graph as `torch.ops.vllm.lora_expand.default(buf22, [arg20_1, arg21_1], buf17, ...)`. Same file and line on both GPUs, both checkpoints, and on **both** FLASH_ATTN and TRITON_ATTN — it is not an attention bug. Without `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING` it surfaces later at a `torch.cuda.synchronize()` inside Inductor's autotuner, which makes it look like a torch.compile problem. ## The threshold matches a 32-bit offset overflow Bisecting `max_model_len` with everything else fixed, the boundary is exactly **87383**: | max_model_len | result | |---|---| | 80000 | ok | | 87300 | ok | | 87376 | ok | | 87381 | ok | | 87382 | ok | | 87383 | illegal memory access | | 87391 / 87392 / 87450 / 87700 / 100001 | illegal memory access | That boundary is exactly where a 32-bit row offset wraps. E2B's `intermediate_size` is 6144, so the merged `gate_up` activation row is `2 * 6144 = 12288` bf16 elements = **24576 bytes**, and the highest row index is `num_tokens - 1`: ``` (87382 - 1) * 24576 = 2147475456 < 2**31 = 2147483648 -> ok (87383 - 1) * 24576 = 2147500032 > 2**31 -> illegal memory access ``` so the crash condition is `(num_tokens - 1) * 24576 >= 2**31`. `do_expand_kernel` builds addresses from products like `ram[:, None] * input_d1_stride` and `slice_id * input_d0_stride`, where the index terms come from `tl.arange` / `tl.load` and are int32, so one of them wraps at that size. E4B is unaffected (different `intermediate_size`, so the same product doesn't reach 2**31 at these lengths). ## Isolation | case | result | |---|---| | no LoRA, 100k (SM120) | ok | | no LoRA, 100k, FLASH_ATTN (H100) | ok | | no LoRA, 100k, `enforce_eager` | ok | | LoRA, 100k | illegal memory access | | LoRA, 100k, `max_lora_rank=16` | illegal memory access | | LoRA, 100k, `enforce_eager` | `Failed to initialize the TMA descriptor 700` (700 = `cudaErrorIllegalAddress`) | Needs `enable_lora` *and* a long `max_model_len`. Not an OOM — it still crashes at `gpu_memory_utilization=0.75` while the no-LoRA run at the same length is fine. ## Reproduce ```python from vllm import LLM # crashes in __init__; max_model_len=87382 succeeds llm = LLM( model="Neural-ICE/Gemma-4-E2B-it-NVFP4", # FP8 E2B checkpoints crash the same way max_model_len=87383, attention_config={"backend": "FLASHINFER"}, # FLASH_ATTN and TRITON_ATTN also crash kv_cache_dtype="fp8", enable_chunked_prefill=False, enable_lora=True, max_lora_rank=16, limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 0}, ) print("engine init ok") ``` ## Related #48862 — illegal memory access in `lora_shrink` with NVFP4. Different trigger (fires on the first short request), but it's the sibling kernel in the same punica Triton op family, so the two may share a root cause in the offset arithmetic.

signals.title: [Bug][Spec Decode] All-NaN logits row is laundered into an out-of-vocab token id by the rejection sampler (device assert far from origin); NaN-metric blind spot on the verify path; uninit-scratch audit
signals.text: ## TL;DR If any verification row of `target_logits` is all-NaN (numerics upset in the model forward — whatever the cause), the V2 GPU-worker rejection sampler does not fail or fall back: its NaN-poisoned block-argmax chain **emits a token id equal to `vocab_size` exactly**, which propagates through `last_sampled_tokens` → `combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens` → `input_ids` and detonates 1–3 steps later as: ``` /pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Indexing.cu:1524: indexSelectSmallIndex: Assertion `srcIndex < srcSelectDimSize` failed. torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered ``` surfacing asynchronously (typically in `AsyncOutput.get_output → copy_event.synchronize()`), far from the origin. We reproduced and instrumented this end-to-end ~10 times. Open issue #42261 (gemma4 + MTP, same assert, intermittent, restart clears it) matches this signature and is plausibly the same bug. Independently, the engine's only NaN detector cannot see these rows (§ NaN-metric gap), and the same file contains a family of latent uninitialized-scratch hazards (§ audit). ## Mechanism (fully instrumented) Configuration: spec decode (dspark; greedy drafts → one-hot verification path), FULL decode cudagraphs, TP4, sustained mixed traffic. All findings verified against `main` as of 2026-08-17. 1. A verification row of `target_logits` arrives **all-NaN** (in our case the numerics fault was in a custom SM80 attention kernel amplifying garbage KV reads — not upstream's code — but any NaN row triggers the rest). 2. In the verify kernel, acceptance comparisons against NaN are false → the position is rejected. 3. `_rejection_resample_kernel` computes the one-hot residual of the NaN row (still NaN), adds gumbel noise (still NaN), and stores per-block maxima/argmaxes. Captured block dump from a live event, `RESAMPLE_BLOCK_SIZE=1024`, vocab 129280 → 127 blocks: ``` local_max[0..125] = NaN (argmax = each block's last lane — NaN-poisoned tl.max) local_max[126] = -inf (its 768 masked padding lanes beat NaN in this comparator order) local_argmax[126] = 129280 (= 126*1024 + 256, the first PADDED lane) ``` 4. `_insert_resampled_kernel`'s cross-block `tl.argmax` over `[NaN ×126, -inf]` is NaN-poisoned and selects block 126, loads `local_argmax[126] = 129280 = vocab_size`, and **stores it into a valid slot of `sampled`**. 5. `post_update` copies it to `last_sampled_tokens`; the next step's `combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens` writes it into `input_ids`; the embedding gather asserts. The failure is worse than the crash: a NaN row whose position is *not* resampled samples an arbitrary in-vocab token **silently**. The crash is the detectable minority. ## Evidence highlights - Bounds guard on the padded `input_ids` window captured the poison pre-crash across multiple events: always exactly `vocab_size` (129280), always via the resample-insert store (per-store clamp counters), `is_bonus` both true and false across events. - Winning-block value bit pattern captured in-kernel: `0xFF800000` (-inf) at block 126 with NaN elsewhere (full 127-block dump above). - With clamp-at-store instrumentation the engine survives indefinitely (45+ contained events in one window), confirming the single injection point. - Race hypotheses excluded by measurement: a cross-kernel greedy-bit disagreement counter read **zero** across >8k steps while mints continued. ## NaN-metric gap `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS` / `corrupted_requests_total` is implemented in `Sampler.sample()` — which the spec-decode verification path never calls. During all of the above, the metric read 0. The engine is blind to NaN logits exactly where they get converted into OOB tokens. Suggest computing `num_nans` on the verification logits as well. ## Proposed fixes 1. **Guard degenerate rows in the resample chain** (minimal): after the cross-block argmax, validate the selected token id (`0 <= id < vocab_size`) and the winning value (finite); on failure, fall back deterministically (e.g., token 0 or the request's last valid token) and increment a corruption counter. This converts undefined behavior into a counted, bounded event. 2. **Close the NaN-metric gap** so operators can see degenerate rows on the spec path. 3. Optionally: make `tl.max`/`tl.argmax` consumers in this file NaN-safe by masking non-finite values to `-inf` before reduction (several sites). ## Audit: latent uninitialized-scratch hazards in the same file While isolating the above we audited `rejection_sampler_utils.py` and found a systemic pattern: **per-request temperature is re-loaded independently by each kernel of a step** (4 independent loads), and those reads gate *writes* to `new_empty` scratch buffers that later kernels *read* under their own temperature load. Nothing enforces agreement (the sampling-state buffers are persistent device arrays updated between steps; async scheduling lets updates land between kernel launches). Five instances: | # | Producer that skips the write | Buffer | Consumer | Worst case | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | stats kernel non-greedy branch skips argmax store | `target_local_argmax` | verify kernel greedy path | uninit int64 emitted as a token id | | 2 | resample kernel greedy-non-bonus early return | `resampled_local_{argmax,max}` | insert kernel | uninit int64 emitted as a token id | | 3 | stats kernel greedy branch skips sumexp | `target_local_sumexp` (+draft) | verify non-greedy accept path | garbage acceptance probabilities | | 4 | `_compute_cumulative_log_p_kernel` `if temp==0: return` | `cumulative_log_p` | 3 gated read sites | `exp(uninit)` ratios (block-verification mode) | | 5 | residual-mass kernel early returns | `local_residual_mass` | `_compute_global_residual_mass` | garbage residuals (block-verification mode) | We hit none of these in production traffic (measured disagreements = 0), but they are trivially fixable (write unconditionally — the values are already computed or nearly free) and the class-level fix (snapshot sampling params once per step for all kernels) closes present and future instances at once. Zero-initializing the scratch is cheap hardening. ## Environment - Observed on vLLM 0.27.1; all cited code verified present on `main` (2026-08-17). - 8×A100 (SM80), TP4, `cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, prefix caching, fp8 KV. - DeepSeek-V4-Flash + dspark (greedy drafts). The NaN *source* in our reproduction was a custom SM80 kernel (not upstream code); the laundering, metric gap, and audit findings are upstream and model-agnostic — any NaN row from any cause takes the same path. ## Reproduction sketch Inject a single all-NaN row into `target_logits` for one verification position (or run any setup that can produce one) under spec decode with rejection sampling; within that step, `sampled` receives a token id ≥ `vocab_size` (frequently exactly `vocab_size`), and the engine dies on the embedding gather 1–3 steps later with the assert cascade above.

signals.title: [Bug]: `set_splitting_ops_for_v1` early return skips the empty-splitting-ops guard — breakable cudagraph + `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` + spec decode silently rejects every draft
signals.text: `CompilationConfig.set_splitting_ops_for_v1` returns early when the compilation mode is not `VLLM_COMPILE`, which skips the guard that would otherwise disable piecewise cudagraphs for an empty `splitting_ops`. The resulting configuration — piecewise cudagraphs with attention *inside* the graph — silently produces wrong results for any batch whose per-request query length differs from the captured one. Speculative decoding is the case where that happens in practice, and the state is reachable in stock vLLM via `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` (auto-enabled for several architectures). ## The early return ```python def set_splitting_ops_for_v1(self, all2all_backend, data_parallel_size=1): if self.mode != CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE: if self.splitting_ops is None: self.splitting_ops = [] return # <-- skips everything below ``` The guard that is skipped: ```python elif len(self.splitting_ops) == 0: if self.cudagraph_mode == CUDAGraphMode.PIECEWISE: logger.warning_once( "Piecewise compilation with empty splitting_ops does not contain " "piecewise cudagraph. Setting cudagraph_mode to NONE. ...") self.cudagraph_mode = CUDAGraphMode.NONE ``` So `mode=NONE` + `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` leaves `splitting_ops=[]` **and** `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`, which the guard exists to prevent. The guard itself is correct; it is simply not reached. ## Why the resulting state is unsound With `splitting_ops=[]` the attention op is inside the captured region. Piecewise graph entries are keyed by `BatchDescriptor` (`forward_context.py`), whose fields are: ```python num_tokens: int num_reqs: int | None # "Can be None for PIECEWISE ... can handle any number of requests" uniform: bool # "True if all the requests in the batch have the same number of tokens" has_lora: bool num_active_loras: int ``` **No field records the per-request query length.** So these two batches share a key: | batch | reqs x query_len | num_tokens | uniform | |---|---|---|---| | plain decode | 16 x 1 | 16 | True | | spec-decode verify | 2 x 8 | 16 | True | `_is_compatible` states the intent explicitly: ```python # desc.uniform_token_count=None (PIECEWISE) can handle any uniform_token_count ``` That assumption is sound **only while attention is outside the graph**. With `splitting_ops=[]` it is not: attention's behaviour depends on `query_start_loc`, which is frozen at capture and replayed against a different query structure. Result: wrong logits on the verify pass, no error raised. ## Observed effect 8xMI325X (gfx942), Qwen3.8-27B (architecture `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`) + DFlash2 drafter, TP=8, `num_speculative_tokens=7`, `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` (see Scope below for why that flag matters): | configuration | compilation mode | mean acceptance length | |---|---|---| | `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE` -> breakable path, attention inside graph | NONE | **1.00** (0 tokens accepted, drafts still generated) | | `--enforce-eager` (no graphs at all) | NONE | 4.03-5.17 | | `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` -> `VLLM_COMPILE`, attention split out | VLLM_COMPILE | **4.47** | The first two rows share the same compilation mode (`NONE`) — the only difference is whether the forward is captured into a graph, which isolates the graph as the cause. The third row is the corrected configuration; end-to-end it is ~3x a non-speculative deployment of the same model on a coding workload (187-207 vs 66.8 tok/s). A non-speculative deployment of the same model is unaffected, because it only ever produces uniform 1-query decode batches — there is only one query structure, so nothing collides. **That is why this is easy to miss: it needs speculative decoding to surface.** ## Scope — how this state is reached We initially believed we reached the unguarded state through a local patch. That was wrong: everything involved is stock vLLM. 1. `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` is an upstream env (`envs.py`: "Experimental: breakable cudagraph does not rely on torch.compile"), and `config/vllm.py` **auto-enables it for an architecture allow-list** (DeepseekV4, Inkling, KimiK3, KimiLinear, ...) unless the env is explicitly set. 2. With it enabled, compilation mode is forced to `NONE` while `cudagraph_mode` can remain piecewise-capable, and `BreakableCUDAGraphWrapper` captures the forward **without** torch.compile — its docstring says exactly that ("PW CUDA graph without torch.compile"). `set_splitting_ops_for_v1`'s early return then leaves `splitting_ops=[]` without the downgrade the guard would have applied. 3. Our deployment set the env to 1 for a model outside the allow-list (the Qwen3.8-27B model above); an allow-listed model with speculative decoding **and `cudagraph_mode` explicitly set to `PIECEWISE`** should reach the same state (the allow-listed defaults are FULL variants, which are keyed differently — see below); we have not tested one directly. Why FULL variants are safe (and a workaround): in `_init_candidates`, the separate-decode routine used by the FULL modes captures one graph **per decode query length** and puts it in the key: ```python if separate_decode_routine and decode_mode: for decode_query_len in decode_query_lens: desc = BatchExecutionDescriptor( cg_mode=decode_mode, num_reqs=rounded_num_reqs, uniform_token_count=decode_query_len, # <- query length in the key ) if mixed_mode: # for PIECEWISE graphs there is no limit on requests when replaying num_reqs = None # <- PIECEWISE: no query length ``` and `_is_compatible`'s first clause checks `uniform_token_count`. So under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` a verify batch and a plain decode batch cannot share a key, which matches what we measure: our DeepSeek-V4 production deployment (allow-listed, breakable auto-enabled, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, DSpark speculative decoding) has a healthy ~3.2 mean acceptance length. **Switching `cudagraph_mode` from `PIECEWISE` to any FULL variant therefore avoids the collision** — though for this drafter the FULL path has its own unresolved problem on our hardware (GPU memory faults, reported separately on the DFlash2 PR), so we run `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` instead. ## Suggested fixes (either would have caught this) * Move the `splitting_ops == [] and cudagraph_mode == PIECEWISE -> NONE` guard so the early return cannot skip it. * Or add the per-request query length to `BatchDescriptor` when speculative decoding is enabled, so verify batches cannot share a key with plain decode. The second is the more general fix: it removes the dependence on "attention is outside the graph" being maintained by every future code path.

signals.title: DFlash speculator `capture()` logs "Capturing model ..." even when nothing is captured — makes drafter-capture state unobservable
signals.text: `DFlashSpeculator.capture()` logs "Capturing model for ... speculator" before checking whether there is anything to capture, so the line appears even when the speculator's cudagraph mode is `NONE` and no graph is captured. `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash/speculator.py`: ```python def capture(self) -> None: logger.info("Capturing model for %s speculator...", self._speculator_name) self.sample_indices.zero_() ... self.query_cudagraph_manager.capture(...) ``` When `init_cudagraph_manager` resolves to `CUDAGraphMode.NONE` (draft attention does not support full cudagraphs, or the runner's decode mode is not FULL), `_init_candidates` returns early on `if not (self.cudagraph_mode and capture_sizes)`, `_capture_descs` stays empty, and the capture loop does nothing — but the log line has already been printed once per worker. The model runner's own path guards this (`gpu/model_runner.py`): ```python if not self.cudagraph_manager.needs_capture(): ``` `needs_capture()` is already defined on the manager, so the speculator can use the same check: ```python def capture(self) -> None: + assert self.query_cudagraph_manager is not None + if not self.query_cudagraph_manager.needs_capture(): + return logger.info("Capturing model for %s speculator...", self._speculator_name) ... ``` Minor, but it cost us real time: we used the presence of these lines as evidence that the drafter was being captured, concluded a configuration change had not taken effect, and drew the wrong conclusion from an otherwise clean experiment. The log is the only externally visible signal for whether the drafter is captured, so it being unconditional makes that state unobservable.
