signals.title: [Spec Decode] Honor positive dynamic K in autoregressive drafting
signals.text: # STACKED / DEPENDENT PR Depends on: - #49652 - fixed-query-length autoregressive draft CUDA graph capture - #51575 - runtime K propagation, K0 behavior, and active-width publication This branch currently contains those prerequisite commits solely so the positive-K follow-on can be built and validated before they merge. The unique contribution of this PR is commit `4d9b59acd5213a93c7389a9a1c7195c73f1f5a89`, and that commit changes only: - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py` - `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py` ## Problem For positive dynamic K below the configured maximum, MRV2 can receive the scheduler-selected K while `AutoRegressiveSpeculator` still physically executes the configured maximum amount of autoregressive draft work. ## Solution - Reuse #51575's runtime `num_speculative_tokens` value. - K1 stops after draft prefill. - Non-fused execution performs exactly K-1 post-prefill draft forwards. - Fused execution captures and selects a graph for each required positive depth. - The configured maximum remains the default/static graph. - Return exactly K draft tokens. This contains no policy, EMA, thresholds, optimistic-depth policy, or workload-specific tuning. ## Validation ### Unit and static - Focused positive-K tests: 13 passed. - Adjacent autoregressive speculator suite: 31 passed. - #51575 K0/lifetime regression: passed. - Ruff check and format: passed. - `git diff --check`: passed. ### Hardware Validated this exact candidate (`4d9b59acd5213a93c7389a9a1c7195c73f1f5a89`) with official Qwen3.8-27B FP8 weights on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell using BF16 KV, MRV2, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, the normal Qwen3.8 chat template/parser stack, and `/v1/chat/completions`: - At configured/default K4, the scheduler selected K4, the default K4 fused graph replayed, three post-prefill draft forwards executed (four total draft generations), and the published draft shape was `[1, 4]`. - At reduced positive K3, the scheduler selected K3, a physically distinct K3 fused graph replayed, two post-prefill draft forwards executed (three total draft generations), and the published draft shape was `[2, 3]`. - Published output storage did not alias proposer-owned storage. - Both normal chat-completions requests completed correctly. - CUDA graph capture and replay completed without CUDA, OOM, Xid, GSP, or NVRM faults. - The candidate worktree remained clean at the exact submitted HEAD. As secondary cross-architecture evidence, the same candidate was previously validated with MiMo 7B through the generic `AutoRegressiveSpeculator` path. External tracing exercised K3, K2, K1, and prerequisite K0 behavior, confirmed depth-specific physical work and publication widths, and completed a basic generation/lifecycle smoke without graph, lifecycle, or driver failure. The bug was discovered during local Qwen3.8 performance work; this PR is intentionally limited to generic positive-K execution semantics. After #49652 and #51575 merge, this branch will be rebased so the PR diff contains only the two-file positive-K follow-on. ## AI assistance disclosure OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, testing, and PR preparation. John reviewed the mechanism and validation and is responsible for the submission.

signals.title: [Spec Decode] Add graph-aware adaptive K for DFlash
signals.text: ## Purpose Addresses the throughput degradation reported in #49730 when a fixed DFlash draft length remains enabled after target verification becomes more expensive than ordinary decoding at larger batches. This change extends `enable_adaptive_verification` to DFlash and selects a batch-level K from graph-compatible candidates (`0, 1, 3, 7, 15` for K15). The policy combines startup-measured drafter/target costs, CUDA graph coverage, an EMA of accepted-prefix survival, and calibrated shared runtime overhead. K=0 skips the drafter and trims the current target verification batch to ordinary decode immediately. The current PR intentionally does not optimize sampling, the non-causal drafter, or fuse Qwen3.5 hybrid-GDN/FP8 target verification. H200 profiling showed target verification is the dominant cost; that kernel-fusion work is a separate follow-up. This is not a duplicate of #52522. That PR makes stochastic speculative decoding batch-invariant and recovers proposals after preemption; it does not choose K from runtime costs or disable speculation when it is predicted to be slower. Searches for `49730 in:body`, `DFlash adaptive K`, and `DFlash performance` found no open PR implementing this policy. AI assistance was used for implementation, review, testing, and documentation. The human submitter reviewed the changes and remains responsible for them. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --noconftest \ tests/test_config.py \ tests/test_sampling_params.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd_cug.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py \ -k 'adaptive or dflash or dspark' SKIP=shellcheck .venv/bin/pre-commit run ``` H200 serving A/B: - Target: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B`, FP8 target path - Drafter: `z-lab/Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash`, K15 - CUDA graph capture sizes: 1 through 512 - Dataset: GSM8K, 256 prompts, 32 warmups, temperature 0 - Concurrency: 1, 8, 32 - Arms: ordinary decode, fixed K15, automatic K - Gate: 256/256 complete and zero failures. Fixed K15 must exactly match ordinary decode; automatic K must retain at least 99% exact full-text matches under the FP8 target path, with the mismatch count reported. ## Test Result - Focused pytest: `37 passed` - Staged pre-commit: passed - H200 A/B (output tokens/s): | Concurrency | Ordinary | Fixed K15 | Automatic K | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 340.84 | 583.96 | 557.78 | | 8 | 2331.09 | 2387.12 | 2392.29 | | 32 | 6863.32 | 4505.21 | 4528.87 | - At concurrency 32 the policy moved from K15 to K7. Automatic K was 0.53% faster than fixed K15, instead of the previous false K0 fallback, while all 256 outputs exactly matched ordinary decoding. - All nine cells completed 256/256 requests with zero failures. Automatic K exact full-text match rate was 100% at concurrency 1, 8, and 32. - Ordinary decoding remains faster at concurrency 32. This isolates the next optimization to the hybrid-GDN/FP8 target verification path rather than sampling or the non-causal drafter. - Durable H200 result: `/threed-code/mokashliu/h200/vllm-dflash-adaptive-k/dflash-adaptive-k-h200-20260817-r30`

signals.title: [Model] Add Qwen3-Omni DSpark support
signals.text: ## Purpose Add framework support for using a dedicated `Qwen3OmniDSparkModel` draft with a Qwen3-Omni thinker target. This change: - registers a dedicated Qwen3-Omni DSpark architecture instead of silently treating it as generic Qwen3 DSpark; - exposes the target thinker's post-DeepStack auxiliary hidden states required by DSpark; - preserves the dedicated architecture and DSpark sampling fields when converting msModelSpec configuration; - validates the target/draft hidden size, attention geometry, target-layer selection, vocabulary contract, and DSpark algorithm settings at startup; - makes embedding/lm-head sharing and rejection-sampling buffers safe when the draft input/output vocabulary differs from the target vocabulary; - adds focused registry, configuration, model-contract, and configuration-bridge tests. A repository search for `Qwen3 Omni DSpark` and `Qwen3OmniDSpark` found no existing PR implementing this support, so this does not duplicate known work. This is a framework integration PR. Qwen3-Omni DSpark checkpoints are not yet available, so it does not claim model quality or acceptance-rate results. AI assistance disclosure: this draft was prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance. It should remain in draft until the submitter has reviewed every changed line and completed the required NPU/model evaluation. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/ruff check vllm/config/speculative.py \ vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py \ vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dspark.py \ vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_omni_dspark.py \ vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_omni_moe_thinker.py \ vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py \ vllm/transformers_utils/configs/speculators/algos.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/speculator.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/utils.py \ tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py \ tests/models/registry.py tests/test_config.py \ tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_dspark_config.py .venv/bin/ruff format --check <the same 13 files> .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_dspark_config.py \ tests/test_config.py \ -k 'qwen3_omni_dspark or dspark_updater' .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py \ -k 'dedicated_model_class or incomplete_vocab_weights or probabilistic_buffer' ``` Before marking ready: - run the Qwen3-Omni hidden-state module tests in an environment with `torchvision`; - load a compatible Qwen3-Omni DSpark checkpoint; - run NPU end-to-end eager and ACLGraph speculative-decoding tests in the dependent vLLM-Ascend PR; - report acceptance length, output correctness, memory, and throughput. ## Test Result - Ruff check: passed. - Ruff format check: passed; 13 files already formatted. - Configuration and msModelSpec bridge tests: 21 passed, 183 deselected. - Dedicated model/vocabulary/sampling-buffer tests: 5 passed, 3 deselected. - `git diff --check`: passed. - Qwen3-Omni hidden-state import tests were not runnable on the local macOS environment because `torchvision` is unavailable. - Model evaluation: not run because no Qwen3-Omni DSpark checkpoint is available.

signals.title: [Rust Frontend] Add MiniMax M2 append-think reasoning parser
signals.text: ## Summary - add the explicit `minimax_m2_append_think` Rust reasoning parser - prepend `<think>` once while preserving all generated output as visible content - preserve special tokens and keep automatic MiniMax model routing on the normal parser - cover parser lifecycle, empty deltas, factory registration, and parser-name diagnostics ## Duplicate-work check This does not duplicate an existing PR. Before implementation I checked: - roadmap issue #44280 and its comments - open PRs referencing `44280` - open PR searches for `minimax_m2_append_think` and MiniMax M2 append-think parser terms No overlapping Rust implementation or claim was found. The item was claimed in #44280 before implementation. ## Tests - `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-parser --lib` — 420 passed - `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-chat --lib` — 266 passed - `cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed - `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` — passed ## Full-model serving regression A CPU-only end-to-end serving regression was run with the locally built PR Rust binary and the full `allenai/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct` weights (13.59 GiB), using `--reasoning-parser minimax_m2_append_think`. A model-quality evaluation is not applicable because this change does not affect model execution, logits, or sampling; the full-model run validates parser integration and HTTP behavior. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to analyze the parser architecture, implement the change, and run validation. signals.title: [CPU] [1/n] Start migrating the CPU extension to the libtorch stable ABI
signals.text:
## Purpose This PR continues the libtorch stable ABI migration (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26946) for vLLM, and is the first PR dedicated completely to the stable CPU build. First CPU libtorch stable-ABI PR. Migrates `silu_and_mul`, `gelu_\*`, `rms_norm`, `fused_add_rms_norm`, and `rotary_embedding` into new corresponding `_C*_stable_libtorch` libraries. Leftover CPU kernels stay on `_C` / `_C_AVX*` until later PRs. cc @janeyx99, @Harry-Chen ### New file: `csrc/libtorch_stable/cpu/cpu_types_arm_vec.hpp` `cpu_types_arm.hpp` used to get its `Vectorized` primitives from `at::vec` (unstable ABI), so this header is a small header-only replacement using only `` and stable `torch/headeronly` types. It specializes `Vectorized` for `float/c10::Half/c10::BFloat16` and implements only the ops/conversions the migrated kernels actually call (no full `at::vec` API surface). `BF16` load/store/convert use hardware NEON instructions when `ARM_BF16_SUPPORT` is set, falling back to bit-manipulation on [uint16x8_t](url) otherwise (see truncation note below). **NOTE:** `csrc/libtorch_stable/cpu/cpu_types_arm_vec.hpp`'s `f32_to_bf16x4()` only uses the hardware `vcvt_bf16_f32` conversion when `ARM_BF16_SUPPORT` is defined (i.e. the build detected `FEAT_BF16`). On ARM hosts without that extension, it falls back to a plain bit-shift truncation. This is in contrast to ATen which does round-to-nearest-even with an explicit NaN check. Practical impact: at most a 1-ULP difference in bf16 outputs on non-FEAT_BF16 ARM hardware only. ## Test Plan - [x] CPU build produces leftover `_C` / `_C_AVX*` **and** the matching `*_stable_libtorch` modules. - [x] `torch-abi-audit` reports the three `*_stable_libtorch` libraries as **STABLE** (`unstable=0`) and leftover `_C` / `_C_AVX*` as **UNSTABLE**. **unit test** VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -x --disable-warnings tests/kernels/core/test_cpu_activation.py VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -x --disable-warnings tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -x --disable-warnings tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_fused_moe.py VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -x --disable-warnings tests/kernels/test_onednn.py Local testing was only done on the x86_64 architecture. The ARM CPU should be tested in the CI through `.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-cpu-test-arm.sh`. ## Test Results ---

signals.title: [XPU] AsyncTP support for W8A8-FP8 static GEMM collective fusion
signals.text: ## Purpose Add AsyncTP support for XPU FP8 static GEMM, extending the existing SP (sequence-parallel) pass. When a prefill batch clears the SP token threshold, GEMM ops and their surrounding all-reduce / reduce-scatter collectives are fused into a single kernel, hiding communication latency behind compute. This PR also documents a required correctness flag (`--linear-backend xpu`): without it, the AsyncTP pattern matcher replaces 0 ops on current vLLM and the arm silently degrades to SP-only. --- ## Test Setup **Model**: `RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8` **Hardware**: 4× Intel Arc Pro B60 Four arms are compared: | Arm | Server command suffix | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `eager` | `--enforce-eager` | no-compile baseline | | `compile_nosp` | `--compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":false}}'` | plain-compile baseline | | `asynctp_off` | `--compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":true},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}'` | SP only (AsyncTP off) | | `asynctp_on` | `--compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"fuse_gemm_comms":true},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}'` | SP + AsyncTP | --- ## Commands ### Server (replace `<COMPILATION_CONFIG>` with one of the four configs above) ```bash VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \ python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --dtype bfloat16 \ -tp 4 \ --gpu-memory-util 0.9 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --max-model-len 8192 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --linear-backend xpu \ <COMPILATION_CONFIG> ``` ### Benchmark ```bash python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench serve \ --model RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 4096 \ --random-output-len 1 \ --num-prompt 16 \ --request-rate inf \ --backend vllm \ --ignore-eos \ --trust-remote-code \ --temperature 0 ``` For the mixed prefill+decode shape, change `--random-input-len 256 --random-output-len 128 --num-prompt 16`. ### Accuracy (GSM8K) Accuracy is measured per arm. Start the server with the arm's compilation config, then run lm_eval while the server is running. Repeat for each arm. **Step 1 — start server** (shown for `asynctp_on`; substitute config for other arms): ```bash VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \ python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8 \ --trust-remote-code --dtype bfloat16 -tp 4 \ --gpu-memory-util 0.9 --max-model-len 8192 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching --linear-backend xpu \ --compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":true,"fuse_gemm_comms":true},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}' ``` | Arm | `--compilation-config` / flag | |---|---| | `asynctp_on` | `{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":true,"fuse_gemm_comms":true},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}` | | `asynctp_off` | `{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":true},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}` | | `compile_nosp` | `{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":false},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}` | | `eager` | `--enforce-eager` (no `--compilation-config`) | **Step 2 — evaluate** (same command for all arms): ```bash python3 -m lm_eval --model local-completions \ --model_args "model=RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8,base_url=http://localhost:8073/v1,tokenized_requests=False,num_concurrent=1" \ --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --limit 250 ``` --- ## Important: `--linear-backend xpu` is required --- ## Performance Results **AsyncTP pattern check**: range `(1, 4095)` → 0 patterns (decode range); range `(4096, 8192)` → **128 patterns** (prefill range). SP threshold for this model = `(8 MiB × TP=4) / (hidden=4096 × sizeof(fp8)=1)` = **4096 tokens**. ### Pure prefill — `output_len=1`, mean TTFT (ms), mean of 2 runs Gain = (compile_nosp − asynctp_on) / compile_nosp; positive = asynctp_on is faster. | Shape | asynctp_on | asynctp_off | compile_nosp | eager | **TTFT gain (on vs nosp)** | AsyncTP-only gain | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 16 prompts × 4096 in | 6935 | 7090 | 7602 | 7931 | **+8.8%** | +2.2% | | 16 prompts × 512 in | 1181 | 1218 | 1320 | 1401 | **+10.5%** | +3.1% | | 2 prompts × 4096 in | 1025 | 1013 | 1133 | 1179 | **+9.5%** | ~0% | SP contributes ~7–8 pp of the ~9–11% TTFT gain; AsyncTP adds ~2–3 pp on top. ### Mixed prefill + decode — mean of 2 runs | Shape | asynctp_on | asynctp_off | compile_nosp | eager | **Gain (on vs nosp)** | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | **Duration (s)** ↓ lower is better | | | | | | | 16 prompts × 256 in × 128 out | 3.5 | 3.4 | 4.2 | 4.8 | **+17.7%** | | **Output tok/s** ↑ higher is better | | | | | | | 16 prompts × 256 in × 128 out | 605 | 614 | 494 | 425 | **+22.5%** | | **TPOT (ms)** ↓ lower is better | | | | | | | 16 prompts × 256 in × 128 out | 21.2 | 20.4 | 27.8 | 31.7 | **+23.6%** | Mean TTFT appears higher for asynctp_on vs compile_nosp on this shape — this is a **queueing artifact**: higher throughput means requests queue behind faster-completing peers. Duration and throughput are the reliable metrics. --- ## Accuracy (GSM8K, 250 questions) | Arm | Accuracy | |---|---:| | asynctp_off (SP on, AsyncTP off) | 0.768 | | eager | 0.748 | | asynctp_on (SP + AsyncTP) | 0.736 | | compile_nosp | 0.736 | Standard error ≈ ±2.7 pp. `asynctp_on == compile_nosp` at 0.736. The 3.2 pp spread across all arms is within 1.2 σ — no statistically significant regression. ---

signals.title: [Bugfix] Support MistralCommonBackend tokenizers in the xgrammar structured-output backend
signals.text: ## Purpose Structured output (`response_format` / guided decoding) fails with **HTTP 500** for Mistral models when the tokenizer is loaded under the default `tokenizer_mode="auto"`. `transformers>=5.5` returns a `MistralCommonBackend` for Mistral repos. That class subclasses `PreTrainedTokenizerBase` (not `PreTrainedTokenizerFast`) and is not vLLM's `MistralTokenizer`, so: - `is_mistral_tokenizer()` returns `False` (it requires `IS_MISTRAL_TOKENIZER` + `isinstance(..., MistralTokenizer)`), so the working Mistral path in `XgrammarBackend.__post_init__` is skipped; - the `else` branch calls `xgr.TokenizerInfo.from_huggingface()`, whose dispatch matches only `PreTrainedTokenizerFast`, tiktoken-backed, or sentencepiece-backed tokenizers, and otherwise raises `ValueError: Unsupported tokenizer type: ...`. `XgrammarBackend` is constructed lazily on the **first structured-output request** (`vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py` → `grammar_init()`), inside engine-core, so the uncaught `ValueError` surfaces as an HTTP 500. Plain completions on the same server keep working, which makes this look like a model problem rather than a backend one. ## Reproduction No GPU, no HF token, public model: ```python from transformers.tokenization_mistral_common import MistralCommonBackend from vllm.config import StructuredOutputsConfig, VllmConfig from vllm.v1.structured_output.backend_types import StructuredOutputOptions from vllm.v1.structured_output.backend_xgrammar import XgrammarBackend tok = MistralCommonBackend.from_pretrained("mistralai/Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407") cfg = VllmConfig(structured_outputs_config=StructuredOutputsConfig(backend="xgrammar")) backend = XgrammarBackend(cfg, tokenizer=tok, vocab_size=tok.vocab_size) backend.compile_grammar(StructuredOutputOptions.JSON, '{"type":"object"}') ``` On `vllm==0.27.0` (stock, from PyPI): ``` ValueError: Unsupported tokenizer type: <class 'transformers.tokenization_mistral_common.MistralCommonBackend'> ``` With this change: ``` grammar compiled: XgrammarGrammar ``` Diagnostics for that tokenizer: ``` MRO : MistralCommonBackend -> PreTrainedTokenizerBase -> PushToHubMixin -> object IS_MISTRAL_TOKENIZER : <absent> # -> is_mistral_tokenizer() == False isinstance(PreTrainedTokenizerFast) : False # -> xgrammar's first branch misses ``` ## Fix `MistralCommonBackend` already carries everything the Mistral path needs — `tok.tokenizer` is a `mistral_common.MistralTokenizer`, reachable as `.instruct_tokenizer.tokenizer` → `Tekkenizer` — and vLLM already has both a helper to detect it (`mistral_common_tekkenizer()`) and a wrapper that consumes it (`MistralTokenizer.__init__(tokenizer: MistralCommonBackend)`). So rather than adding new vocabulary-construction logic, this change routes a tekken-backed `MistralCommonBackend` through the existing `MistralTokenizer`, which already builds a correct `xgr.TokenizerInfo` (byte-fallback handling, `is_tekken` → `VocabType.RAW`, eos as stop token). The Mistral branch body is unchanged apart from reading the local `tokenizer` variable. ## Test `tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_xgrammar_mistral_common.py` builds the backend from a `MistralCommonBackend` and compiles a JSON grammar. Verified both directions against stock `vllm==0.27.0`: - without the change: `1 failed` (`ValueError: Unsupported tokenizer type`) - with the change: `1 passed` ## Notes - The new branch is deliberately narrow: it triggers only when `mistral_common_tekkenizer()` returns a `Tekkenizer`, i.e. exactly the case reproduced above. Behaviour for every other tokenizer is unchanged, including the `backend="auto"` fallback path. - I did not extend this to sentencepiece-backed `MistralCommonBackend` instances because I have not reproduced a failure there. If maintainers know that path is also affected, widening the condition to any `MistralCommonBackend` would be a small follow-up — happy to do it in this PR if preferred.

signals.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Enable Qwen3.8-27B LM-only mode without vision tower
signals.text: ## Purpose This PR targets Qwen3.8-27B language-model-only deployments. Qwen3.8-27B is served through vLLM's Qwen3.5-compatible hybrid model path. When `--language-model-only` is enabled, all image and video limits are zero, so the vision tower cannot execute. Before this change, the shared model path could still construct and load the vision tower, and the runtime could still prepare encoder CUDA graphs even though no configured modality could use them. That unnecessary work is particularly costly for a 27B deployment: it consumes GPU memory that should be available to the language model and KV cache, and it can add avoidable initialization and CUDA-graph setup to a text-only serving path. This change: - Uses a metadata-only vision-tower placeholder in the Qwen3.5-compatible path used by Qwen3.8-27B when image and video limits are both zero. - Preserves the tower metadata needed by the language-model code path without allocating vision parameters or buffers. - Adds an explicit multimodal-encoder capability check and skips encoder CUDA graph setup when no configured modality can execute the encoder. - Covers both dense and MoE variants of the shared Qwen3.5-compatible path with regression tests. This is not a new model implementation. It makes the existing hybrid execution path honor text-only mode for Qwen3.8-27B and avoids allocating components that cannot execute in that deployment. ## Test Plan Unit tests: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_5_language_model_only.py \ tests/multimodal/test_registry.py::test_supports_multimodal_encoder \ tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py::test_embedding_only_mode_skips_encoder_cudagraph_manager \ -q ``` Regression vehicle and runtime smoke test on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090: - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, the smallest available checkpoint exercising the same Qwen3.5-compatible hybrid implementation path. - Run once with `language_model_only=True` and once without the flag. - Generate a short text response from each configuration. The Qwen3.5-0.8B test is a minimal regression vehicle for the Qwen3.8-27B execution path. It is not intended to represent a Qwen3.8-27B memory measurement. ## Test Result Unit tests: ```text 11 passed, 14 warnings in 49.20s ``` Both runtime configurations loaded the real `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` checkpoint and returned text. The LM-only run logged: ```text All limits of multimodal modalities supported by the model are set to 0, running in text-only mode. ``` Example generated response from the LM-only run: ```text The sky appears blue because the atmosphere scatters shorter wavelengths of light (blue) more effectively than ... ``` Memory comparison (same model and prompt; values are rounded from vLLM logs): | Configuration | Model loading | KV cache | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Default multimodal | 1.72 GiB | 34.70 GiB | | `language_model_only=True` | 1.53 GiB | 36.17 GiB | | Difference | **0.19 GiB less** | **1.47 GiB more available** | This measurement is from the 0.8B regression vehicle and is not presented as a 27B projection. It demonstrates the allocation that the LM-only path removes; for Qwen3.8-27B, the value is avoiding that unnecessary vision allocation and encoder setup within a much tighter model-serving memory budget. No model-accuracy evaluation was added because this change only controls multimodal module construction and encoder CUDA-graph setup; the language-model weights and text generation path are unchanged. A real-weight generation smoke test was run for both configurations. ## Duplicate-work Check No issue was assigned to this PR. Searches of open vLLM pull requests and issues for Qwen3.8-27B, Qwen3.5, `language_model_only`, vision tower, and multimodal encoder found no existing PR covering this fix. Related Qwen3.8-27B reports, including [#52654](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52654) and [#52682](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52682), address multimodal encoder TP behavior and CUDA-graph startup hangs rather than unnecessary vision-tower construction in LM-only mode. ## Documentation No documentation update is required; the existing supported-models documentation already describes text-only mode via `--language-model-only`. ## AI Assistance AI assistance was used to inspect the branch, draft this description, run the unit tests, run real-weight Qwen3.5 generation, and measure the memory difference. The human submitter must review every changed line and verify the reported test and runtime results before submitting the PR.

signals.title: [ROCm][Perf] Fuse DeepSeek-V4 mHC post/pre and RMSNorm with AITER
signals.text:
## Purpose This PR improves the ROCm DeepSeek-V4 mHC path by wiring the existing AITER fused mHC operators into vLLM. The ROCm path can now replace the previous sequence of separate mHC/RMSNorm kernels with the fused AITER flow: - `mhc_post` + `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` -> `mhc_fused_post_pre_gemm_sqrsum` - `mhc_pre_big_fuse` + `add_rmsnorm_quant` -> `mhc_pre_big_fuse_rmsnorm` For unsupported fused-RMSNorm hidden sizes, the path still uses fused post+pre where available, while preserving the standalone RMSNorm fallback. > [!NOTE] > The change is scoped to the ROCm/AITER path and does not change the CUDA or XPU implementations. --- Before fuse: After fuse (**38.35%** faster): ## Test Plan Benchmark with SA InferenceX `8k1k` workload. ```bash # Launch the server vllm serve /shared/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --port 8333 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --async-scheduling \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --distributed-executor-backend mp \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --moe-backend aiter \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \ --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' # Bench client CONCS=${CONCS:-"1 4 16 64"} for CONC in ${CONCS}; do NUM_PROMPTS=$((CONC * 10)) NUM_WARMUPS=$((CONC * 2)) python InferenceX/utils/bench_serving/benchmark_serving.py \ --model /shared/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --backend vllm \ --base-url "http://0.0.0.0:8333" \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 8192 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 0.8 \ --num-prompts "${NUM_PROMPTS}" \ --max-concurrency "${CONC}" \ --num-warmups "${NUM_WARMUPS}" \ --request-rate inf \ --ignore-eos \ --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \ --trust-remote-code \ --use-chat-template --dsv4 done ``` Accuracy test with `gsm8k` dataset. ```bash CONC=${CONC:-256} NUM_FEWSHOT=${NUM_FEWSHOT:-30} ... python -m lm_eval ... ``` ## Test Result > [!NOTE] > The tests below are executed on AMD MI350X GPU, so the performance could be slightly lower than the MI355X baseline, so I verified this PR with an A/B test compared with vLLM `main` on the same machine. ### Benchmark Concurrency | Version | Output token throughput (tok/s) | Change | Mean TTFT (ms) | Change | Mean TPOT (ms) | Change -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 1 | Main | 54.91 | — | 425.04 | — | 17.77 | — 1 | This PR | 55.74 | 1.51% ↑ | 466.94 | 9.86% ↑ | 17.46 | 1.74% ↓ 4 | Main | 176.57 | — | 527.68 | — | 21.55 | — 4 | This PR | 179.77 | 1.81% ↑ | 524.51 | 0.60% ↓ | 21.16 | 1.81% ↓ 16 | Main | 517.54 | — | 822.58 | — | 29.02 | — 16 | This PR | 526.55 | 1.74% ↑ | 813.08 | 1.15% ↓ | 28.52 | 1.72% ↓ 64 | Main | 1,032.93 | — | 1,824.43 | — | 58.89 | — 64 | This PR | 1,039.79 | 0.66% ↑ | 1,857.28 | 1.80% ↑ | 58.46 | 0.73% ↓ 256 | Main | 1,554.35 | — | 6,092.57 | — | 156.20 | — 256 | This PR | 1,580.19 | 1.66% ↑ | 5,812.90 | 4.59% ↓ | 153.83 | 1.52% ↓ The results show that **This PR improves Output Token Throughput across all concurrency levels, with gains ranging from +0.66% to +1.81%**. **Mean TPOT also improves consistently, decreasing by 0.73% to 1.81% across all concurrency levels**. For **Mean TTFT**, the results are mixed: it **increases slightly at conc=1 (+9.86%) and conc=64 (+1.80%)**, while it **decreases at conc=4 (-0.60%), conc=16 (-1.15%), and conc=256 (-4.59%)**. signals.title: [Perf] Backfill divergent local hybrid hits from the offloading connector
signals.text: ## Purpose Addresses #52773. With hybrid models (Mamba + full attention), per-group local prefix hits diverge under block pressure: the full-attention prefix survives deeper in HBM than the recurrent state, which can only resume at a boundary with a state snapshot. Today the offloading connector never sees the divergent hit (`supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits` is `False`, #50344), so the resident full-attention KV above the common boundary is given up and re-fetched from the store; capable connectors reconcile to the common boundary whenever no external tokens lie beyond the deep hit (#48425), without asking whether the store can back an intermediate boundary. In the common write-through setup the store holds full per-group chunk sets — exactly the missing piece — but no path asks for it (measured ~80× cost per event on a revisit/fork workload, see the linked issue). This PR adds a backfill path: - **`KVConnectorBase_V1.get_hybrid_backfill_tokens(request, num_computed_tokens) -> (num_local, num_external)`** (optional, default `(0, 0)`): consulted only for connectors with `supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits`, when the local hits diverged and `get_num_new_matched_tokens()` reported no external tokens beyond the divergent hit. - **Scheduler** (`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`): in the `hit_diverged and ext == 0` branch, if the connector reports a backed boundary, keep the local prefix below it (`truncate_computed_blocks`, whose Mamba-aware slicing already models the ragged groups) and async-load just the boundary chunk; otherwise reconcile exactly as before. - **`OffloadingConnector`**: implements the hook with a boundary-walk probe over the per-group offload keys (deepest boundary whose chunk is `HIT` in every group; boundaries being loaded are skipped), and now opts into `supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits` when every group resumes from a single chunk: uniform `tokens_per_chunk`, every sliding window ≤ 1 chunk (recurrent groups are modeled as one-chunk windows), no eagle groups. Configs outside that (wider SWA windows, eagle) keep today's behavior — the capability stays `False`. - **`MultiConnector`**: forwards the probe; the first child reporting a backed boundary is assigned the request (the hook is only consulted when no child had matched tokens, so no child has been assigned yet). The load itself reuses the existing external-load path unchanged (`update_state_after_alloc` computes the chunk set from the probe-adjusted bookkeeping); `get_hybrid_backfill_tokens` must be called after `get_num_new_matched_tokens()`, which is the order the scheduler uses. Known minor: `update_num_hit_chunks` is recorded at the pre-backfill query, so per-group hit metrics do not count the backfilled boundary chunk. ## Test Plan ```bash VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k "hybrid" -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -k "backfill or partial_lookup" -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py -v pre-commit run --files <changed files> ``` New tests: - `test_hybrid_fa_deeper_hit_backfilled_by_connector` (core scheduler, both backfill-hit and backfill-miss parametrizations, including the async-load resume flow); - `test_hybrid_backfill_returns_deepest_fully_backed_boundary`, `test_hybrid_backfill_misses_when_no_boundary_is_fully_backed`, `test_hybrid_backfill_skips_boundaries_being_loaded` (offloading probe). ## Test Result - `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k "hybrid"`: **7 passed** (5 pre-existing divergence cases unchanged + 2 new). - `offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -k "backfill or partial_lookup"`: **5 passed**. - `test_multi_connector.py`: **21 passed, 2 failed** — the same 2 failures (`test_multi_example_connector_consistency`, `test_multi_connector_mixed_hma_disables_hybrid_kv_cache`) reproduce identically on pristine `main` in this environment and are unrelated; the override-completeness guard `test_multi_connector_overrides_all_base_methods` passes with the new base method delegated. - `pre-commit` hooks pass on all changed files. Marked as **draft**: I plan to attach paired end-to-end numbers (hybrid revisit/fork workload, offloading on, backfill on/off) from our test rig, and I'm happy to split the base-API change from the offloading implementation if preferred. --- *Disclosure per `AGENTS.md`: this PR was AI-assisted (Claude Code). I have reviewed every changed line and run the tests above. Duplicate-work check (2026-08-18): searched issues/PRs for `hit_diverged`, `get_computed_blocks_for_connector`, `supports_divergent_local_hybrid_hits`, "divergent hybrid mamba", "mamba offloading", "backfill mamba" — the correctness lineage (#48425, #50344, and open #46455 / #48195) reconciles or scopes divergent hits; no existing issue or PR consults the offload store below a divergent hit. This change affects scheduling only when the new probe reports a backed boundary; output correctness is covered by the resume-boundary invariant the existing divergence tests assert.*

signals.title: [Kernel][MoE] DeepEP v2: async finalize to overlap shared experts with combine (env-gated)
signals.text: FIX #52744 ### What `prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py` issues the ElasticBuffer combine synchronously at both call sites, so the modular-kernel shared-expert overlap window (`finalize_async` -> shared experts on the compute stream -> receiver join, `MK_INTERNAL_OVERLAPPED`) is never used: for MoE models with a shared expert (DeepSeek-R1/V3) the shared-expert FFN serializes behind the cross-node all-to-all on every MoE layer during decode. This PR makes `finalize_async` issue the combine with `async_with_compute_stream=True` (+ `allocate_on_comm_stream`) and return a receiver closure that joins via a device-side `event.current_stream_wait()` — graph-replay safe (the closure keeps `combined_x` and the event alive; no host synchronization inside the captured region). ### Safety - **Env-gated, default off**: `VLLM_DEEPEP_V2_COMBINE_OVERLAP=1`. The flag is read once in `__init__` (never touches `os.environ` inside the captured region). Default path is byte-identical to the current synchronous combine. - **DBO**: overlap is disabled under DBO (`dbo_enabled()`), synchronous fallback, log-once. - **No-event capability gate**: if a DeepEP build returns no combine event, the overlap self-disables permanently (warn-once + a single eager full-sync join) — a pre-capture decision, since warmup always precedes capture; if it is ever hit during capture anyway, a hard `RuntimeError` is raised instead of hiding a sync inside the graph. ### Tests - `tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_overlap_gate.py` (new, hermetic, no GPU collectives): contract tests for the gate — eager no-event self-disable / capture no-event raise / event-path deferred device-side join. (Ported from a validated harness; the same three contracts pass against this module logic.) - `tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_moe.py`: `test_deep_ep_v2_moe_cudagraph` parametrized over the flag, so the existing torch-reference comparison doubles as the correctness oracle with overlap ON inside captured graphs. ### Performance (deployment observation) DeepSeek-R1-671B FP8, EP8 (2 nodes x TP4xDP2, GB300 / multi-node NVLink), full cudagraphs, `--all2all-backend deepep_v2`; pre-registered A/B, 4 independent server starts (ABBA), greedy, forced 128 output tokens, steady-state: | metric | OFF | ON | delta | |---|---|---|---| | C=1 decode ITL p50 | 15.71 ms | 14.32 ms | **-8.8%** | | C=24 decode ITL p50 | 22.05 ms | 20.89 ms | **-5.3%** | | C=1 TTFT p50 (negative control) | 236.9 ms | 236.8 ms | -0.1 ms | Greedy outputs bit-identical across all four arms. Serving traces: each combine kernel overlapped by shared-expert GEMMs ~9.7 us on average with the flag ON vs exactly 0 OFF. An ablation with the event-wait placed *before* the shared-expert GEMMs (offload without overlap) shows ~0 gain — the benefit is true overlap. Full evidence in #52744. ### Validation scope GPU validation was performed on a v0.26.0-era tree; the finalize/combine region is unchanged between v0.26.0 and current main (the dispatch-side drift is unrelated), so the port is mechanical. The contract tests pass against this module logic; the parametrized cudagraph test covers the captured path wherever DeepEP v2 CI runners exist. Happy to adjust the shape (config-gated instead of env, or default-on) per maintainer preference.

signals.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Drop the redundant eagle trailing-chunk pop on load
signals.text: ## Summary `_lookup()` decrements every eagle group's backend result by one chunk: ```python if is_eagle_unverified: num_hit_chunks -= 1 ``` but `storable_chunks()` **already** excludes the volatile trailing chunk on the **store** side while decoding, and its docstring records why the other case is safe: > For eagle/MTP groups the volatile trailing chunk of the offloadable range is excluded while decoding … During prefill the trailing chunk is stable (the draft input for a chunk's last position is the next prompt token), so it is stored immediately. If nothing volatile is ever offloaded, the load-side pop is a **second, redundant exclusion** that discards a chunk which is safe by construction. ## Measured impact Instrumented build on a hybrid GDN+GQA MoE with `method='mtp'`, `tokens_per_chunk` 2128, DP=4 × TP=4, 8 workers, ~3 % mirrored production traffic: | observation | count | |---|---| | `RAW_HIT 1` → popped to `0` | **1064 / 1064** | | backend-answered lookups discarded | **1064 / 1169 (91 %)** | | survivors, all with `RAW_HIT ≥ 2` | 105 | The symptom at the metric level is `kv_offload_total_bytes_total{transfer_type="GPU_to_CPU"}` climbing while `CPU_to_GPU` stays near zero — the host tier writes and almost never reads back. ## Why `RAW_HIT == 1` is the common case, not an edge case The `num_hit_chunks == 0` guard sits **before** the pop, so a raw hit of exactly 1 clears the guard and is then decremented to zero, ending at `new_num_hit_tokens < tokens_per_chunk → return 0`. And once the GPU tier already covers most of the prefix, the lookup queries a single key. A real trace: ``` ENTER req_tokens 113826 ncomp 110656 maxhit_after_align 112784 mamba_align 2128 lookup_groups 4 grp 3 eagle 1 swa None align None start 52 nchunks 53 keys 1 tpc 2128 RAW_HIT 1 grp 3 POST hit_chunks 0 maxhit 110656 new_hit_tok 0 RET0-rounding grp 3 new_hit_tok 0 tpc 2128 ``` `start_chunk_idx = 110656/2128 = 52`, `len(offload_keys) ≈ 53`, so exactly one key is queried and `RAW_HIT` is bounded at 1 by construction. The backend **has** the chunk; the pop throws it away and the request re-prefills. ## The widening is removed with it ```python # For eagle groups, query one extra chunk that will be popped. # We only need to increase the query size for sliding window groups. if is_eagle_unverified and sliding_window_size_in_chunks is not None: query_max = min(max_hit_size_tokens + tokens_per_chunk, len(offload_keys) * tokens_per_chunk) ``` It existed solely to feed the pop. I previously tried making it unconditional (#52674, now closed) and it changed nothing, which the arithmetic explains: it is clamped by `len(offload_keys) * tokens_per_chunk`, which already equals `max_hit_size_tokens` whenever the tail of the request is what is being looked up. On the trace above, widened and unwidened both yield `keys = 1`. ## Scope / caveats - All four KV groups are flagged eagle here via the `use_eagle and not eagle_groups` fallback, so the pop applies universally rather than to a draft-specific group. Narrowing that fallback may be worth doing separately, but it is not what produces this loss. - I have **not** re-run the instrumented capture with this patch applied — filing as draft for that reason and for maintainer review of the safety argument. The claim rests on `storable_chunks()` being the sole gate on what reaches the backend; if there is a path that offloads a volatile trailing chunk without going through it, the pop is load-bearing and this is wrong. - A single-KV-group model does not reproduce the loss (verified: dense model with a real eagle3 head, 75 % acceptance, reads back normally), because `keys == 1` with a large `tokens_per_chunk` is what makes the pop fatal.

signals.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Scope DSpark backend inheritance to DeepSeek V4
signals.text: ## Purpose #52288 made an unspecified DSpark draft backend inherit the target's backend. That fallback is required for DeepSeek V4 because its target and draft layers share a KV-cache layout, but it is not valid for every DSpark architecture. For example, a Kimi MLA target can use a Qwen3/SWA DSpark draft. Inheriting `FLASHINFER_MLA` makes draft initialization fail because that backend does not support sliding-window attention. Keep the explicit draft override behavior, but inherit the target backend only when the normalized DSpark draft has `model_type == "deepseek_v4"`. Other DSpark drafts leave the backend unset so their own attention kind participates in normal backend auto-selection. ## Why this is not a duplicate This is a narrowly scoped follow-up to the regression introduced by #52288. No open PR matched the backend-inheritance regression. Nearby #48381 addresses the draft KV-cache dtype and #51042 addresses DSV4 SWA index width; neither changes draft backend selection. ## Tests ```text HF_HOME=/data/mgoin PYTHONPATH=/home/mgoin/code/vllm-dspark-backend-scope \ /home/mgoin/code/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_utils.py -v # 3 passed /home/mgoin/code/vllm/.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/utils.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_utils.py # passed /home/mgoin/code/vllm/.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual \ --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/utils.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_utils.py # passed ``` The regression test covers DSV4 inheritance, non-DSV4 auto-selection, and an explicit draft override. ## Model validation On 4x B300, main reproduced the non-DSV4 failure with a Kimi-K3 MLA target and the Qwen3/SWA `RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-speculator.dspark`: the inherited `FLASHINFER_MLA` backend was rejected because sliding-window attention is not supported. With the independent-selection behavior restored, the target chose `FLASHINFER_MLA`, the draft chose `FLASHINFER`, the engine initialized, and a 32-token chat request completed. No output-accuracy evaluation was run because this changes startup-time backend routing only. The DSV4 path retains the behavior validated in #52288. ## AI assistance This PR was produced with AI assistance. It is intentionally a draft; the human submitter must review every changed line before marking it ready.

signals.title: [Spec Decode] DFlash2: local convolution + candidate selector
signals.text: Two additions to the DFlash drafter, carried by a separate architecture: a checkpoint declaring `DFlash2DraftModel` gets them, and every existing `DFlashDraftModel` checkpoint resolves to the class it resolves to today, untouched by this PR. **Grouped dynamic depthwise convolution** inside each block, so a proposal position can see the ones before it without another backbone pass. `out[i,c] = Σ_t (base[t,c] + δ[i,t,g(c)]) · x[i−t,c]`, taps zero across the block boundary. Wraps each sublayer in and out from one projection of its input. Sized by `conv_kernel_size` and `conv_group_size` in the draft config. **Candidate selector.** Instead of an independent argmax per slot, keep the target head's top-K per slot, score adjacent transitions `edge(p→c) = ⟨A[p] ⊙ project(h), B[c]⟩ + unary[c]`, and walk the best path from the verified anchor. At T>0 it walks by inverse CDF and returns q over the K candidates for the lossless verify. Sized by `selector_rank` and `selector_top_k` in the draft config. ``` model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash2.py the convolution and the selector v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash2/speculator.py the walk kernel and the proposal model_executor/models/registry.py DFlash2DraftModel v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/__init__.py speculator selection ``` The selector runs after the draft model's forward and carries its own `@support_torch_compile`. The path walk is one Triton program per request: a slot's K scores stay in registers, and the slot-to-slot dependency is a loop inside the program rather than a kernel per slot. The vocabulary top-k, the selector's largest single cost, uses FlashInfer's radix kernel where FlashInfer is available and `torch.topk` otherwise. DFlash2 runs on the V2 model runner, which is where its speculator lives. `use_v2_model_runner` selects V2 for a DFlash2 draft, as it already does for DSpark: the V1 `DFlashProposer` has no candidate selector, so a DFlash2 checkpoint reaching it would draft as DFlash1 without raising. ## Results `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` on one H200, against [`RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark`](https://huggingface.co/RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark) and autoregressive decoding. Seven draft tokens per verification step for both drafters. Qwen3.8's recommended sampling — temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20 — with `xhigh` reasoning effort and 4096 max new tokens; prompt formatting from [`z-lab/dflash`](https://github.com/z-lab/dflash). ### Acceptance length, GSM8K Mean over per-request acceptance, the statistic the model cards report. vLLM's counters give a pooled ratio — total accepted tokens over total drafts — so the per-request values are recovered at concurrency 1, where a counter delta around a single request belongs to that request alone. | | DSpark | DFlash 2 | | |---|-------:|---------:|---| | per-request mean | 4.27 | **5.34** | +25.2% | | pooled ratio | 3.64 | **4.65** | +27.8% | Acceptance does not move with concurrency: DFlash 2's pooled ratio reads 4.65, 4.82 and 4.74 at concurrency 1, 8 and 32. ### Throughput, GSM8K Output tokens over end-to-end wall time. Each point is 128 × concurrency requests split over four shards, each shard one H200 serving at the stated concurrency; the four shard rates are averaged, not summed, so a cell is a single-GPU number measured four times. A warmup of `concurrency` requests runs before the clock starts and is dropped, as in `z-lab/dflash`. | conc | requests | autoregressive | DSpark | DFlash 2 | |------|---------:|---------------:|-------:|---------:| | 1 | 124 | 64.1 | 178.5 (2.79×) | **224.6 (3.51×)** | | 8 | 992 | 416.4 | 966.2 (2.32×) | **1,211.7 (2.91×)** | | 32 | 3,968 | 1,256.9 | 2,220.9 (1.77×) | **2,759.4 (2.20×)** | All three methods are served one after another inside the same container, so a difference between them is never a difference between GPUs. Spread across the four shards is 2.1–2.5% for autoregressive and 2.6–15.2% for the drafters, which is the shape to expect: a drafter's rate depends on which prompts it drew and autoregressive decoding has no such freedom. ### What the conv and the selector cost Each component timed alone in its own CUDA graph at the shapes the draft runs (5 layers, hidden 5120, vocab 248320, block 8, K=16), against the measured serving step — draft proposal plus target verification — taken from the run above as `pooled acceptance × concurrency / tok s`. | batch | conv | top-k | lattice | walk | selector | conv+selector | step | share | |-------|-----:|------:|--------:|-----:|---------:|--------------:|-----:|------:| | 1 | 0.113 | 0.041 | 0.014 | 0.006 | 0.061 | **0.174 ms** | 20.70 ms | **0.84%** | | 8 | 0.121 | 0.084 | 0.016 | 0.006 | 0.106 | **0.227 ms** | 31.80 ms | **0.71%** | | 32 | 0.173 | 0.173 | 0.018 | 0.006 | 0.197 | **0.370 ms** | 54.93 ms | **0.67%** | The selector's own math — the lattice and the walk — is 0.020 ms and flat in batch; the rest of that column is the vocabulary top-k, where FlashInfer's radix kernel is 1.9× `torch.topk` at batch 1 and 4.5× at batch 32. The convolution is 20 small calls over `[8, 5120]` tensors, so it is launch-bound rather than FLOP-bound: 0.477 ms as eager modules, 0.0096 ms compiled as a single graph across all 20 calls, and 0.113 ms — the figure above — with each call compiled on its own, which is what the model's compiled region gives it, since attention and the MLP run between `prepare` and `finish`. A hand-fused kernel would collect most of the remaining 12×. ## Test Result ``` pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py 4 passed pytest tests/test_config.py::test_dflash2_draft_forces_v2... 1 passed pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_lookahead.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py 19 passed ``` The three DFlash v1 files pass unchanged. `test_dflash_causality.py` is edited here, in the same change that touches `_dflash_layer_causal`, so its updated tests do not by themselves speak to v1 compatibility; the versions of those tests as they stood before this change also pass against this tree. Serving results are the tables above: GSM8K at three concurrencies on `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`, run through vLLM's OpenAI server, 128 × concurrency requests per point. ## Not a duplicate `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "DFlash in:title"` returns work on the existing DFlash v1 path — adaptive K (#52559), SWA (#47511), fused cache insert (#46911), profiling annotations (#52782) — and `--search "dflash2"` returns nothing. This adds the DFlash2 drafter, which none of those touch. AI assistance was used for this change.

signals.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Reject n > 1 in the Rust /inference/v1/generate route
signals.text: ## Purpose Closes #52843 With `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, `/inference/v1/generate` silently ignores `n > 1`: `vllm_text::SamplingParams` has no `n` field, so the key is dropped at deserialization and a single choice is returned. The Rust OpenAI routes already reject `n > 1` explicitly; this makes the raw generate route do the same. Route-local change only (a wrapper capturing `n` + validation mirroring the completions validator); the shared `vllm_text` crate is untouched. Rust-frontend counterpart of #52399, which fixed the same silent drop in the Python frontend and skips its regression test under the Rust frontend. ## Demo ```bash curl -s localhost:8000/inference/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"token_ids": [1, 2, 3], "sampling_params": {"max_tokens": 5, "n": 4}, "stream": false}' ``` Before — HTTP 200, three completions silently missing: ```json {"request_id":"42a4300a","choices":[{"index":0,"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"length","token_ids":[1805,3263,1085,138472,55057]}], ...} ``` After — HTTP 400: ```json {"error":{"message":"Only n=1 is supported.","type":"invalid_request_error","param":"n","code":"invalid_request_error"}} ``` ## Test Plan / Result New tests: validator (`rejects_parallel_sampling`, `accepts_explicit_n_one`) and HTTP route level (`raw_generate_rejects_parallel_sampling`). `cargo test -p vllm-server --lib`, fmt and clippy: all pass.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Pad the MiniMax-M3 decode index tile to a power of two
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #49157. `_decode_index_score_kernel` derives its lane tile directly from the head count: ```python BLOCK_SIZE_HQ: tl.constexpr = num_idx_heads * BLOCK_SIZE_Q hq_offsets = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE_HQ) ``` `tl.arange` requires a power-of-two extent, so decode fails to compile whenever `num_idx_heads * BLOCK_SIZE_Q` is not one: ``` ValueError: arange's range must be a power of 2 ``` `num_idx_heads == num_kv_heads`, which is not a power of two for every TP split — e.g. 96 query heads over 6 KV heads. The prefill kernel is unaffected because it puts the head dimension in the program grid, so the head count never becomes a `tl.arange` extent there. This rounds the tile up to the next power of two and bounds the head dimension in the existing `q_mask`, which already guards every load, score and store indexed by `hq_offsets`. The trailing lanes are masked out, so results for the real heads are unchanged. ## Test Plan `test_decode_index_topk_correctness` hardcoded `num_idx_heads = 2`, which is a power of two, so it could never reach this path. It is now parametrized over `[2, 3, 6]` and checks the kernel against the reference implementation already in that file. ```bash pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py::test_decode_index_topk_correctness -v ``` ## Test Result | | failed | passed | |---|---|---| | before | 12 | 6 | | after | **0** | **18** | The 12 failures are exactly the `num_idx_heads` 3 and 6 cases; the `2` cases pass either way. Full-file run, comparing the same commit with and without the kernel change: ``` fixed by this patch (12): test_decode_index_topk_correctness[3-0-1-1] … [3-2-4-4] test_decode_index_topk_correctness[6-0-1-1] … [6-2-4-4] broken by this patch: (none) ``` I also checked that the padded lanes do not perturb results: for `num_idx_heads` in {3, 5, 6, 12}, decode scores are bit-identical to an unpadded run over the same inputs (max abs diff exactly 0), and `decode_query_len > 1` (spec decode, where `BLOCK_SIZE_Q > 1` widens the product) compiles and runs for the same head counts. Tested on sm120. The remaining failures in that file are pre-existing and unrelated — they come from `tl.make_block_ptr` having been removed in newer Triton (`NotImplementedError: Block pointers have been removed in favor of the tensor descriptor API`), and the failure set is identical with and without this change.

signals.title: [ROCm][PERF] Enable AITER PA gluon decode for MiniMax-M3 MTP and dense layers
signals.text: ## Purpose The gluon paged-attention decode kernel handles multi-token query lengths, so EAGLE3 speculative decoding no longer has to fall back to native vllm unified_attention. ## Test Plan Server cmd to run EAGLE3 speculative decoding ``` export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1800 export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_CAST_BF16_TO_FP16=0 export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION_MIN_SIZE_KB=256 export VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1 export VLLM_CUSTOM_SCOPES_FOR_PROFILING=1 vllm serve amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 \ --served-model-name MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \ --port 8888 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --trust-remote-code \ --block-size 128 \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --enable-chunked-prefill \ --language-model-only \ --max-num-batched-tokens 65536 \ --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"thinking_mode":"enabled"}' \ --max-num-seqs 128 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \ --moe-backend aiter \ --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \ --speculative-config '{"method": "eagle3", "model": "Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "attention_backend": "ROCM_AITER_FA"}' ``` ## Test Result MiniMax-M3 with EAGLE3 3-token speculative decoding sees a significant uplift at long context: the AITER gluon paged-attention kernel replaces the unified_attention fallback and is substantially faster for longer contexts. Accuracy score: |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9689|± |0.0048| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9689|± |0.0048|
signals.author: ukannika

signals.title: [XPU] Add block FP8 AsyncTP all-gather collective fusion
signals.text: ## Purpose This PR extends AsyncTP (asynchronous tensor-parallel collective fusion, added for per-channel static-scale FP8 in #52683) on XPU to **block-quantized** W8A8 FP8 GEMM — i.e. models with a 2D `weight_scale_inv` tensor (`block_structure=[128,128]`, e.g. DeepSeek-style block-FP8 checkpoints), building on top of the existing block-FP8 SP support (#49009). The pattern matcher and replacement in `collective_fusion.py` now recognize block-FP8's 2D per-block scale GEMM alongside the existing per-channel static-scale GEMM, fusing GEMM + its surrounding reduce-scatter/all-gather collectives into a single kernel once a prefill batch clears the SP token threshold. Validation uses `RedHatAI/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-block`, the same Llama-3.1-8B architecture and SP threshold as the static-FP8 8B case (`../w8a8-fp8-static-8b/pr.md`), to confirm block-FP8's 2D weight-scale tensor works correctly with AsyncTP and quantify any difference in gains versus the per-channel static-scale variant. This is a re-run with the previously-missing `asynctp_off` (SP-only) arm and GSM8K accuracy added for all four arms, to isolate whether the mixed prefill+decode regression seen in the first pass comes from SP or from the GEMM-comm fusion (AsyncTP) on top of it. --- ## Test Setup **Model**: `RedHatAI/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-block` **Hardware**: 4× Intel Arc Pro B60 (TP=4) **SP threshold**: `(8 MiB × TP=4) / (hidden=4096 × 2 bytes)` = **4096 tokens** (identical to the static-FP8 8B case, since architecture/hidden_size match). Four arms are compared: | Arm | Server command suffix | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `eager` | `--enforce-eager` | no-compile baseline | | `compile_nosp` | `--compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":false},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}'` | plain-compile baseline | | `asynctp_off` | `--compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":true},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}'` | SP only (AsyncTP off) | | `asynctp_on` | `--compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":true,"fuse_gemm_comms":true},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}'` | SP + AsyncTP | --- ## Commands ### Server (replace `<COMPILATION_CONFIG>` with one of the configs above) ```bash VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \ python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model RedHatAI/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-block \ --trust-remote-code \ --dtype bfloat16 \ -tp 4 \ --gpu-memory-util 0.9 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --max-model-len 8192 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ <COMPILATION_CONFIG> ``` ### Benchmark ```bash python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench serve \ --model RedHatAI/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-block \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 4096 \ --random-output-len 1 \ --num-prompt 16 \ --request-rate inf \ --backend vllm \ --ignore-eos \ --trust-remote-code \ --temperature 0 ``` For the mixed prefill+decode shapes, use `--random-input-len 256 --random-output-len 128 --num-prompt 16` or `--random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 64 --num-prompt 32`. ### Accuracy (GSM8K, 250 questions) Accuracy is measured per arm. Start the server with the arm's compilation config, then run lm_eval while the server is running. Repeat for each arm. **Step 1 — start server** (shown for `asynctp_on`; substitute config for other arms): ```bash VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \ python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model RedHatAI/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-block \ --trust-remote-code --dtype bfloat16 -tp 4 \ --gpu-memory-util 0.9 --max-model-len 8192 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":true,"fuse_gemm_comms":true},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}' ``` | Arm | `--compilation-config` / flag | |---|---| | `asynctp_on` | `{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":true,"fuse_gemm_comms":true},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}` | | `asynctp_off` | `{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":true},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}` | | `compile_nosp` | `{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":false},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}` | | `eager` | `--enforce-eager` (no `--compilation-config`) | **Step 2 — evaluate** (same command for all arms): ```bash python3 -m lm_eval --model local-completions \ --model_args "model=RedHatAI/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-block,base_url=http://localhost:8073/v1,tokenized_requests=False,num_concurrent=1" \ --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --limit 250 ``` --- ## Performance Results ### Pure prefill — `output_len=1`, mean TTFT (ms), mean of 2 runs Gain = (compile_nosp − X) / compile_nosp; positive = X is faster. | Shape | asynctp_on | asynctp_off | compile_nosp | eager | **on vs nosp** | **off vs nosp (SP only)** | **on vs off (AsyncTP-only)** | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 16 prompts × 4096 in | 8879 | 9364 | 10323 | 10653 | **+14.0%** | +9.3% | +5.2% | | 16 prompts × 512 in | 1554 | 1561 | 1756 | 1806 | **+11.5%** | +11.1% | +0.5% | | 2 prompts × 4096 in | 1265 | 1304 | 1509 | 1558 | **+16.2%** | +13.6% | +3.0% | Consistent with the static-FP8 8B case: SP alone captures most of the gain (+9–14%), and AsyncTP's GEMM-comm fusion adds a further +0.5–5.2% on top. ### Mixed prefill + decode — mean of 2 runs Gain = (compile_nosp − X) / compile_nosp for Duration/TPOT/TTFT (positive = X faster); (X − compile_nosp) / compile_nosp for tok/s (positive = X higher throughput). | Shape | asynctp_on | asynctp_off | compile_nosp | eager | **on vs nosp** | **off vs nosp (SP only)** | **on vs off (AsyncTP-only)** | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | **Duration (s)** ↓ lower is better | | | | | | | | | 16 prompts × 256 in × 128 out | 4.13 | 3.38 | 3.76 | 4.30 | −9.7% | **+10.1%** | −22.2% | | 32 prompts × 128 in × 64 out | 2.67 | 2.10 | 2.42 | 3.07 | −10.4% | **+13.0%** | −27.1% | | **Output tok/s** ↑ higher is better | | | | | | | | | 16 prompts × 256 in × 128 out | 502 | 608 | 549 | 477 | −8.6% | **+10.7%** | −17.4% | | 32 prompts × 128 in × 64 out | 769 | 977 | 848 | 672 | −9.3% | **+15.3%** | −21.3% | | **TPOT (ms)** ↓ lower is better | | | | | | | | | 16 prompts × 256 in × 128 out | 25.7 | 19.4 | 21.1 | 26.5 | −21.7% | **+8.3%** | −32.6% | | 32 prompts × 128 in × 64 out | 31.1 | 22.6 | 25.4 | 35.1 | −22.7% | **+11.0%** | −37.6% | | **Mean TTFT (ms)** ↓ lower is better | | | | | | | | | 16 prompts × 256 in × 128 out | 838.5 | 904.1 | 1072.6 | 894.9 | **+21.8%** | +15.7% | +7.3% | | 32 prompts × 128 in × 64 out | 677.2 | 650.1 | 801.7 | 832.8 | **+15.5%** | +18.9% | −4.2% | --- ## Accuracy (GSM8K, 250 questions) | Arm | Accuracy | |---|---:| | asynctp_on (SP + AsyncTP) | 0.784 | | compile_nosp | 0.776 | | eager | 0.772 | | asynctp_off (SP only) | 0.768 | --- ## Summary - **Pure prefill**: SP alone gives +9–14% TTFT; AsyncTP's GEMM-comm fusion adds +0.5–5.2% on top. Clean win, consistent with the static-FP8 8B case, and no accuracy regression. - **Mixed prefill+decode**: SP alone (`asynctp_off`) is still a clean win (+8–15% duration/tok/s/TPOT). But AsyncTP (`asynctp_on`, `fuse_gemm_comms=True`) turns that into a ~9–10% net *loss* vs. `compile_nosp` — a real, repeatable ~20–27pp swing (confirmed stable across both runs on the 32:128:64 shape). **The regression is caused by AsyncTP's GEMM-comm fusion specifically, not by SP.** (Mean TTFT is a queueing artifact on these two shapes and should be ignored — duration/tok/s/TPOT are authoritative.) - **Accuracy**: no statistically significant regression from either SP or AsyncTP (0.768–0.784 across all four arms, well within ±2.6pp SE). - **Recommendation**: enable SP (`enable_sp=true`) for this model/workload without reservation. Do **not** enable `fuse_gemm_comms` unconditionally for block-FP8 8B until the mixed-shape regression is root-caused (likely the fused GEMM-comm collective's overhead isn't hidden by the small per-rank compute chunk in these batch/output-length combos) — either gate it more precisely or scope this case's recommendation to pure-prefill-dominated deployments only.
signals.author: chaojun-zhang

signals.title: [Kernel][PCP] Publish replicated KV updates through PyTorch symmetric memory
signals.text: ## Summary Skip the PCP KV AllGather: each producer writes the final quantized Main-KV and Indexer-K rows into every replica through PyTorch SymmetricMemory. Opt-in (`VLLM_USE_PCP_DIRECT_KV=1`). Feature-off is the current #52046 gather+insert path and stays the same-class reference. ## As-is vs this PR Current `main` after [#52046](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52046) already keeps a **full KV replica on every PCP rank**, but the update still goes through a communication boundary: ```text AS-IS (main / #52046, feature off) ================================== each rank, local tokens | v fused_norm_rope RMSNorm + RoPE emit kv_c / k_pe / indexer_k (does not write the cache) | +---- AllGather kv_c --------+ +---- AllGather k_pe --------+--> every rank now has all tokens +---- AllGather indexer_k ---+ | v receive-side insert do_kv_cache_update --> local Main-KV replica indexer insert --> local Indexer-K replica | v Indexer + sparse MLA read the ordinary local tensors | v existing hidden / output collective (unchanged) ``` This PR deletes that KV-update collective. The producer already holds the final cache bytes, so it stores them into every replica: ```text THIS PR (VLLM_USE_PCP_DIRECT_KV=1) ================================== init (once) symm_mem.empty(full replica) -> rendezvous(PCP group) -> peer_ptrs[rank] each rank, local tokens | v fused_norm_rope RMSNorm + RoPE + FP8 quant (once) | +-- st.final row --> replica[0] @ this rank's slot row +-- st.final row --> replica[1] +-- st.final row --> replica[2] +-- st.final row --> replica[3] | v system-scope release / acquire fence | X no AllGather of kv_c / k_pe / indexer_k X no do_kv_cache_update / indexer insert | v Indexer + sparse MLA still read ordinary local tensors | v existing hidden / output collective (unchanged) ``` Layout and capacity do not change. Attention backends do not learn that the backing is symmetric. For review, in order: 1. **Hook.** `collect_pcp = use_pcp and not direct_kv`. When the flag is on, fused writes the cache through `mla_peer_ptrs` / `indexer_peer_ptrs` and `maybe_gather_*` plus `do_kv_cache_update` do not run. 2. **Slots.** Gathered slot maps are rank-major `[rank0 | rank1 | ...]`. Each producer must use **its own row** (`select_pcp_direct_slot_row`), not the leading slice (rank 0's slots). 3. **Bytes.** Fused oracle: replica rows match a gather-then-insert reference on the same tensors (`fp8_ds_mla` + packed indexer). 4. **Fail-closed.** Multi-host, TP/DCP/DP ≠ 1, CUDA graphs, prefix cache, KV connectors, etc. reject the flag and stay on the collective path. ## Results (this PR, post-#52046 `main`) Same-source 10-pair cold-start engine A/B on 4× GB200. GLM-5.2 NVFP4, TP1/PCP4/DCP1, eager, EP + FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, FP8 KV, prefix caching off. **Only** `VLLM_USE_PCP_DIRECT_KV=0/1` changed. Counterbalanced `AB, BA`. 40/40 JSONs `failed=0`. Changes are paired geometric means; 95% CIs are percentile bootstrap over the 10 log-ratios (200,000 resamples). #### 1,024-input / 32-output, concurrency 16 | Metric | Collective (#52046) | Direct SymmMem | Paired change | 95% CI | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Mean TTFT (ms) | 795.133 | 694.690 | **−12.64%** | **[−13.69%, −11.47%]** | | Mean TPOT (ms) | 202.552 | 197.210 | −2.66% | [−3.95%, −1.37%] | | Request throughput (req/s) | 2.165 | 2.249 | +3.83% | [+2.57%, +5.15%] | | p95 TTFT (ms) | 1147.083 | 999.425 | −12.88% | [−13.99%, −11.70%] | TTFT pairs favoring direct: **10/10** (two-sided sign p=0.00195). #### 3,584-input / 32-output, concurrency 4 | Metric | Collective (#52046) | Direct SymmMem | Paired change | 95% CI | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Mean TTFT (ms) | 592.124 | 514.821 | **−13.05%** | **[−14.23%, −12.08%]** | | Mean TPOT (ms) | 205.571 | 199.345 | −3.03% | [−3.77%, −2.23%] | | Request throughput (req/s) | 0.534 | 0.554 | +3.87% | [+3.04%, +4.69%] | | p95 TTFT (ms) | 907.761 | 783.097 | −13.73% | [−15.07%, −12.56%] | TTFT pairs favoring direct: **10/10** (two-sided sign p=0.00195). KV capacity: **706,624 tokens** on both arms (+0.000%). Kernel microbench (PCP4, 20 warmup / 100 measured, slowest-rank p50, byte-identical images before timing): **4.36×–5.12×** vs three AllGathers + insert, at 1–2048 local tokens/rank. These land in the same ~12–13% TTFT band that #49517 published for the VMM implementation of this data model. The VMM numbers are **not** copied here as this PR's result. ## Relationship to existing PRs | PR | Role | |---|---| | [#49517](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49517) | Idea we port (direct-final replicated KV). Stays open. | | [#52046](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52046) | Current `main` as-is: fused emit + AllGather + insert. Feature-off reference. | | [#50484](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50484) | Common substrate we reuse (SymmMem / peer ptrs / fence). Different object (transient DCP). | | [#50366](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50366) | Precedent that peer-pointer SymmMem can replace VMM. Different object (DCP Top-K). | | [#49741](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49741) / [#49756](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49756) | Other Shared-PCP objects. Not in this diff. | ## Correctness - PCP2/PCP4 fused oracle: `fp8_ds_mla` + Indexer-K (fp8 + scale) replica rows match gather-then-insert on the same inputs, on a packed backing with a nonzero layer offset (guard bytes unchanged). - Destination-row unit test: rank 2 sees its own slots, not rank 0's. - Fail-closed config checks live in `PCPManager.validate_config`. Opt-in allocation/rendezvous is all-or-nothing and fails startup; no ordinary-memory fallback. `PCPManager.direct_kv_enabled` is requested at construct time and is only observed as true after bind succeeds, because a failed allocate/bind aborts startup. - Fence wait uses an unconditional PTX `trap` on timeout (not `device_assert`). - Dummy / padded tokens use a local PAD slot row so the fused write does not index past the slot tensor. ## Scope **In:** single-node NVIDIA, eager, GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek-V3.2 sparse-MLA PCP, replicated Main KV + Indexer K, FP8 / `fp8_ds_mla`, PCP2/PCP4. **Out:** prefix caching, KV connectors, sleep mode, multi-host PCP, TP/DCP/DP > 1, CUDA graphs, async scheduling, DBO, owner-sharded history, Kimi DCP features, a generic SymmMem framework rewrite. Implementation and validation used AI coding assistance. The human submitter reviews the changed lines, sets the acceptance criteria, and owns the numbers above. ## Lineage This is a more common, easier-to-review port of the **direct-final PCP KV** idea from [#49517](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49517) onto the already-merged PyTorch SymmetricMemory path from [#50484](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50484). Same data model as #49517: each PCP producer writes the **final** quantized Main-KV and Indexer-K rows into every replica, then publishes visibility. No KV AllGather. No receive-side insert. Different substrate: no `cuda_vmm.py`, no POSIX FD exchange, no manufactured rank-major virtual address. Reviewers already know `symm_mem.empty → rendezvous → get_buffer → peer_ptrs` from #50484. This PR applies that common API to **persistent PCP cache replicas**, not a transient DCP workspace. ```text #49517 (idea we port) this PR (same idea, common API) --------------------- ------------------------------ cuda_vmm.py vllm/distributed/.../symm_mem.py POSIX FD exchange torch.distributed._symmetric_memory import / map every peer empty -> rendezvous -> get_buffer manufactured rank-major VA int64 peer_ptrs table custom VMM lifetime same release/acquire pattern already reviewed in #50484 review load: new allocator review load: "is the producer + new comms + new cache path writing the right final bytes into the right slots?" ``` ## Experimental: NVLS `multimem.st` (open for discussion) After the P2P path was up, we tried one `multimem.st` into the **same** final replica backing (`handle.multicast_ptr`) instead of a per-peer store loop. Not in this diff; default stays P2P. Numbers are for discussion, not a claim that multicast should land in this PR. PCP4 fused oracle on 4× GB200: P2P and multimem replica bytes both match the gather+insert reference (`p2p_match=True`, `mcast_match=True` on all ranks). Same fused producer + publication fence, 20 warmup / 100 measured, slowest-rank p50, `fp8` MLA: | Local tokens/rank | P2P p50 (µs) | Multimem p50 (µs) | vs P2P | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 141.552 | 133.856 | −5.44% | | 8 | 137.696 | 132.320 | −3.90% | | 32 | 131.376 | 132.752 | +1.05% | | 128 | 131.600 | 134.672 | +2.33% | | 512 | 134.224 | 133.472 | −0.56% | | 2048 | 133.376 | 131.408 | −1.48% | The store is a small slice of fused compute + fence, so the kernel p50 is flat and there is no clear win. We kept P2P as the reviewed path. Happy to follow up with `multimem.st` (or a vectorized `v4.f32` variant) if reviewers want that transport on this backing.
signals.author: foraxe

signals.title: [Bugfix][Parser] Fix DeepSeek V4 and V3.2 tool argument streaming (#52846)
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52846. In DeepSeek V4 and DeepSeek V3.2 parsers (`vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py` and `vllm/parser/deepseek_v32.py`), `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")` was configured. During streaming tool calls, when generating a long string parameter body (e.g. `{"text": "..."}`), the incoming token chunks do not contain `>`. As a result, `ParserEngine._compute_arg_delta()` returned `None` for every single body chunk because `self._arg_structural_chars.isdisjoint(raw_delta)` evaluated to `True`. The entire string parameter body was withheld and buffered until the closing `</parameter>` tag arrived, at which point all accumulated characters were emitted in one large delta. While `_safe_arg_prefix()` was added in #46351 specifically to stream prefix-stable string values for schema-typed properties, it never executed for parameter body chunks because the `arg_structural_chars` check discarded them beforehand. This PR removes `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")` from `deepseek_v4_config()` and `deepseek_v32_config()`, allowing `_dsml_arg_converter` and `_safe_arg_prefix` to stream string argument deltas incrementally in real time as tokens are generated. cc @thegoldenflow @flexwang @keivenchang @YilongL @QwertyJack ### Duplicate Work Check - Verified open and unassigned on #52846 (`gh issue view 52846 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments`). - Verified 0 open PRs for issue #52846 (`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "52846 in:body"`). - Verified no open PRs addressing DeepSeek tool-argument streaming (`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "deepseek v4 tool"`). ## Test Plan - Added regression test `TestLongStringParameterStreaming::test_long_string_parameter_incremental_streaming` in `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py`. - Verified that a long string argument (4096 characters) streams incrementally across chunks before the closing tag, with exact JSON reconstruction. - Verified that all 3,791 parser engine tests pass.
