PYTORCH_NVML_BASED_CUDA_CHECK=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1 TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_vllm ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary Long-running vLLM engine processes leak host memory (VmRSS/VmData) on paths where a libtorch stable-ABI custom op with a `str` argument is dispatched **eagerly** in the hot loop. Each such call leaks ~48 bytes; over hours this grows unbounded and can OOM the engine (~0.5 GB/hour under continuous load in our reproduction). The root cause is **not in vLLM** — it is a bug in PyTorch's stable ABI, which heap-allocates a `std::string` when unboxing a `str` argument and never frees it. **Upstream issue:** https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191340 ## Where it hits vLLM `reshape_and_cache_flash` is registered as a stable op with a `str kv_cache_dtype` argument: - schema: `csrc/libtorch_stable/torch_bindings.cpp` (`reshape_and_cache_flash(Tensor key, ... str kv_cache_dtype, ...) -> ()`) - impl: `csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu` (`void reshape_and_cache_flash(..., const std::string& kv_cache_dtype, ...)`) - bind: `ops.impl("reshape_and_cache_flash", TORCH_BOX(&reshape_and_cache_flash))` On most paths this op is captured into a CUDA graph and replayed, so it is not re-dispatched per step and the leak does not accumulate. But on the **Voxtral/Whisper realtime streaming** path it is dispatched eagerly — once per attention layer per decode step — so every KV-cache write leaks and the process grows without bound. Any other eagerly-dispatched stable op with a `str` argument is affected the same way. ## Symptoms - Steady, linear host-memory growth (VmRSS/VmData) proportional to decode steps, not to batch size or sequence length. - Invisible to `tracemalloc` (the allocation is C++-side, not Python). - Not reclaimed by `malloc_trim(0)` — the memory is live, not fragmentation. - glibc `mallinfo2().uordblks` grows in lockstep with RSS. - Present only on eager (non-CUDA-graph) dispatch paths. ## Root cause (upstream) In PyTorch's `torch/csrc/stable/stableivalue_conversions.h`, the `str` → `std::string` unboxing (`ToImpl<std::string>::call`) does: ```cpp auto strptr = new std::string(data, length); // heap-allocated TORCH_ERROR_CODE_CHECK(torch_delete_string(handle)); return *strptr; // returns a COPY; *strptr is never deleted ``` Each unbox orphans one heap-allocated `std::string` control object (~48 bytes: `sizeof(std::string)` + allocator overhead; the value's characters are irrelevant since short strings like `"auto"` fit small-string optimization). Fix is upstream: construct the string on the stack instead of with `new`. See https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191340 for details and the patch. ## Impact on vLLM - Realtime/streaming ASR paths (Voxtral, Whisper) that dispatch KV-cache writes eagerly leak continuously and can OOM long-running servers. - Standard batched/CUDA-graph serving is largely unaffected because the op is replayed, not re-dispatched. ## Fix / mitigation - **Real fix:** upstream PyTorch (https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191340). The fix is header-only in the stable ABI, so vLLM's custom-op `.so` must be recompiled. - **Possible vLLM-side mitigations** while waiting for an upstream release: - Avoid re-dispatching stable ops with `str` arguments in eager hot loops (e.g. pass the dtype as an enum/int rather than a `str`, if a non-`str` schema is feasible). - Ensure the affected streaming paths use CUDA-graph capture/replay where possible. ## Reproduction Minimal, self-contained (CPU-only) reproduction of the underlying leak — two no-op stable ops identical except one takes a `str` — is in the upstream issue: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191340 ## Environment ``` torch: 2.11.0+cu130 CUDA: 13.0 OS: Linux (x86_64) ``` ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

signal.title: [Bug][Spec Decode] All-NaN logits row is laundered into an out-of-vocab token id by the rejection sampler (device assert far from origin); NaN-metric blind spot on the verify path; uninit-scratch audit
signal.text: ## TL;DR If any verification row of `target_logits` is all-NaN (numerics upset in the model forward — whatever the cause), the V2 GPU-worker rejection sampler does not fail or fall back: its NaN-poisoned block-argmax chain **emits a token id equal to `vocab_size` exactly**, which propagates through `last_sampled_tokens` → `combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens` → `input_ids` and detonates 1–3 steps later as: ``` /pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Indexing.cu:1524: indexSelectSmallIndex: Assertion `srcIndex < srcSelectDimSize` failed. torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered ``` surfacing asynchronously (typically in `AsyncOutput.get_output → copy_event.synchronize()`), far from the origin. We reproduced and instrumented this end-to-end ~10 times. Open issue #42261 (gemma4 + MTP, same assert, intermittent, restart clears it) matches this signature and is plausibly the same bug. Independently, the engine's only NaN detector cannot see these rows (§ NaN-metric gap), and the same file contains a family of latent uninitialized-scratch hazards (§ audit). ## Mechanism (fully instrumented) Configuration: spec decode (dspark; greedy drafts → one-hot verification path), FULL decode cudagraphs, TP4, sustained mixed traffic. All findings verified against `main` as of 2026-08-17. 1. A verification row of `target_logits` arrives **all-NaN** (in our case the numerics fault was in a custom SM80 attention kernel amplifying garbage KV reads — not upstream's code — but any NaN row triggers the rest). 2. In the verify kernel, acceptance comparisons against NaN are false → the position is rejected. 3. `_rejection_resample_kernel` computes the one-hot residual of the NaN row (still NaN), adds gumbel noise (still NaN), and stores per-block maxima/argmaxes. Captured block dump from a live event, `RESAMPLE_BLOCK_SIZE=1024`, vocab 129280 → 127 blocks: ``` local_max[0..125] = NaN (argmax = each block's last lane — NaN-poisoned tl.max) local_max[126] = -inf (its 768 masked padding lanes beat NaN in this comparator order) local_argmax[126] = 129280 (= 126*1024 + 256, the first PADDED lane) ``` 4. `_insert_resampled_kernel`'s cross-block `tl.argmax` over `[NaN ×126, -inf]` is NaN-poisoned and selects block 126, loads `local_argmax[126] = 129280 = vocab_size`, and **stores it into a valid slot of `sampled`**. 5. `post_update` copies it to `last_sampled_tokens`; the next step's `combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens` writes it into `input_ids`; the embedding gather asserts. The failure is worse than the crash: a NaN row whose position is *not* resampled samples an arbitrary in-vocab token **silently**. The crash is the detectable minority. ## Evidence highlights - Bounds guard on the padded `input_ids` window captured the poison pre-crash across multiple events: always exactly `vocab_size` (129280), always via the resample-insert store (per-store clamp counters), `is_bonus` both true and false across events. - Winning-block value bit pattern captured in-kernel: `0xFF800000` (-inf) at block 126 with NaN elsewhere (full 127-block dump above). - With clamp-at-store instrumentation the engine survives indefinitely (45+ contained events in one window), confirming the single injection point. - Race hypotheses excluded by measurement: a cross-kernel greedy-bit disagreement counter read **zero** across >8k steps while mints continued. ## NaN-metric gap `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS` / `corrupted_requests_total` is implemented in `Sampler.sample()` — which the spec-decode verification path never calls. During all of the above, the metric read 0. The engine is blind to NaN logits exactly where they get converted into OOB tokens. Suggest computing `num_nans` on the verification logits as well. ## Proposed fixes 1. **Guard degenerate rows in the resample chain** (minimal): after the cross-block argmax, validate the selected token id (`0 <= id < vocab_size`) and the winning value (finite); on failure, fall back deterministically (e.g., token 0 or the request's last valid token) and increment a corruption counter. This converts undefined behavior into a counted, bounded event. 2. **Close the NaN-metric gap** so operators can see degenerate rows on the spec path. 3. Optionally: make `tl.max`/`tl.argmax` consumers in this file NaN-safe by masking non-finite values to `-inf` before reduction (several sites). ## Audit: latent uninitialized-scratch hazards in the same file While isolating the above we audited `rejection_sampler_utils.py` and found a systemic pattern: **per-request temperature is re-loaded independently by each kernel of a step** (4 independent loads), and those reads gate *writes* to `new_empty` scratch buffers that later kernels *read* under their own temperature load. Nothing enforces agreement (the sampling-state buffers are persistent device arrays updated between steps; async scheduling lets updates land between kernel launches). Five instances: | # | Producer that skips the write | Buffer | Consumer | Worst case | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | stats kernel non-greedy branch skips argmax store | `target_local_argmax` | verify kernel greedy path | uninit int64 emitted as a token id | | 2 | resample kernel greedy-non-bonus early return | `resampled_local_{argmax,max}` | insert kernel | uninit int64 emitted as a token id | | 3 | stats kernel greedy branch skips sumexp | `target_local_sumexp` (+draft) | verify non-greedy accept path | garbage acceptance probabilities | | 4 | `_compute_cumulative_log_p_kernel` `if temp==0: return` | `cumulative_log_p` | 3 gated read sites | `exp(uninit)` ratios (block-verification mode) | | 5 | residual-mass kernel early returns | `local_residual_mass` | `_compute_global_residual_mass` | garbage residuals (block-verification mode) | We hit none of these in production traffic (measured disagreements = 0), but they are trivially fixable (write unconditionally — the values are already computed or nearly free) and the class-level fix (snapshot sampling params once per step for all kernels) closes present and future instances at once. Zero-initializing the scratch is cheap hardening. ## Environment - Observed on vLLM 0.27.1; all cited code verified present on `main` (2026-08-17). - 8×A100 (SM80), TP4, `cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, prefix caching, fp8 KV. - DeepSeek-V4-Flash + dspark (greedy drafts). The NaN *source* in our reproduction was a custom SM80 kernel (not upstream code); the laundering, metric gap, and audit findings are upstream and model-agnostic — any NaN row from any cause takes the same path. ## Reproduction sketch Inject a single all-NaN row into `target_logits` for one verification position (or run any setup that can produce one) under spec decode with rejection sampling; within that step, `sampled` receives a token id ≥ `vocab_size` (frequently exactly `vocab_size`), and the engine dies on the embedding gather 1–3 steps later with the assert cascade above.

signal.title: [Bugfix] Support MistralCommonBackend tokenizers in the xgrammar structured-output backend
signal.text: ## Purpose Structured output (`response_format` / guided decoding) fails with **HTTP 500** for Mistral models when the tokenizer is loaded under the default `tokenizer_mode="auto"`. `transformers>=5.5` returns a `MistralCommonBackend` for Mistral repos. That class subclasses `PreTrainedTokenizerBase` (not `PreTrainedTokenizerFast`) and is not vLLM's `MistralTokenizer`, so: - `is_mistral_tokenizer()` returns `False` (it requires `IS_MISTRAL_TOKENIZER` + `isinstance(..., MistralTokenizer)`), so the working Mistral path in `XgrammarBackend.__post_init__` is skipped; - the `else` branch calls `xgr.TokenizerInfo.from_huggingface()`, whose dispatch matches only `PreTrainedTokenizerFast`, tiktoken-backed, or sentencepiece-backed tokenizers, and otherwise raises `ValueError: Unsupported tokenizer type: ...`. `XgrammarBackend` is constructed lazily on the **first structured-output request** (`vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py` → `grammar_init()`), inside engine-core, so the uncaught `ValueError` surfaces as an HTTP 500. Plain completions on the same server keep working, which makes this look like a model problem rather than a backend one. ## Reproduction No GPU, no HF token, public model: ```python from transformers.tokenization_mistral_common import MistralCommonBackend from vllm.config import StructuredOutputsConfig, VllmConfig from vllm.v1.structured_output.backend_types import StructuredOutputOptions from vllm.v1.structured_output.backend_xgrammar import XgrammarBackend tok = MistralCommonBackend.from_pretrained("mistralai/Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407") cfg = VllmConfig(structured_outputs_config=StructuredOutputsConfig(backend="xgrammar")) backend = XgrammarBackend(cfg, tokenizer=tok, vocab_size=tok.vocab_size) backend.compile_grammar(StructuredOutputOptions.JSON, '{"type":"object"}') ``` On `vllm==0.27.0` (stock, from PyPI): ``` ValueError: Unsupported tokenizer type: <class 'transformers.tokenization_mistral_common.MistralCommonBackend'> ``` With this change: ``` grammar compiled: XgrammarGrammar ``` Diagnostics for that tokenizer: ``` MRO : MistralCommonBackend -> PreTrainedTokenizerBase -> PushToHubMixin -> object IS_MISTRAL_TOKENIZER : <absent> # -> is_mistral_tokenizer() == False isinstance(PreTrainedTokenizerFast) : False # -> xgrammar's first branch misses ``` ## Fix `MistralCommonBackend` already carries everything the Mistral path needs — `tok.tokenizer` is a `mistral_common.MistralTokenizer`, reachable as `.instruct_tokenizer.tokenizer` → `Tekkenizer` — and vLLM already has both a helper to detect it (`mistral_common_tekkenizer()`) and a wrapper that consumes it (`MistralTokenizer.__init__(tokenizer: MistralCommonBackend)`). So rather than adding new vocabulary-construction logic, this change routes a tekken-backed `MistralCommonBackend` through the existing `MistralTokenizer`, which already builds a correct `xgr.TokenizerInfo` (byte-fallback handling, `is_tekken` → `VocabType.RAW`, eos as stop token). The Mistral branch body is unchanged apart from reading the local `tokenizer` variable. ## Test `tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_xgrammar_mistral_common.py` builds the backend from a `MistralCommonBackend` and compiles a JSON grammar. Verified both directions against stock `vllm==0.27.0`: - without the change: `1 failed` (`ValueError: Unsupported tokenizer type`) - with the change: `1 passed` ## Notes - The new branch is deliberately narrow: it triggers only when `mistral_common_tekkenizer()` returns a `Tekkenizer`, i.e. exactly the case reproduced above. Behaviour for every other tokenizer is unchanged, including the `backend="auto"` fallback path. - I did not extend this to sentencepiece-backed `MistralCommonBackend` instances because I have not reproduced a failure there. If maintainers know that path is also affected, widening the condition to any `MistralCommonBackend` would be a small follow-up — happy to do it in this PR if preferred.

signal.title: fix(v1): skip full GC during EngineCore process exit
signal.text: ## Summary Skip explicit full-heap garbage collection when the V1 EngineCore child process is definitively exiting. The normal in-process shutdown behavior is preserved. Only the terminal child-process path propagates process-exit semantics through: ``` EngineCoreProc -> EngineCore -> UniProcExecutor -> GPUWorker -> GPUModelRunner -> distributed cleanup ``` This avoids unfreezing and scanning the frozen startup heap immediately before the operating system reclaims the process. Fixes #48620. ## Changes - Add `process_exiting` semantics to `EngineCore.shutdown()`. - Mark `EngineCoreProc.run_engine_core()` final shutdown as terminal. - Preserve default cleanup for reusable paths such as Ray actors. - Add backward-compatible process-exit shutdown fallbacks to Executor and WorkerBase. - Propagate terminal shutdown only through UniProcExecutor. - Allow V1 and V2 GPU model runners to skip explicit GC during terminal teardown. - Preserve connector, profiler, cache, allocator, worker, and distributed cleanup. - Preserve full-GC behavior for normal in-process shutdown and V1 profiling cleanup. - Add deterministic default and terminal cleanup tests. ## Validation ### Regression tests ```text tests/v1/engine/test_process_exit_cleanup.py 21 passed, 20 warnings ``` The focused regression suite covers normal, SystemExit, and exception EngineCore exits; normal and terminal shutdown; DPEngineCoreProc forwarding; Executor, WorkerBase, WorkerWrapper, and XPUWorker fallbacks/forwarding; UniProc propagation; GPUWorker; V1/V2 GPU model-runner terminal forwarding; V1 profiling cleanup; and distributed cleanup with and without explicit GC. ### Patch coverage ```text Changed executable lines: 53 Covered lines: 51 Patch coverage: 96.2% ``` The only uncovered changed lines are the ROCm/XPU-specific GC branch in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`. The platform behavior was not mocked solely to inflate coverage. ### End-to-end Docker validation The base and PR head were built in isolated Docker images from: ```text base: e6d1310b2ac52e56e266450693af9de12a871a51 Runtime validation was performed on: db0c6ab28ac32bd8a28ff5924b24488ed554c34f ``` Both images used the same precompiled native-extension wheel commit: ```text e6d1310b2ac52e56e266450693af9de12a871a51 ``` This kept the native extensions constant while varying the Python source between the base and PR head. A subsequent test-only commit made the cleanup mocks portable to PyTorch builds where XPU platform branches are active or torch._C._host_emptyCache is unavailable. No runtime code changed. Environment: - Model: Qwen2.5-7B - GPU: NVIDIA RTX 4090 - Python: 3.12.13 - PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 - CUDA: 13.0 - Attention backend: TRITON_ATTN - External flash_attn package: not installed - vLLM FA2/FA3 extensions: available Both runs resolved to the default single-GPU executor topology: ```text distributed_executor_backend=uni ``` Both images successfully loaded the model, generated output, exited with status 0, produced no traceback, and left no EngineCore or Worker processes behind. #### Terminal GC call tracing A diagnostic sitecustomize wrapper traced gc.freeze, gc.unfreeze, and gc.collect using direct os.write output so that the evidence did not depend on logging during interpreter teardown. Each wrapper recorded the call and stack, immediately invoked the saved original function exactly once, and returned the original result. During terminal EngineCore teardown, the base executed: ```text EngineCore.shutdown -> UniProcExecutor.shutdown -> GPUWorker.shutdown -> gc.unfreeze() EngineCore.shutdown -> UniProcExecutor.shutdown -> GPUWorker.shutdown -> GPUModelRunner.shutdown -> gc.collect() ``` The PR head executed neither terminal `gc.unfreeze()` nor terminal `gc.collect()`. This directly confirms that the process-exit propagation removes the targeted explicit GC calls on the default single-GPU UniProc path while preserving successful generation and process exit. #### Non-instrumented timing observation A single non-instrumented run observed: ```text base process_exit_begin -> process exit: 8.816 s head process_exit_begin -> process exit: 4.283 s ``` These values are reported only as a local observation. They are not a general performance benchmark, and no percentage improvement is claimed. ## Validation limitations The non-instrumented exit timings are from a single local run and are reported as observations rather than a general benchmark. The GC tracer changes teardown timing and was used only to establish the presence or absence of explicit GC calls; tracer-run timings were not used. Full pre-commit hooks were not completed locally because external hook environments could not be initialized. CI should run the repository-standard lint and test checks. ### Additional observation In the PR-head runs, the frontend occasionally logged: ```text MPClient: engine core exited unexpectedly; starting cleanup ``` The message appeared after the EngineCore had entered terminal shutdown and before the MPClient cleanup sequence. The process still exited with status 0, produced no traceback, completed MPClient cleanup, and left no residual processes. The ordering is consistent with the EngineCore exiting before the frontend monitor/finalizer has completed its normal-shutdown state transition. This validation does not establish whether that warning should be handled in this PR or separately. ## Compatibility The default behavior remains unchanged: - Normal in-process shutdown still performs explicit GC. - Reusable actors do not receive terminal shutdown semantics. - Out-of-tree/custom executors and workers fall back to their existing `shutdown()` implementation. - CPU, XPU, and custom model runners are not passed GPU-specific cleanup arguments. The optimized terminal propagation applies to UniProcExecutor, where the GPU worker lives in the exiting EngineCore process. Executors with workers in separate processes, including MultiprocExecutor, retain their existing full worker-shutdown behavior. ## AI assistance disclosure This change was developed with AI assistance. The human submitter reviewed the changed lines and validation results.

signal.title: [Kernel][PCP] Publish replicated KV updates through PyTorch symmetric memory
signal.text: ## Summary Skip the PCP KV AllGather: each producer writes the final quantized Main-KV and Indexer-K rows into every replica through PyTorch SymmetricMemory. Opt-in (`VLLM_USE_PCP_DIRECT_KV=1`). Feature-off is the current #52046 gather+insert path and stays the same-class reference. ## As-is vs this PR Current `main` after [#52046](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52046) already keeps a **full KV replica on every PCP rank**, but the update still goes through a communication boundary: ```text AS-IS (main / #52046, feature off) ================================== each rank, local tokens | v fused_norm_rope RMSNorm + RoPE emit kv_c / k_pe / indexer_k (does not write the cache) | +---- AllGather kv_c --------+ +---- AllGather k_pe --------+--> every rank now has all tokens +---- AllGather indexer_k ---+ | v receive-side insert do_kv_cache_update --> local Main-KV replica indexer insert --> local Indexer-K replica | v Indexer + sparse MLA read the ordinary local tensors | v existing hidden / output collective (unchanged) ``` This PR deletes that KV-update collective. The producer already holds the final cache bytes, so it stores them into every replica: ```text THIS PR (VLLM_USE_PCP_DIRECT_KV=1) ================================== init (once) symm_mem.empty(full replica) -> rendezvous(PCP group) -> peer_ptrs[rank] each rank, local tokens | v fused_norm_rope RMSNorm + RoPE + FP8 quant (once) | +-- st.final row --> replica[0] @ this rank's slot row +-- st.final row --> replica[1] +-- st.final row --> replica[2] +-- st.final row --> replica[3] | v system-scope release / acquire fence | X no AllGather of kv_c / k_pe / indexer_k X no do_kv_cache_update / indexer insert | v Indexer + sparse MLA still read ordinary local tensors | v existing hidden / output collective (unchanged) ``` Layout and capacity do not change. Attention backends do not learn that the backing is symmetric. For review, in order: 1. **Hook.** `collect_pcp = use_pcp and not direct_kv`. When the flag is on, fused writes the cache through `mla_peer_ptrs` / `indexer_peer_ptrs` and `maybe_gather_*` plus `do_kv_cache_update` do not run. 2. **Slots.** Gathered slot maps are rank-major `[rank0 | rank1 | ...]`. Each producer must use **its own row** (`select_pcp_direct_slot_row`), not the leading slice (rank 0's slots). 3. **Bytes.** Fused oracle: replica rows match a gather-then-insert reference on the same tensors (`fp8_ds_mla` + packed indexer). 4. **Fail-closed.** Multi-host, TP/DCP/DP ≠ 1, CUDA graphs, prefix cache, KV connectors, etc. reject the flag and stay on the collective path. ## Results (this PR, post-#52046 `main`) Same-source 10-pair cold-start engine A/B on 4× GB200. GLM-5.2 NVFP4, TP1/PCP4/DCP1, eager, EP + FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, FP8 KV, prefix caching off. **Only** `VLLM_USE_PCP_DIRECT_KV=0/1` changed. Counterbalanced `AB, BA`. 40/40 JSONs `failed=0`. Changes are paired geometric means; 95% CIs are percentile bootstrap over the 10 log-ratios (200,000 resamples). #### 1,024-input / 32-output, concurrency 16 | Metric | Collective (#52046) | Direct SymmMem | Paired change | 95% CI | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Mean TTFT (ms) | 795.133 | 694.690 | **−12.64%** | **[−13.69%, −11.47%]** | | Mean TPOT (ms) | 202.552 | 197.210 | −2.66% | [−3.95%, −1.37%] | | Request throughput (req/s) | 2.165 | 2.249 | +3.83% | [+2.57%, +5.15%] | | p95 TTFT (ms) | 1147.083 | 999.425 | −12.88% | [−13.99%, −11.70%] | TTFT pairs favoring direct: **10/10** (two-sided sign p=0.00195). #### 3,584-input / 32-output, concurrency 4 | Metric | Collective (#52046) | Direct SymmMem | Paired change | 95% CI | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Mean TTFT (ms) | 592.124 | 514.821 | **−13.05%** | **[−14.23%, −12.08%]** | | Mean TPOT (ms) | 205.571 | 199.345 | −3.03% | [−3.77%, −2.23%] | | Request throughput (req/s) | 0.534 | 0.554 | +3.87% | [+3.04%, +4.69%] | | p95 TTFT (ms) | 907.761 | 783.097 | −13.73% | [−15.07%, −12.56%] | TTFT pairs favoring direct: **10/10** (two-sided sign p=0.00195). KV capacity: **706,624 tokens** on both arms (+0.000%). Kernel microbench (PCP4, 20 warmup / 100 measured, slowest-rank p50, byte-identical images before timing): **4.36×–5.12×** vs three AllGathers + insert, at 1–2048 local tokens/rank. These land in the same ~12–13% TTFT band that #49517 published for the VMM implementation of this data model. The VMM numbers are **not** copied here as this PR's result. ## Relationship to existing PRs | PR | Role | |---|---| | [#49517](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49517) | Idea we port (direct-final replicated KV). Stays open. | | [#52046](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52046) | Current `main` as-is: fused emit + AllGather + insert. Feature-off reference. | | [#50484](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50484) | Common substrate we reuse (SymmMem / peer ptrs / fence). Different object (transient DCP). | | [#50366](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50366) | Precedent that peer-pointer SymmMem can replace VMM. Different object (DCP Top-K). | | [#49741](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49741) / [#49756](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49756) | Other Shared-PCP objects. Not in this diff. | ## Correctness - PCP2/PCP4 fused oracle: `fp8_ds_mla` + Indexer-K (fp8 + scale) replica rows match gather-then-insert on the same inputs, on a packed backing with a nonzero layer offset (guard bytes unchanged). - Destination-row unit test: rank 2 sees its own slots, not rank 0's. - Fail-closed config checks live in `PCPManager.validate_config`. Opt-in allocation/rendezvous is all-or-nothing and fails startup; no ordinary-memory fallback. `PCPManager.direct_kv_enabled` is requested at construct time and is only observed as true after bind succeeds, because a failed allocate/bind aborts startup. - Fence wait uses an unconditional PTX `trap` on timeout (not `device_assert`). - Dummy / padded tokens use a local PAD slot row so the fused write does not index past the slot tensor. ## Scope **In:** single-node NVIDIA, eager, GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek-V3.2 sparse-MLA PCP, replicated Main KV + Indexer K, FP8 / `fp8_ds_mla`, PCP2/PCP4. **Out:** prefix caching, KV connectors, sleep mode, multi-host PCP, TP/DCP/DP > 1, CUDA graphs, async scheduling, DBO, owner-sharded history, Kimi DCP features, a generic SymmMem framework rewrite. Implementation and validation used AI coding assistance. The human submitter reviews the changed lines, sets the acceptance criteria, and owns the numbers above. ## Lineage This is a more common, easier-to-review port of the **direct-final PCP KV** idea from [#49517](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49517) onto the already-merged PyTorch SymmetricMemory path from [#50484](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50484). Same data model as #49517: each PCP producer writes the **final** quantized Main-KV and Indexer-K rows into every replica, then publishes visibility. No KV AllGather. No receive-side insert. Different substrate: no `cuda_vmm.py`, no POSIX FD exchange, no manufactured rank-major virtual address. Reviewers already know `symm_mem.empty → rendezvous → get_buffer → peer_ptrs` from #50484. This PR applies that common API to **persistent PCP cache replicas**, not a transient DCP workspace. ```text #49517 (idea we port) this PR (same idea, common API) --------------------- ------------------------------ cuda_vmm.py vllm/distributed/.../symm_mem.py POSIX FD exchange torch.distributed._symmetric_memory import / map every peer empty -> rendezvous -> get_buffer manufactured rank-major VA int64 peer_ptrs table custom VMM lifetime same release/acquire pattern already reviewed in #50484 review load: new allocator review load: "is the producer + new comms + new cache path writing the right final bytes into the right slots?" ``` ## Experimental: NVLS `multimem.st` (open for discussion) After the P2P path was up, we tried one `multimem.st` into the **same** final replica backing (`handle.multicast_ptr`) instead of a per-peer store loop. Not in this diff; default stays P2P. Numbers are for discussion, not a claim that multicast should land in this PR. PCP4 fused oracle on 4× GB200: P2P and multimem replica bytes both match the gather+insert reference (`p2p_match=True`, `mcast_match=True` on all ranks). Same fused producer + publication fence, 20 warmup / 100 measured, slowest-rank p50, `fp8` MLA: | Local tokens/rank | P2P p50 (µs) | Multimem p50 (µs) | vs P2P | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 141.552 | 133.856 | −5.44% | | 8 | 137.696 | 132.320 | −3.90% | | 32 | 131.376 | 132.752 | +1.05% | | 128 | 131.600 | 134.672 | +2.33% | | 512 | 134.224 | 133.472 | −0.56% | | 2048 | 133.376 | 131.408 | −1.48% | The store is a small slice of fused compute + fence, so the kernel p50 is flat and there is no clear win. We kept P2P as the reviewed path. Happy to follow up with `multimem.st` (or a vectorized `v4.f32` variant) if reviewers want that transport on this backing.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Core] Reserve the KV null block when validating max_model_len
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #35541 (still not fully resolved). That issue was previously addressed by #41069, which made the startup capacity check account for `num_gpu_blocks_override`. However, #41069 validates against the **total** block count, so the exact-boundary case — where the KV cache holds exactly as many blocks as a `max_model_len` request needs — still passes at startup and then hangs at runtime. It also only covers the override path, not `kv_cache_memory_bytes` or profiled memory. This PR completes the fix. `BlockPool` permanently reserves one block as the null block, so only `num_gpu_blocks - 1` blocks are usable for requests (`BlockPool.get_usage()` already subtracts it). But the startup check (`_check_enough_kv_cache_memory` in `get_kv_cache_configs`) compares `max_model_len` against the **total** block count. A config with exactly `ceil(max_model_len / block_size)` blocks passes the check (it logs `Maximum concurrency for <max_model_len> tokens per request: 1.00x`) but is one usable block short at runtime, so a request can never be scheduled and the engine hangs (0 tok/s). ### When it happens All sources of the block count flow into the same check, so any can hit the boundary: - `num_gpu_blocks_override = N` with `max_model_len == N * block_size` - `kv_cache_memory_bytes` sized to exactly `N` blocks - `gpu_memory_utilization` (including the default) when the profiled block count equals `ceil(max_model_len / block_size)` — uncommon (auto-profiling usually leaves head-room), but the same bug. ### Why it hangs With `block_size=16`, 50 total blocks -> 49 usable (784 tokens), and `max_model_len=800` (needs 50 blocks): 1. Startup: needed = 50, total = 50 -> the check passes. 2. A prompt fits in the 49 usable blocks and starts decoding. 3. When the length crosses 784 tokens it needs a 50th block; only 49 are usable, so `allocate_slots()` returns `None`. 4. The request is preempted, `num_computed_tokens` reset to 0, and requeued. 5. It is re-admitted, needs the same 50 blocks, and fails again. Nothing is running to preempt and there is no infeasibility guard, so it retries identically every step. 6. `running == 0`, `waiting >= 1`, `scheduled_tokens == 0` every step -> 0 tok/s. ### Reproduction (current `main`) ```python from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams # 50 total KV blocks -> BlockPool reserves 1 null block -> 49 usable = 784 tokens. # max_model_len=800 needs ceil(800/16)=50 blocks: the check counts the 50 total # blocks and passes, but only 49 are usable. llm = LLM( model="facebook/opt-125m", load_format="dummy", block_size=16, num_gpu_blocks_override=50, max_model_len=800, ) sp = SamplingParams(max_tokens=40, ignore_eos=True) llm.generate({"prompt_token_ids": list(range(1, 771))}, sp) # current main: hangs forever. With this PR: raises ValueError at startup. ``` ## The fix In `get_kv_cache_configs`, reserve one block (the null block) in the capacity used by the admission check and auto-fit, while allocation keeps using the full memory. Since all sources of the block count funnel into `available_memory`, this covers `num_gpu_blocks_override`, `kv_cache_memory_bytes`, and profiled memory with one change, and keeps auto-fit consistent with the check. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py -k reserves_null_block ``` Plus the reproduction above. ## Test Result - Reproduction — before: hangs at 0 tok/s; after: raises at startup with `ValueError: ... max seq len (800) ... estimated maximum model length is 784` (= 49 usable blocks × 16). - New unit tests cover the boundary for both the override and the memory-derived paths; related `test_kv_cache_utils.py` tests pass with no regressions. ## Not a duplicate #41069 (merged) is override-only and validates against the total block count, leaving the null-block boundary unfixed. #35542 (an earlier, unmerged attempt) added a separate override-only check. This PR fixes the shared capacity accounting for all sources of the block count. --- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate and draft this change; all changed lines were reviewed and the tests were run locally as described above.

signal.title: [Core] Sync DP state on the first step of a wave
signal.text: Part of #51476. Independent of #52914 (no shared commits, either can land first): #52914 makes the pause-manufactured GPU work harmless; this PR makes it (nearly) not exist. ## Purpose Pausing an idle MoE DP engine kick-starts every rank into the stepping loop so the ranks can reach the pause-consensus all-reduce — and the fixed every-32-step sync cadence in `_has_global_unfinished_reqs` then forces **32 dummy forwards per rank per pause call** before the pause can complete. For RL post-training, which pauses on every weight sync, that is seconds of latency and pure GPU burn on every training step. Measured with a ~110ms inflated step: `pause_generation()` on an idle DP=2+EP engine takes **3.40s**. The same cost is paid a second time by `sleep()`, which internally re-runs `pause_scheduler` (it must: it is the quiescence consensus for direct-sleep callers and enforces `mode="abort"` semantics on requests kept by a prior `pause(mode="keep")`). This PR caps that redundancy at one dummy step too. The burst cannot simply be skipped per-rank: ranks must enter the blocking gloo all-reduce with equal forward-launch counts, or a peer's in-flight collective waits for a launch that never comes and its host never reaches the all-reduce — distributed deadlock. Any cadence decision must therefore be a pure function of state all ranks observe identically. ## Change One condition: also sync on the **first** step of a wave (`step_counter == 1`), keeping the every-32 cadence afterwards. `step_counter` is already rank-synchronized (reset together at the wave-end consensus, restored by the elastic-EP state sync), so the new cadence remains a pure function of lockstep state — no new state, no protocol change, immune to elastic EP by construction. Effect: an idle-engine pause reaches consensus after **one** dummy forward instead of 32. A mid-wave pause still detects at the next cadence point, but those steps are real serving work. Steady-state serving pays one extra gloo all-reduce per wave, on the step where the wave's first real batch is already running. `step_counter` semantics (+1 per step, reset at wave end) are unchanged; its other consumers (`SchedulerStats.step_counter`, `_should_throttle_prefills`) are unaffected, and `test_dp_prefill_schedule_interval` is included in the runs below. ## Test Plan Two new unit tests (no GPU, scripted `sync_dp_state`): a normal wave syncs at steps {1, 32, 64}; an idle-engine pause (`pending_pause=True`) reaches consensus on step 1 and sets `ignore_start_dp_wave`. Regression: `tests/v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py -k "dp_pause or dp_sleep or prefill_schedule"` — includes the staggered-race and barrier-deadlock guards and the late-request pair from #51481. ```bash python -m pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py -k dp_sync -v python -m pytest tests/v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py -k "dp_pause or dp_sleep or prefill_schedule" -v ``` ## Test Result `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (`0.26.1rc1.dev942`), A/B in containers on 2×H200 (`patch -p1` of this diff into site-packages; mount the branch's `tests/`). | suite | before (nightly) | after (this PR) | |---|---|---| | `test_engine_core.py -k dp_sync` | **2 failed** | **2 passed** | | `test_async_llm_dp.py` (12 cases) | 12 passed | 12 passed | Pause latency, measured with #52914's barrier applied in both arms (an idle-engine `pause_generation()` on DP=2+EP PowerMoE-3b, dummy step inflated to ~110ms to make the burst visible): | scenario | 32-step cadence | with this PR | |---|---|---| | `pause_generation()` wall time, idle engine | **3.40s** | **0.17s** | | second pause+drain immediately before `sleep()` | 3.40s | **0.20s** | <details> <summary>Reproduction: measure the pause burst (same kit as #52914)</summary> The scripts and container invocation are in the description of #52914 (`gpupatch.py` instruments `execute_dummy_batch` with `torch.cuda._sleep` and a stream-idle probe; `repro_gpu.py` times `pause_generation()` on an idle DP=2 engine and the pause+drain-before-sleep recipe). Run them on bare nightly vs. nightly + this patch to reproduce the 3.40s → 0.17s delta; the per-pause dummy-forward count per rank drops from 32 to 1 in the instrumentation log. </details> ## Essential Elements - Not a duplicate: `gh pr list --search "dp sync cadence"` / `"step_counter pause"` show no open PR touching the DP finish-sync cadence; filed under #51476 as a follow-up alongside #52914. - Control-plane only; no effect on model output, so no eval run is included. - AI assistance was used (Claude; the design was adversarially reviewed with a second model, which surfaced the elastic-EP divergence risk that motivated the stateless form). The submitter has reviewed each changed line and the test runs above.

signal.title: [Performance][Model] Fuse GLM indexer attention projections
signal.text: ## Summary Fuse two pairs of GLM-5.2 sparse-indexer projections when they consume the same activation and use compatible unquantized BF16 linear methods: - pack indexer `wk` and `weights_proj` into the attention `fused_qkv_a_proj` - pack indexer `wq_b` into the attention `q_b_proj` The fusion is limited to CUDA GLM indexer layers without LoRA or MTP. The checkpoint loader continues to accept the original parameter names and handles the existing FP8-indexer-`wk` checkpoint layout by dequantizing it into the appropriate fused shard. ## Why The indexer projections currently launch separate GEMMs beside attention projections that consume the same tensors. Packing compatible weights removes two GEMM launches per indexer layer while retaining the existing tensor-parallel layout and checkpoint format. ## Impact This reduces decode TPOT for GLM-5.2 NVFP4 at TP4. The fusion is enabled only when both participating linears use the same unquantized method and parameter dtype; other quantization configurations keep the existing path. Focused tests cover: - loading a TP-sharded attention Q weight together with replicated indexer Q - loading indexer K and score weights into the fused QKV-A projection - routing an FP8 indexer K checkpoint through dequantization into the fused parameter - numerical projection output from the packed weights ## Performance Measured on Slurm node `gb200-rack1-03` with GLM-5.2 NVFP4, TP4, dummy weights, FlashInfer autotune disabled, max concurrency 1, 128 input tokens, 128 output tokens, 2 warmup requests, and 20 measured requests. | | Baseline | Fused | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Mean TPOT | 7.1569 ms | 7.0201 ms | -1.91% | | Decode TPS (`1000 / mean TPOT`) | 139.73 | 142.45 | +1.95% | | Completed / failed | 20 / 0 | 20 / 0 | — | Decode used the full CUDA graph at batch size 1. Although piecewise CUDA graphs were enabled, the 128-token prefill exceeded the captured sizes `[1, 2]`, so TTFT did not use a piecewise CUDA graph. TTFT is excluded from the decode-TPS numbers above. The benchmark compared baseline `425d3934f4` with fused `ad7efb59f2`; the fusion diff is carried here as `0e23c8eb0f` after splitting it from the unrelated dead-code change. ## Duplicate-work check Searched open PRs for `GLM indexer`, `indexer linear fusion`, `GLM indexer projection fusion`, and `wk_weights_proj`. PR #39943 overlaps indexer and attention GEMMs using a side stream but does not pack these same-input projections into single GEMMs. Other open indexer PRs target kernels, ROCm paths, sparse-index remapping, or logits precision. signal.title: [Core][V1] Support trace_decode_token_ids for deterministic decode replay
signal.text: Add inference trace-replay: a new SamplingParams.trace_decode_token_ids field that forces the v1 sampler to emit a predetermined sequence of decode token IDs, step by step, instead of sampling. Real logprobs and token ranks are still computed from the unmodified logit distribution. The sampler injects each trace token after sampling (so logprobs stay real); InputBatch tracks the trace per request in parallel with spec_token_ids; and EngineCore.add_request caps generation to the trace length / forces ignore_eos, falling back to normal sampling (with a warning) for incompatible modes (speculative decoding, n > 1). Tests cover the SamplingParams field, sampler injection (including async -1 placeholders and past-end-of-trace), and engine-core admission. A demo example script is added under examples/generate/. ## Purpose Add **inference trace-replay**: a new `SamplingParams.trace_decode_token_ids` field that forces the v1 sampler to emit a predetermined sequence of decode token IDs, step by step, instead of sampling. Real logprobs and token ranks are still computed from the unmodified logit distribution at each step. **Motivation.** The goal is to make a request follow a *fixed* token trace and return the logprobs the model assigns to that exact trace. This is useful for: - **Quantifying differences between settings/backends.** Replaying the same trace under different configs (dtype, quantization, attention/MoE backend, TP size, etc.) and comparing per-token logprobs gives a direct, apples-to-apples measure of numerical divergence on identical token sequences. - **RL training.** It lets you recompute logprobs for a rollout's exact tokens under the training engine, so the rollout↔train logprob gap can be measured and minimized — without re-sampling and drifting onto a different trajectory. **Why decode-replay and not prefill-only scoring?** Computing logprobs by prefilling the full (prompt + response) sequence does *not* faithfully reproduce the decode-time distribution: many models run **different operators / kernels in the prefill path vs. the decode path** (e.g. attention and MoE kernels differ between the two phases). To measure the logprobs a model would actually produce while *decoding*, the tokens must go through the decode path one step at a time — which is exactly what trace-replay does. ### How it works 1. Set `SamplingParams.trace_decode_token_ids` to the list of decode token IDs to force. 2. The sampler injects each trace token **after** sampling (`Sampler._inject_trace_tokens` in `vllm/v1/sample/sampler.py`), so logprobs stay real — they are computed from the original logits, before injection. 3. `InputBatch` tracks the trace per request in parallel with `spec_token_ids` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_input_batch.py`); the per-request step index counts real output tokens, skipping the trailing `-1` async-scheduling placeholder. 4. `EngineCore.add_request` caps generation to the trace length and forces `ignore_eos`, so EOS tokens inside the trace do not halt generation early. It falls back to normal sampling (with a warning) for incompatible modes (speculative decoding, `n > 1`). ### Not a duplicate No open PR addresses this — searched the repo for open PRs matching `trace_decode_token_ids` and `trace`/`replay` in title (0 results). The closest existing features are `logprob_token_ids` (only *scores* a fixed token set, doesn't force the output sequence) and `spec_token_ids` (speculative decoding, different purpose); neither forces a predetermined decode trace. ## Test Plan ```bash # Unit tests (CPU-only, no GPU required) .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/sample/test_trace_replay.py \ tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_trace_replay.py -v # Lint / type-check as in CI pre-commit run --all-files pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual ``` - `tests/v1/sample/test_trace_replay.py` — `SamplingParams` field defaults, clone preservation, and validation (empty / negative / non-int rejected); sampler injection covering step 0, mixed per-request steps, past-end-of-trace (no-op), the async `-1` placeholder, and the unset/none path. - `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_trace_replay.py` — engine-core admission: generation bounds capped to trace length + `ignore_eos` forced; fallback to normal sampling for speculative decoding and `n > 1`. - Demo: `examples/generate/trace_replay_offline.py` — greedy-generate to capture decode tokens, then replay them and assert a token-by-token match while printing per-token logprobs. ## Test Result ```text $ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/sample/test_trace_replay.py \ tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_trace_replay.py tests/v1/sample/test_trace_replay.py .............. [ 82%] tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_trace_replay.py ... signal.title: fix: don't ship uninitialized prompt logprobs after remote prefill
signal.text: Fixes #50792 ## Why this is not a duplicate Checked `gh pr list --state open --search "50792 in:body"` and related prompt_logprobs/PD-disagg searches — no open PR addresses this. Issue has no assignee. ## Summary In `_get_prompt_logprobs_dict` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`), the last-chunk branch shipped the target `LogprobsTensors` *before* checking whether anything remains to fill: ```python else: num_logits = num_remaining_tokens completed_prefill_reqs.append(req_id) prompt_logprobs_dict[req_id] = logprobs_tensors # shipped unconditionally if num_logits <= 0: continue # copy_ never runs ``` When an external KV connector (Mooncake/NIXL/LMCache) pre-fills the whole prompt, `num_computed_tokens` is advanced to `prompt_len`, so `num_remaining_tokens` is 0 or negative. The freshly-created `LogprobsTensors.empty_cpu` is uninitialized (`torch.empty(int32)`), and since this is the first and only visit the copy_ never runs — the decoder then crashes with `OverflowError` decoding garbage int32 token ids. The fix ships the tensors only when there is something to fill (`num_logits > 0`) or the tensors were already populated in prior chunked-prefill steps (`logprobs_preexisting`). The latter keeps the local path working: on the final chunk `num_logits` is 0 but the tensors hold all produced prompt logprobs and must still be returned. (The suggested fix in the issue unconditionally drops the last-chunk ship, which would silently discard prompt logprobs on the local chunked-prefill path.) ## Model evaluation No model weights or output-affecting computation is touched. For requests affected by the bug the prompt_logprobs are simply not emitted (the prefiller would need to return them, as the issue notes); no generated text is changed. ## Tests Added `TestGetPromptLogprobsDict` in `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py`: - `test_skips_remote_prefilled_request` — remote-prefilled request (`num_computed_tokens == prompt_len`) must not ship uninitialized tensors. Fails on the unpatched code (verified by reverting), passes with the fix. - `test_ships_preexisting_tensors_on_final_chunk` — final chunk (`num_remaining_tokens == 0`) with tensors populated in prior steps still ships them, guarding the local path. Both run fully on CPU (no accelerator needed; `_sync_device` stubbed). Commands and results: - `python -m pytest "tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::TestGetPromptLogprobsDict" -q` → 2 passed. - `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on both changed files → clean. - mypy: no new errors in changed lines (gpu_model_runner.py's 51 errors and the test file's errors are all pre-existing, confirmed by diffing against the unmodified files). AI assistance was used in the design and implementation of this change.

signal.title: [WIP][Feature] Add layerwise KV cache transfer support with mooncake session API
signal.text: ## Purpose ### What this PR does This PR implements [RFC #51930](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51930) — layerwise (per-layer) KV cache transfer for the Mooncake store connector, reusing vLLM's existing layerwise infrastructure (`@maybe_transfer_kv_layer` decorator) to pipeline KV load/save with per-layer attention computation, and integrating the **Mooncake Session API** (https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/2881) to eliminate the key-explosion problem. Specifically: 1. **Per-layer task construction & dispatch** — At each scheduler step, per-layer `LayerTransferTask` objects are pre-built for every active request. During the forward pass, the `@maybe_transfer_kv_layer` decorator drives the pipeline: `wait_for_layer_load(layer.i)` → attention forward → `save_kv_layer(layer.i)`, per layer, with per-layer `threading.Event` synchronization. The last layer's `save_kv_layer()` waits for all layer saves to complete. 2. **Session API integration (key explosion fix)** — Instead of encoding the layer index into the key, each KV block keeps a **single content-hash key**, and its data is stored as one contiguous page covering all layers. Per-layer read/write is addressed by a byte offset `layer_id × page_size_bytes + segment_offset` via the Session API's range-based operations. This restores the O(M) key space, dramatically reducing lookup and master overhead. ### Key design points - **No scheduler / engine / model-execution changes** — the PR implements the layerwise hooks entirely inside the Mooncake store connector, reusing `@maybe_transfer_kv_layer`. (The one exception is `MooncakeStoreScheduler` forcing `load_async = False`, see below.) - **Requires PIECEWISE cudagraph** — layerwise hooks contain blocking Python synchronization that cannot be captured in monolithic CUDA graphs, so `requires_piecewise_for_cudagraph()` signals the framework to use PIECEWISE capture when layerwise mode is on. - **`load_async` disabled** — layerwise mode embeds KV load into the forward pass (requests enter RUNNING directly); the async-load path (which moves requests to `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`) is incompatible and is disabled. ## Changed Files #### `mooncake/store/worker.py` The bulk of the implementation. Adds: - **`KVCacheStoreSendingThread` (save path)**: - `start_put_sessions(keys, object_size)` — `batch_put_session_start` to reserve object space before the forward. - `_revoke_range_keys(keys)` — `batch_put_session_revoke` for failed/partial puts. - `_handle_layer_range_task()` — Session-API save: layers `0..N-2` do `batch_put_from_multi_buffer_ranges` at layer offsets; layer `N-1` additionally calls `batch_put_session_end` to commit. - `_handle_layer_task()` — legacy per-layer-key save path: save kv cache via `batch_put_from_multi_buffers` without mooncake session API; on the last layer marks the request finished. - **`KVCacheStoreRecvingThread` (load path)**: - `start_get_sessions(keys)` / `end_get_sessions(keys)` — open/close get sessions. - `_handle_layer_range_task()` — Session-API load via `batch_get_into_multi_buffer_ranges`; - `_handle_layer_task()` — legacy per-layer-key load path: `batch_get_into_multi_buffers` pulls the layer's KV; signals the per-layer load-finished event and finalizes the request on the last layer. - **`MooncakeStoreWorker`**: - `_init_layerwise_config()` — per-layer task/event initialization, page-size computation, Session API state. - `_start_layerwise_sessions()` — collect deduplicated save/load keys, open put/get sessions before task construction. - `_build_layer_tasks_from_requests()` — build per-layer `LayerTransferTask`s for save and load. - `save_kv_layer()` / `wait_for_layer_load()` — per-layer dispatch driven by `@maybe_transfer_kv_layer`; last-layer barrier waits for all saves, closes get sessions, resets state. - `_wait_for_all_layer_saves()` / `_reset_layer_state()` / `_close_load_sessions_once()` — synchronization and cleanup. #### `mooncake/store/data.py` - **`key_for_layer(hash, layer_id)`** — legacy per-layer key (`...@layer:N`). - **`key_for_block(hash)`** — Session-API block-level key (no layer suffix). - **`prepare_values_for_layer(chunks, block_ids, layer_id)`** — compute per-layer memory addresses via `block_len` slicing. - **`prepare_values_for_layer_offset(chunks, block_ids, layer_id)`** — compute per-layer addresses, sizes, **byte offsets** (`layer_id × page_size_bytes + segment_offset`), and block IDs (Session API path). - **`LayerTransferTask`** — per-layer transfer task data structure. #### `mooncake/store/connector.py` - **`start_load_kv()`** — builds per-layer tasks before the model forward when layerwise mode is on (was a no-op). - **`wait_for_layer_load()` / `save_kv_layer()`** — forward per-layer hooks to the worker. - **`_layerwise_enabled`** property and **`requires_piecewise_for_cudagraph()`** — signals PIECEWISE cudagraph requirement. #### `mooncake/store/scheduler.py` - **Disable `load_async` in layerwise mode** — layerwise embeds KV load into forward pass; requests must enter RUNNING directly, so the async-load path (`WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`) is skipped. ## Test Plan ``` .venv/bin/python -m pytest signal.title: [CPU] [1/n] Start migrating the CPU extension to the libtorch stable ABI
signal.text:
## Purpose This PR continues the libtorch stable ABI migration (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26946) for vLLM, and is the first PR dedicated completely to the stable CPU build. First CPU libtorch stable-ABI PR. Migrates `silu_and_mul`, `gelu_\*`, `rms_norm`, `fused_add_rms_norm`, and `rotary_embedding` into new corresponding `_C*_stable_libtorch` libraries. Leftover CPU kernels stay on `_C` / `_C_AVX*` until later PRs. cc @janeyx99, @Harry-Chen ### New file: `csrc/libtorch_stable/cpu/cpu_types_arm_vec.hpp` `cpu_types_arm.hpp` used to get its `Vectorized` primitives from `at::vec` (unstable ABI), so this header is a small header-only replacement using only `` and stable `torch/headeronly` types. It specializes `Vectorized` for `float/c10::Half/c10::BFloat16` and implements only the ops/conversions the migrated kernels actually call (no full `at::vec` API surface). `BF16` load/store/convert use hardware NEON instructions when `ARM_BF16_SUPPORT` is set, falling back to bit-manipulation on [uint16x8_t](url) otherwise (see truncation note below). **NOTE:** `csrc/libtorch_stable/cpu/cpu_types_arm_vec.hpp`'s `f32_to_bf16x4()` only uses the hardware `vcvt_bf16_f32` conversion when `ARM_BF16_SUPPORT` is defined (i.e. the build detected `FEAT_BF16`). On ARM hosts without that extension, it falls back to a plain bit-shift truncation. This is in contrast to ATen which does round-to-nearest-even with an explicit NaN check. Practical impact: at most a 1-ULP difference in bf16 outputs on non-FEAT_BF16 ARM hardware only. ## Test Plan - [x] CPU build produces leftover `_C` / `_C_AVX*` **and** the matching `*_stable_libtorch` modules. - [x] `torch-abi-audit` reports the three `*_stable_libtorch` libraries as **STABLE** (`unstable=0`) and leftover `_C` / `_C_AVX*` as **UNSTABLE**. **unit test** VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -x --disable-warnings tests/kernels/core/test_cpu_activation.py VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -x --disable-warnings tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -x --disable-warnings tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_fused_moe.py VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -x --disable-warnings tests/kernels/test_onednn.py Local testing was only done on the x86_64 architecture. The ARM CPU should be tested in the CI through `.buildkite/scripts/hardware_ci/run-cpu-test-arm.sh`. ## Test Results ---

------------------------------------------------------------------------------- geomean 1.003x +0.3% slower ``` **Kernel-bound (`2048x4096`)** — no meaningful regression. Geometric mean over the 10 ops is **1.00×** (within ~0.1%). Individual ops stay within about ±3% (`gelu_quick` +2.8% slower on stable is the largest outlier; `rms_norm` was 2.7% faster). **Dispatch-bound (`1x64`)** — calls are ~4µs, so the C-shim / boxed-dispatch path may show up in the runtime differences. Across repeats the geometric mean was **< 1% slower** on stable. That is a fraction of a microsecond per call and is negligible in a forward pass.

signal.title: [BugFix] bound FlashMLA sparse decode intermediate tensors size
signal.text: ## Purpose Fix #44545 - not in an ideal way though. When FlashMLA sparse kernel is selected with FP8 KV cache dtype, FlashMLA sparse decode kernel(https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashMLA/blob/a8f794d1251cbfd88a5011445dd5582289c727e4/csrc/api/sparse_decode.h#L184) is called in mixed batch mode. This kernel internally allocates intermediate tensors (`o_accum`) on call, which quickly dominates the usual unallocated workspace size (~2GB per the comment in `flashmla_sparse.py`) for long prefill: For 32k input on H200, the bytesize of `o_accum` is ``` # b = 1 # num_sm_parts = 1 # s_q = 32768 # h_q = 64 # d_v = 512 (b + num_sm_parts) * s_q * h_q * d_v * 4 bytes = 8 GiB ``` For BF16 KV cache, a different kernel (FlashMLA sparse prefill kernel - https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashMLA/blob/a8f794d1251cbfd88a5011445dd5582289c727e4/csrc/api/sparse_fwd.h#L101) is called, which does not allocate a massive VRAM on kernel call and thus does not suffer an OOM contrary to the FP8 code branch. (Note the additional `d_v` factor in the formular for `o_accum`, no other scratch tensors in FlashMLA have this factor thus negligible in terms of VRAM occupancy) Hence we chunk the mixed-batch input into manageable bytes (`VLLM_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_MAX_SCRATCH_MB`) and loop over the chunks to aggregate the output attention tensor, which is in the same spirit as the indexer budget management logic in #36178. Due to the mechanism (looping the kernel over sub-chunks instead of single big shot), it may incur a throughput penalty as a tradeoff, but I have no better idea yet. As the context window for MLA model families keep growing, FP8 KV cache is kind of inevitable, so I think this PR can work as a bandaid. ## Test Plan No OOM for the reproducer in #44545 ## Test Result pass --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>
signal.author: cjackal

signal.title: [Bugfix] Stop mamba align prefill at the replay boundary
signal.text: Fixes #50235 `_mamba_block_aligned_split` picks its mandatory chunk stops from `last_cache_position = num_tokens - num_tokens % block_size`. When the prompt length is an exact multiple of the block size that is `num_tokens` itself, so the prefill runs as a single chunk and, in `align` mode where SSM state only materializes at chunk ends, the only Mamba state cached sits at `num_tokens`. `get_computed_blocks` caps every lookup at `num_tokens - 1`, one token below it, so the Mamba group reports a 0-token hit and the reconciled hybrid hit is 0 even though full attention has the whole prefix. The patch adds the replay boundary, `(num_tokens - 1) // block_size * block_size`, as another mandatory stop. It is clamped to `last_cache_position`, so it only differs from an existing stop when `num_tokens % block_size == 0`, and it is always a duplicate under eagle (which already backs `last_cache_position` off by a block). Cost is one extra scheduling step for prompts whose length is an exact multiple of the block size. Verified on CPU only, driving a real `Scheduler` with a full attention + Mamba `align` KV cache config (block 16, prefix caching on, no connector): a producer prompt of 32 tokens followed by the same 32-token prompt went from a 0-token local prefix hit to 16, and 48 -> 48 went from 0 to 32. Producer lengths 31 and 33 were already fine and are unchanged, and `mamba_cache_mode="all"` is unaffected. A sweep over producer lengths 1-66, consumer lengths P, P+1, P+2, block/hash sizes 16/16 and 16/4, both cache modes, two token budgets and two pool sizes shows no other change. Tests run: - `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py` -> 18 passed. The new test `test_mamba_align_split_stops_at_replay_boundary` fails with the scheduler change reverted (`assert 4096 == 3584`). - `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`, `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/` -> 198 passed, 1 failure that only reproduces with `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=ERROR` set (a caplog assertion) and passes without it. - `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` -> 136 passed, 1 failure (`test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders`) that reproduces on a clean tree. - `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both changed files. Not verified: nothing here ran on a real Kimi-K3 deployment, on 8x TP, with fp8 KV cache, or with the `OffloadingConnector`, so no model eval is included. The change only moves a chunk boundary and does not touch what is computed, so model output is unchanged by construction. One caveat on the reported reproduction. Rows 1 and 4 of the table in the issue reproduce exactly. Rows 2 and 3 (producer 3072, consumer 3073 / 3074) do not: a consumer of `P+1` tokens has a lookup cap of exactly `P`, so it still reaches the state at `P` both before and after this patch. The case I do reproduce has the same trigger, a producer whose prompt length is an exact multiple of the block size, with the consumer's cap landing below that boundary. There may be a second cause behind rows 2 and 3 that this patch does not address. Thanks to the reporter for the length table, which is what made the boundary condition obvious. AI assistance was used to investigate and write this change. Duplicate check: no open PR references #50235. Two open PRs do touch `_mamba_block_aligned_split` and neither covers this. #45477 fixes the eagle prune zeroing `last_cache_position` on short prompts, which lets chunk ends drift off the block grid and poisons the cache under spec decode; that is a correctness bug on a different branch of the same function. #48815 adds an opt-in MTP retention tweak behind `VLLM_MAMBA_ALIGN_RETAIN_MTP_CACHE_BLOCK` and explicitly leaves prompts ending exactly at a block boundary on the existing eagle backoff. This change is on the non-eagle path and adds a stop that neither PR adds.

signal.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Reject n > 1 in the Rust /inference/v1/generate route
signal.text: ## Purpose Closes #52843 With `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, `/inference/v1/generate` silently ignores `n > 1`: `vllm_text::SamplingParams` has no `n` field, so the key is dropped at deserialization and a single choice is returned. The Rust OpenAI routes already reject `n > 1` explicitly; this makes the raw generate route do the same. Route-local change only (a wrapper capturing `n` + validation mirroring the completions validator); the shared `vllm_text` crate is untouched. Rust-frontend counterpart of #52399, which fixed the same silent drop in the Python frontend and skips its regression test under the Rust frontend. ## Demo ```bash curl -s localhost:8000/inference/v1/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"token_ids": [1, 2, 3], "sampling_params": {"max_tokens": 5, "n": 4}, "stream": false}' ``` Before — HTTP 200, three completions silently missing: ```json {"request_id":"42a4300a","choices":[{"index":0,"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"length","token_ids":[1805,3263,1085,138472,55057]}], ...} ``` After — HTTP 400: ```json {"error":{"message":"Only n=1 is supported.","type":"invalid_request_error","param":"n","code":"invalid_request_error"}} ``` ## Test Plan / Result New tests: validator (`rejects_parallel_sampling`, `accepts_explicit_n_one`) and HTTP route level (`raw_generate_rejects_parallel_sampling`). `cargo test -p vllm-server --lib`, fmt and clippy: all pass.
signal.author: qgallouedec

signal.title: [Bugfix] Fix RustToolParser streaming final flush
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #51549. Rust-backed tool parsers may retain an ambiguous partial tool-call marker in their incremental buffer. The non-streaming `RustToolParser` path calls `finish()`, but the streaming path previously had no finalization hook. As a result, buffered text could be silently omitted when generation ended. For example, MiniMax M3 streaming output for: ```text plain ]<]minimax[>[<tool_ca ``` previously emitted only `plain `, while non-streaming parsing returned the complete text. This change: - adds a `finish_streaming()` hook to `RustToolParser`; - calls it from `DelegatingParser` when generation finishes; - uses the Rust parser's `reset()` result to recover uncommitted text after parse/finalization errors; - degrades later deltas in a failed stream to normal content instead of silently dropping them; and - reuses one delta-message merge helper for engine and non-engine parser finalization. Streaming recovery preserves events that were already committed. It does not attempt to retract a structured tool call that may already have been sent; only the parser's uncommitted suffix is recovered as content. AI assistance was used to investigate the lifecycle mismatch, construct regression cases, draft the implementation, and review counterexamples. I reviewed the final diff and the test results below. ## Test Plan - Cover a partial MiniMax M3 tool-start marker at end of stream. - Cover a completed first invocation followed by a truncated second invocation, ensuring the first remains structured and is not leaked into content. - Cover `parse_into()` error recovery, later-delta pass-through, parser reuse, and the real `DelegatingParser(finished=True)` path. - Run the MiniMax M3 and generic Rust tool-parser unit-test files. ## Test Result Before the fix, the minimal stream-end regression failed because streaming content was only: ```text plain ``` instead of: ```text plain ]<]minimax[>[<tool_ca ``` After the fix: ```text 19 passed, 3 warnings in 2.40s ``` Command: ```bash python -m pytest -q \ tests/tool_parsers/test_minimax_m3_tool_parser.py \ tests/tool_parsers/test_rust_tool_parser.py ``` `git diff --check` also passes.

signal.title: [Bug]: Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime permanent engine hang on a specific audio file via /v1/audio/transcriptions (empty multimodal embeddings)
signal.text: > **About this report**: This analysis was produced automatically by **Hermes (an autonomous AI agent)** on behalf of a user. Reproduction happened on a rented cloud GPU instance (vast.ai, RTX 3090 24 GB, CUDA 13.0.2) accessed via SSH — there is no local GPU involved. ### Your current environment ```text OS : Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm) (x86_64) — vast.ai cloud instance GPU : NVIDIA RTX 3090 (24 GB, sm_86) CUDA Version : 13.0.2 Python : 3.12 vLLM Version : 0.27.1 (official image vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1) VLLM Build Commit : 6e448d0ea9bf3d88d898b65449ca6dc2aec170ac Model : mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602 (snapshot 2769294da9567371363522aac9bbcfdd19447add) vLLM serve args : --tokenizer-mode mistral --config-format mistral --load-format mistral --trust-remote-code --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE"}' --max-model-len 16000 --max-num-seqs 1 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --served-model-name whisper-1 ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug Serving `mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602` with vLLM v0.27.1 (V1 engine), one specific WAV file sent to `/v1/audio/transcriptions` makes the **entire engine hang permanently**: - The log floods with `Realtime model received empty multimodal embeddings for 1 input tokens. Returning zero embeddings to avoid engine crash.` (`voxtral_realtime.py:305`). - The GPU stays at **100 % utilization** and VRAM at ~21/24 GB — the engine appears to decode indefinitely (zero embeddings never produce an EOS). - `/health` stops responding, the port stays open but no request is ever answered. The only way out is killing the vLLM process. - Reproduced **twice in a row** at exactly the same audio file (the first 150 requests of the same benchmark batch all succeeded, then this file hangs the server deterministically). The audio file is **not** silent or unusual: 16 kHz, mono, 16-bit WAV, 5.4 s, RMS −24.5 dBFS, peak −3.8 dBFS, 62 % silence. Its RMS/silence statistics are almost identical to 9 sibling files of the same batch that all transcribe fine. **Failing audio file (for reproduction):** https://drop.n0ne.de/u/NZsVNE.wav ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start vLLM as above (Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602, any GPU with ≥ 16 GB VRAM). 2. Wait for `/health` to return OK. 3. POST the attached WAV to `/v1/audio/transcriptions` (multipart `file`, `model=whisper-1` or any served name, `language=de`). A plain curl `-F file=@...` is enough. 4. Observe: the request never returns, `/health` stops responding, GPU stays at 100 %. Expected behavior: the request either returns a transcription (the reference text of this TTS sample is "Zug einfährt auf Gleis sieben, bitte zurücktreten von der Bahnsteigkante."), or the engine survives and continues serving. Actual behavior: permanent engine hang; the whole server becomes unresponsive and must be restarted. ### Logs Excerpt of `vllm.log` during the hang (repeated thousands of times): ```text (EngineCore pid=2044) WARNING 08-19 09:45:46 [voxtral_realtime.py:305] Realtime model received empty multimodal embeddings for 1 input tokens. Returning zero em (EngineCore pid=2044) WARNING 08-19 09:45:47 [voxtral_realtime.py:305] Realtime model received empty multimodal embeddings for 1 input tokens. Returning zero em (EngineCore pid=2044) WARNING 08-19 09:45:47 [voxtral_realtime.py:305] Realtime model received empty multimodal embeddings for 1 input tokens. Returning zero em ``` Meanwhile `nvidia-smi` reports `100 %, 21208 MiB, 24576 MiB` and `curl /health` times out / returns nothing. ### Related issues — checked, none explains this - **#38233** (closed, "Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime hangs/crashes on multiple sessions due to encoder_cache_usage saturation on 16GB GPU") — multiple `/v1/realtime` sessions and encoder-cache saturation on 16 GB. Ours: a **single** `/v1/audio/transcriptions` request, 24 GB GPU, no cache saturation, no sessions. - **#45022** (open PR, "fix boot-OOM / silent-hang / max-len crash on 16 GiB") — fixes boot-time failures on 16 GiB. Ours: boots fine on 24 GB, hangs after ~150 healthy requests at one specific file. - **#44461** (closed, "Fix token feedback timeout silent hang") — a timeout in the realtime `feed_tokens()` background task. Ours: plain transcription endpoint, no realtime session, no token feedback involved. - **#39229 / #39202** ("Fix Voxtral Realtime crash on mixed-batch transcription") — crash with mixed prefill+decode batches. Ours: `--max-num-seqs 1`, strictly one request at a time, no mixed batch. - **#50860** (open, "Resumable (realtime) sessions retain raw mm_feature.data...") — memory retention across realtime sessions. Ours: single short request, no sessions. The common denominator of the existing reports is that the *zero-embedding fallback* in `voxtral_realtime.py` is a known fragile spot; this report adds a concrete deterministic input that turns that fallback into a **permanent whole-server hang** instead of the intended "keep other requests alive".

signal.title: [Bugfix] Reload speculative draft weights after Level 2 sleep wake
signal.text: Addresses #52479 ## Problem After the documented Level 2 sleep/wake sequence, MTP speculative decoding silently stops helping: every drafted token is rejected (`Mean acceptance length: 1.00`, `Accepted throughput: 0.00`) and decode throughput falls to approximately the no-speculation rate. Target-model outputs remain correct, so the failure appears only as a large performance regression. Level 2 sleep discards draft parameters together with the target parameters. `wake_up()` restores the saved draft buffers, but the documented subsequent `reload_weights()` call reloads only the target model. The drafter is a separate module and therefore continues with discarded parameter storage. ## Fix Put the disk-backed draft reload in `GPUModelRunner.reload_weights` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`), on the existing `weights_iterator is None` path, before the target load: - Resolve the draft through the existing `get_draft_model()` accessor. - Read the configured draft checkpoint with its model loader. MTP configurations without a separate `draft_load_config` use the target load configuration. - Load in place through `initialize_layerwise_reload` / `finalize_layerwise_reload`, preserving the parameter addresses captured by the compiled runtime. - Invoke the helper unbound (`GPUModelRunner._reload_draft_weights_from_disk(self)`) because Model Runner V2 already delegates this method with a V2 `self` and does not inherit the helper. - Reload the target last because EAGLE-style drafts can share embeddings or an output head with it; the target checkpoint therefore remains authoritative for any shared storage. - Leave iterator-based reloads unchanged; those weights are supplied by their caller and are not assumed to contain a second draft checkpoint. Model Runner V2 keeps its existing one-line delegate into that method. There is no V2 wrapper and no production-file diff under `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/`. This mirrors Level 1 sleep semantics: both paths restore the existing target and draft modules in place. Level 1 restores their tagged allocations from host RAM, while Level 2 restores saved buffers during `wake_up()` and reloads model parameters from their disk checkpoints during `reload_weights()`. ### Why not `start_draft_weight_update()`? The draft weight-update API added by #46725 selects the draft as the destination of an already-configured `WeightTransferEngine`. Its built-in NCCL and IPC backends receive weights supplied by an external trainer; they do not accept a checkpoint path or read weights from disk. The API also requires the server to start with `weight_transfer_config`. It remains the correct path for runtime trainer/RL weight transfer; this PR does not replace it. The failing workflow is the separate, documented disk-restore path and does not require a trainer or weight-transfer engine: ```python llm.sleep(level=2) llm.wake_up(tags=["weights"]) llm.collective_rpc("reload_weights") llm.wake_up(tags=["kv_cache"]) ``` This change reuses #46725's `get_draft_model()` accessor and the same layerwise reload lifecycle used by checkpoint-format transfer engines, while keeping the checkpoint source appropriate to this workflow. This is not a duplicate of #46725: that change added externally supplied runtime draft updates, while this PR completes the separate documented disk-backed `reload_weights()` recovery path. ## Live evidence Measured on the previous MRV2-wrapper revision of this PR (same disk draft loader, layerwise lifecycle, and draft-first / target-last order) on 2x RTX 5090, TP=2, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=2`, with sleep mode enabled. Each throughput entry is the median of three 256-token HTTP generations. This head was not re-run on GPU; the placement change is covered by the unit tests below. | State | Throughput | Mean acceptance length | Reload RPC | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Cold baseline | 109.4 tok/s | not recorded | — | | L2 wake cycle 1 | 108.9 tok/s (100% of baseline) | 2.17 | 4.18 s | | L2 wake cycle 2 | 104.9 tok/s (96% of baseline) | 2.43 | 4.11 s | Both cycles used the documented staged sequence above plus a prefix-cache reset. Both produced coherent, non-empty output. The harness's final service restart also completed normally and the health endpoint returned ready. No errors or tracebacks were recorded. Reload RPC timing covers the complete disk-backed draft-plus-target `reload_weights()` call. For comparison, the unpatched reproduction was 51.8 tok/s with acceptance length 1.00 and zero accepted draft tokens. ## Tests Four focused unit tests cover: 1. A disk-backed reload restores the draft through its configured loader and the layerwise lifecycle before reloading the target. 2. The same disk path through Model Runner V2's existing `GPUModelRunnerV1.reload_weights(self, ...)` delegate. 3. A disk-backed reload without a draft still reloads the target normally. 4. A caller-supplied weight iterator does not trigger an implicit draft reload. ```text .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::TestReloadDraftWeights -q # 4 passed ``` ## Scope and limitations - The serving path of interest is Model Runner V2. The implementation lives in the shared `GPUModelRunner.reload_weights` that V2 already calls, so a legacy V1 engine using that method also gets the disk draft reload. - Live validation covers same-checkpoint MTP on one TP=2 hardware/model configuration, measured on the previous wrapper revision. Separate EAGLE checkpoints were not tested live; target-last ordering protects shared target storage, but does not establish compatibility between an arbitrary target and draft checkpoint. - The configured draft checkpoint remains the source of draft weights. This change does not redefine draft selection during `weights_path` model swaps. - Draft formats whose loaders do not implement `get_all_weights` raise `NotImplementedError`, matching the existing target-model disk reload. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, review-response analysis, and test orchestration. The submitter reviewed the changes and the live validation described above.
