signal.title: [WIP] Add Dynamic Context Parallelism for long-context serving
signal.text: ## Summary This is a WIP implementation of Dynamic Context Parallelism (DyCP) for vLLM V1, following the RFC below: - RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/29295 The main goal is to support request-level heterogeneous parallelism across data-parallel attention replicas. Long-sequence requests can be processed cooperatively by multiple DP ranks within a Domain, while short-sequence requests continue to use the normal single-DP path. This PR publishes the current experimental implementation for visibility and design discussion. ## Motivation In large-scale MoE serving, DP-attention + EP has become a common architecture, but production traffic often contains mixed long- and short-sequence workloads. Existing context-parallel strategies are mostly limited within a single DP domain and do not directly solve workload imbalance across DP-attention replicas. This becomes especially visible in PD colocation and PD disaggregation scenarios: - In PD colocation, a long prefill on a single DP rank can serialize attention computation and leave other DP workers underutilized. - In PD disaggregation, long prompts in the decode cluster can inflate the KV-cache working set on one shard, creating stragglers and skewing load balance. DyCP introduces a Domain abstraction above multiple DP ranks and allows the scheduler to dynamically choose CP size per request. ## What Changed - Adds DyCP / domain-parallel configuration: - `--dp-per-domain` - `--num-cp-seqs` - `--long-request-threshold` - Adds V1 `CrossDPScheduler` and `AsyncCrossDPScheduler`. - Adds `CrossDPKVCacheManager` for managing KV cache block allocation across DP ranks inside a Domain. - Adds DYCP process group initialization. - Adds domain engine / engine core launch support for serving and headless paths. - Extends scheduler and model-runner outputs with CP-rank metadata, including CP size and per-rank request placement. - Updates worker, block table, GPU input batch, attention metadata, and cudagraph dispatching paths to handle DyCP requests. - Adds experimental cross-DP KV connector integration. ## Design Context The implementation follows the high-level design in the RFC: - The scheduler introduces a `CrossDPScheduler` path that can produce `list[SchedulerOutput]`, one per CP/DP rank participating in the current step. - The engine/executor path introduces Domain-level orchestration so that multiple DP ranks can be coordinated as one scheduling unit. - The model runner reorders CP requests in the batch to make attention score / LSE aggregation easier. - The KV cache manager uses a cross-DP structure to coordinate block allocation across multiple DP ranks in the same Domain. - The attention path is extended for different CP behavior in prefill and decode. ## Current Status This PR is intentionally WIP and is not ready for final review or merge. The core multi-GPU end-to-end benchmark validation has been completed for the current DyCP decode and Dynamic PrefillCP paths. The remaining WIP items are cleanup-oriented: - Full cleanup of debug comments / experimental code. - Follow-up code refactoring and commit-stack cleanup before this becomes merge-ready. Current scope limitations: - Prefix caching in the cross-DP KV manager is incomplete. - Priority scheduling is not implemented in the cross-DP scheduler. - Encoder input scheduling is not fully implemented in the DyCP path. - Domain parallelism currently has multi-node limitations. - MoE, Mooncake/P-D, and async KV-loading paths are not the primary validated path in this WIP PR. ## Non-Duplicate Check I checked related open PRs and did not find another PR implementing DyCP / cross-DP scheduling. PR #43483 is related to DP load balancing, but it addresses a different problem. ## Preliminary Decode Performance Results Preliminary decode-side benchmark results were collected with DeepSeek-R1 W8A8 on 4 x 8 H800 GPUs, using `Domain4DyCP8`. Workloads include normal 4k context and mixed long-context traffic where 1% of requests use 256k / 512k / 1M context. Metrics are P90 TPOT and P90 ITL. Lower is better. Note: for the `1%512k` and `1%1M` workloads, the DP baseline hit OOM, so only DyCP and DCP results are reported. ### P90 TPOT | Context | System | 1 rps | 2 rps | 4 rps | 8 rps | 16 rps | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4k | DP | 28.70 | 28.65 | 31.95 | 41.61 | 41.24 | | 4k | DyCP | 28.82 | 28.54 | 32.10 | 39.30 | 41.59 | | 4k | DCP | 31.65 | 34.98 | 53.49 | 66.16 | 67.86 | | 1%256k | DP | 36.27 | 38.67 | 41.28 | 50.12 | 49.44 | | 1%256k | DyCP | 33.08 | 37.16 | 38.69 | 47.73 | 49.28 | | 1%256k | DCP | 36.53 | 42.98 | 60.09 | 69.03 | 70.10 | | 1%512k | DP | OOM | OOM | OOM | OOM | OOM | | 1%512k | DyCP | 34.89 | 39.53 | 41.64 | 50.67 | 51.58 | | 1%512k | DCP | 38.74 | 43.19 | 64.80 | 72.07 | 72.56 | | 1%1M | DP | OOM | OOM | OOM | OOM | OOM | | 1%1M | DyCP | 36.59 | 42.33 | 47.72 | 55.80 | 59.10 | | 1%1M | DCP | 44.14 | 49.49 | 74.52 | 77.87 | 77.31 | ### P90 ITL | Context | System | 1 rps | 2 rps | 4 rps | 8 rps | 16 rps | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4k | DP | 28.88 | 29.05 | 32.99 | 43.86 | 44.06 | | 4k | DyCP | 29.29 | 29.72 | 34.87 | 46.78 | 49.81 | | 4k | DCP | 31.96 | 36.12 | 56.96 | 74.76 | 75.00 | | 1%256k | DP | 36.76 | 39.28 | 42.55 | 52.92 | 52.65 | | 1%256k | DyCP | 33.19 | 37.99 | 41.44 | 54.46 | 55.13 | | 1%256k | DCP | 36.56 | 43.65 | 63.98 | 77.70 | 76.97 | | 1%512k | DP | OOM | OOM | OOM | OOM | OOM | | 1%512k | DyCP | 35.11 | 40.22 | 44.25 | 56.42 | 56.47 | | 1%512k | DCP | 39.41 | 45.45 | 70.53 | 79.85 | 80.79 | | 1%1M | DP | OOM | OOM | OOM | OOM | OOM | | 1%1M | DyCP | 37.01 | 42.83 | 48.83 | 58.39 | 59.99 | | 1%1M | DCP | 44.94 | 51.84 | 79.93 | 84.91 | 84.32 | Overall, DyCP preserves near-DP behavior on short-context traffic and avoids DP OOM on the 512k / 1M mixed long-context workloads. Compared with DCP, DyCP reduces P90 TPOT by roughly 8.5% to 40.6% and P90 ITL by roughly 8.4% to 38.9% in these preliminary runs. ## Additional Dynamic PrefillCP Results We also collected preliminary Dynamic PrefillCP results on DeepSeek-V2-Lite with 8 x H800 GPUs. This benchmark was collected under a concurrent 1M-request serving run: all services were running at the same time and processing the 1M-request workload. The table reports TTFT at different context lengths observed in that run. Lower is better. | Context | DP TTFT | Static PrefillCP TTFT | Dynamic PrefillCP TTFT | |---|---:|---:|---:| | 1k | 6779.72 | 7914.02 | 6631.87 | | 2k | 6794.65 | 7693.53 | 6600.88 | | 4k | 6842.30 | 7678.62 | 6602.14 | | 8k | 6932.31 | 7780.02 | 6671.67 | | 16k | 7066.20 | 8130.26 | 6856.81 | | 32k | 7670.29 | 8203.37 | 7914.19 | | 64k | 8283.04 | 9033.21 | 7946.18 | | 128k | 15005.76 | 10845.96 | 10810.29 | | 256k | 33296.49 | 14595.38 | 14431.86 | | 512k | 90435.45 | 22204.50 | 21759.60 | | 1M | 245852.50 | 43171.60 | 43045.48 | In this concurrent 1M-request run, Dynamic PrefillCP improves TTFT over Static PrefillCP across all reported context lengths. Compared with DP, it keeps similar TTFT for short contexts and significantly reduces long-context TTFT, especially from 128k onward. ## Test Plan Current verification includes multi-GPU end-to-end benchmark runs and a local Python compile check. Checked locally: ```bash PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/private/tmp/vllm-pycache python3 -m py_compile \ vllm/v1/core/sched/cross_dp_scheduler.py \ vllm/v1/core/cross_dp_kv_cache_manager.py \ vllm/v1/core/sched/dynamic_bucket_load_balancer.py \ vllm/v1/engine/core.py \ vllm/v1/engine/utils.py \ vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu_input_batch.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py \ vllm/v1/cudagraph_dispatcher.py \ vllm/engine/arg_utils.py \ vllm/config/parallel.py \ vllm/config/scheduler.py ``` Result: passed locally with Python 3.9.6. Completed multi-GPU end-to-end validation: - Decode-side DeepSeek-R1 W8A8 benchmark on 4 x 8 H800 GPUs with `Domain4DyCP8`. - Dynamic PrefillCP DeepSeek-V2-Lite benchmark on 8 x H800 GPUs under a concurrent 1M-request serving run. Remaining work before this becomes merge-ready: - Full cleanup of debug comments / experimental code. - Follow-up code refactoring and commit-stack cleanup.

signal.title: fix(structured_output): pass new_token_ids to should_advance() to fix MTP spec-decode off-by-one
signal.text: Fixes #34650. ## Problem When Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) speculative decoding accepts a draft token, `_update_after_schedule` pre-increments `num_computed_tokens` by `(1 main + N spec)` tokens **before** model execution. After `update_from_output` appends the accepted tokens, the index-based delta in `should_advance()` starts one position past the main token. This means a `</think>` token emitted as the main token is silently missed: `reasoning_ended` is never set to `True`, and grammar constraints (JSON mode, structured output) are **permanently disabled** for the rest of the request. Users running Qwen3 models with MTP enabled see unstructured output with no error or warning. ## Root Cause `should_advance()` infers which new tokens to scan by computing a delta from `num_computed_tokens`: ```python delta_from = request.num_computed_tokens - request.num_output_placeholders start = delta_from if delta_from >= 0 else max(len(all_token_ids) + delta_from, 0) ``` After an MTP step, `num_computed_tokens` has already been pre-incremented to include the spec tokens, so `start` lands past the `</think>` token — it is never examined by `is_reasoning_end_streaming`. ## Fix Add an optional `new_token_ids: list[int] | None = None` parameter to `should_advance()`. The one call site inside `update_from_output()` already holds the accepted token list, so passing it directly bypasses the broken index arithmetic: ```python # scheduler.py — caller passes accepted tokens directly if new_token_ids and self.structured_output_manager.should_advance( request, new_token_ids ): # structured_output/__init__.py — use provided delta when available if new_token_ids is not None: delta: Iterable[int] = new_token_ids else: # existing path for non-MTP callers: async-scheduling-aware delta delta_from = request.num_computed_tokens - request.num_output_placeholders ... delta = itertools.islice(all_token_ids, start, None) if reasoner.is_reasoning_end_streaming(all_token_ids, delta): ``` All other call sites (`update_draft_token_ids`, `update_draft_token_ids_in_output`) omit the new parameter and continue using the existing async-scheduling-aware delta, which is correct for those contexts. ## Tests `tests/v1/structured_output/test_reasoning_structured_output.py` — added `test_mtp_reasoning_grammar_not_disabled`: - Simulates an MTP step by pre-incrementing `num_computed_tokens` as `_update_after_schedule` would - Calls `update_from_output` with a `</think>` token appended - Asserts `reasoning_ended` is `True` (was `False` before fix) - Asserts `should_advance()` returns `True`, confirming grammar is still enabled

signal.title: [Core] FlowPrefill: adaptive sub-chunk preemption for v1 Scheduler
signal.text: ## Purpose Implements **FlowPrefill** - adaptive sub-chunk preemption for long prefill requests in vLLM v1 (Q2 2026 roadmap item: "avoid excessive preemption, prefill HoL blocking", #39749, now closed). **Problem:** In vLLM's v1 scheduler, long prefill chunks monopolize GPU time for 50–200 ms, causing decode TPOT spikes when new decode requests arrive mid-prefill. There is no mechanism to yield GPU mid-chunk - the entire chunk must complete before decodes can be serviced. **Solution:** `FlowPrefillMixin` integrates CUDA event checkpoints at sub-chunk granularity. A non-blocking `Event.query()` detects decode pressure (queue depth ≥ `preemption_decode_threshold`). When pressure is detected at a checkpoint boundary, the scheduler suspends the current prefill and resumes from that token position in the next scheduling cycle, preserving all allocated KV blocks and adding zero `.synchronize()` calls. **Result — real server A/B** (Qwen3-1.7B, `vllm bench serve`, concurrency=4, random dataset; full methodology and the starvation bug this required fixing are below): | Config | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | P99 TTFT | |---|---|---|---| | No FlowPrefill (plain scheduler) | 449.84ms | 417.72ms | 990.66ms | | FlowPrefill, with `preemption_max_suspend_ms` bound | 411.73ms | 427.04ms | 778.79ms | **FlowPrefill beats the plain scheduler on every TTFT metric** (mean -8.5%, P99 -21.4%) on this workload. **Key design decisions:** - **Zero-overhead when disabled:** `FlowPrefillMixin` activates only when `SchedulerConfig.preemption_granularity` is not `None`. Default `None` preserves 100% of existing behavior — no code path change. - **MRO-safe mixin:** `class Scheduler(FlowPrefillMixin, SchedulerInterface)` - placed first in MRO so hooks can be cleanly overridden. - **Pre-allocated event pool:** `CudaEventPool` pre-allocates 256 `torch.cuda.Event` instances at init time, avoiding per-scheduling-step allocation overhead. - **Cooperative suspension:** `PrefillCheckpointState` tracks the suspension position and KV block count; the scheduler resumes by feeding tokens from `[checkpoint_pos : checkpoint_pos + granularity]` with existing KV cache intact. - **Starvation bound (`preemption_max_suspend_ms`, default 50ms):** see "Bug found during benchmarking" below — without this, a suspended prefill can starve indefinitely under sustained decode load. **Files changed:** | File | Change | |------|--------| | `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` | `PrefillCheckpointState`, `CudaEventPool`, `FlowPrefillMixin`; `Scheduler` wires hooks in `__init__` and `schedule()` | | `vllm/config/scheduler.py` | `preemption_granularity: int \| None = None`, `preemption_decode_threshold: int = 1`, `preemption_max_suspend_ms: int = 50` fields | | `vllm/engine/arg_utils.py` | `--preemption-granularity` CLI argument | | `tests/v1/core/test_flowprefill.py` | 21 unit tests (no GPU required) covering all code paths, including forced-resume-at-timeout and no-resume-before-timeout | This PR does not duplicate any existing open PR - verified against the current vllm-project/vllm PR list. Related: vLLM Q2 2026 roadmap, FlowPrefill paper (arXiv Feb 2026). > **AI assistance disclosure:** This PR was co-authored with Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Claude Code). I have reviewed all changed lines end-to-end and can explain any part of the implementation. ## Bug found during benchmarking, and the fix `preemption_decode_threshold` gated both suspend (`depth >= threshold`) and resume (`depth < threshold`) with no hysteresis gap. Under sustained decode load, queue depth can stay `>= threshold` indefinitely, so a checkpointed prefill never resumes — inflating TTFT instead of improving it. This didn't show up in the unit tests (mocked events, no real queue-depth dynamics) — only a real server benchmark surfaced it. **Fix:** added `preemption_max_suspend_ms` (default 50ms) as a starvation bound — a suspended checkpoint force-resumes on its next eligible step once it's waited this long, regardless of decode pressure. ## Test Plan ```bash # No GPU required - FlowPrefill scheduler tests use mocked CUDA events # 1. FlowPrefill unit tests (21 tests) PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_flowprefill.py -v --tb=short # 2. Full scheduler regression suite PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q --tb=short # 3. Real server A/B (see below) vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B ... vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --max-concurrency 4 ... ``` ## Test Result **Unit tests** — 21/21 passed (19 original + 2 new covering the starvation-bound fix). **Scheduler regression suite** — 71/102 passed, 31 pre-existing failures. All 31 failures (`test_ec_connector_*`, `test_eagle3_mm_encoder_cache_with_shift`, `test_schedule_multimodal_requests`, `test_schedule_partial_requests`, `test_no_mm_input_chunking`, `test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_*`) are confirmed pre-existing on upstream main — reproduced with identical output by checking out main and running the same suite. Zero regressions introduced by this PR. | Suite | Before (main) | After (this PR) | Delta | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `test_flowprefill.py` | N/A (new file) | 21/21 ✅ | +21 | | `test_scheduler.py` | 71/102 (31 pre-existing fails) | 71/102 | 0 regressions | **Real server A/B benchmark** (Qwen3-1.7B, `vllm bench serve`, concurrency=4, random dataset) — this is the result that actually matters, and it's why the starvation-bound fix above exists: | Config | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | P99 TTFT | |---|---|---|---| | No FlowPrefill (plain scheduler) | 449.84ms | 417.72ms | 990.66ms | | FlowPrefill, unbounded suspend (the bug above) | 969.43ms | 655.17ms | 2256.12ms | | FlowPrefill, with `preemption_max_suspend_ms` bound | 411.73ms | 427.04ms | 778.79ms | Without the bound, FlowPrefill made TTFT more than 2x worse than the plain scheduler. With the bound, it beats the plain scheduler on every TTFT metric (mean -8.5%, median +2.2% within noise, P99 -21.4%). **Behaviour Table:** | `preemption_granularity` | Behavior | | --- | --- | | `None` (default) | Identical to upstream — `FlowPrefillMixin` adds no overhead, no code path change | | `256` (example) | Checkpoint every 256 tokens; decode pressure triggers suspension at next boundary, force-resumes after `preemption_max_suspend_ms` regardless of pressure | **Hardware:** Linux/WSL2, RTX 3070Ti (sm_86), PyTorch 2.6.0+cu124, CUDA 13.3 ## Open question on scope/fit This PR was written against the Q2 2026 roadmap item "avoid excessive preemption, prefill HoL blocking" (#39749, now closed). I noticed vllm-project/vllm#37308 (the closest real-world HoL-blocking report) traces its root cause to CPU-side engine-loop scheduling stalls rather than GPU-level prefill monopolization — a different layer than what this PR's CUDA-event checkpointing addresses. Happy to discuss whether this is still a fit for the Q3 "Scheduler refactoring" direction (#48168) or if it should be scoped differently. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR: implements FlowPrefill adaptive sub-chunk preemption for v1 Scheduler; zero-overhead when disabled (default). - [x] The test plan: pytest tests/v1/core/test_flowprefill.py -v (no GPU needed); regression run on full tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py; real server A/B via vllm bench serve. - [x] The test results: 21/21 new tests pass; all 31 scheduler failures are pre-existing on upstream main — zero regressions; real A/B shows a genuine TTFT win after fixing a starvation bug the benchmark itself surfaced. - [ ] Documentation update: no user-facing doc changes needed until the feature graduates from experimental. `--preemption-granularity` CLI flag is self-documenting; field docstrings in `SchedulerConfig` cover the API. </details>

signal.title: [Kimi K3][Pref] Export prefill checkpoints in a single FlashKDA pass
signal.text: ## Purpose This PR adds an optional Kimi-K3 prefill checkpoint mode for fine-grained prefix caching. When enabled, FlashKDA exports an intermediate recurrent-state checkpoint during the prefill. The checkpoint is stored in an internal request-owned Mamba block, allowing prefix cache entries smaller than the Mamba block size to be reused without an additional FlashKDA forward. Main changes: - Export recurrent-state checkpoints from the existing packed FlashKDA prefill. - Export the matching causal-conv state. - Support partial prefix caching. - Add internal checkpoint block allocation, lifecycle management, and scheduler metadata. - Allow the scheduler to skip the additional checkpoint-boundary forward. - Add unit tests for checkpoint metadata, block lifecycle, and prefix caching. [#52789](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52789) introduced the prefill-checkpoint infrastructure. This PR adds efficient support for fine-grained partial prefix caching and exports the checkpoint directly from the existing FlashKDA kernel, avoiding an additional or split FlashKDA forward. ## Usage ```bash VLLM_KIMI_K3_KDA_CHECKPOINT_MODE=1 \ vllm serve <model> \ --kda-prefill-backend flashkda \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --mamba-cache-mode align \ --prefix-match-unit 128 ``` This PR depends on [vllm-project/FlashKDA#7](https://github.com/vllm-project/FlashKDA/pull/7). The FlashKDA commit is temporarily pinned and should be updated after that PR is merged. ## Test Plan Setup: - TP8 on 2 × 4 GB300 - Growing prefix from 120K to 164K tokens - +2K tokens per round - 8 concurrent streams - Three runs per variant ## Test Result | Variant | P50 TTFT | **Improvement** | | --- | ---: | ---: | | #52789, non-partial | 2,151.53 ms | Baseline | | #52789, partial128 | 2,375.23 ms | **-10.40%** | | This PR, non-partial | 2,141.67 ms | Baseline | | **This PR, partial128** | **1,398.49 ms** | **34.70%** | ## Correctness Three consecutive full OCRBench runs with checkpoint mode and partial128 produced: 89.4% 89.6% 89.3% mean: 89.43% --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix][Core] Ignore stale KV transfer completions
signal.text: ## Purpose Fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46240 Prevent stale, duplicate, or out-of-order KV transfer completion notifications from crashing the scheduler or freeing blocks owned by a live request. `KVConnectorOutput.finished_recving` and `finished_sending` currently identify a transfer only by request ID. A delayed completion may therefore arrive after the request has been removed, or after the same request has moved into a different lifecycle state. The scheduler currently treats these cases as fatal ownership violations: ```python assert req_id in self.requests assert RequestStatus.is_finished(req.status) ``` This PR makes KV transfer completion handling idempotent and state-aware: - Ignore and log completions for request IDs that no longer exist. - Free blocks when the corresponding request is already finished. - Ignore and log unexpected completions for a live request instead of freeing blocks belonging to its current lifecycle. - Apply the same protection to both receive and send completions. - Add regression tests for unknown request IDs and duplicate/out-of-order completions targeting a running request. ### Duplicate-work check - #46304 overlaps with this PR for completions targeting an already-freed request and the same-step finished_recving/finished_sending case. This PR additionally covers stale or out-of-order completions whose request ID still exists but now belongs to a live lifecycle, such as a request that has already been promoted to RUNNING. In that case, checking only whether the request ID exists is insufficient and may still assert or free live blocks. - #50565 fixes a Mooncake-specific cleanup-only pull after an early abort. It does not cover connector-agnostic delayed or duplicate completion paths ## Test Plan ``` .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py -v ``` ## Test Result --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signal.title: [Bugfix][Model][NVIDIA] Fix DeepSeek V4 mHC TileLang warmup for nvidi…
signal.text: [Bugfix][Model][NVIDIA] Fix DeepSeek V4 mHC TileLang warmup for nvidia GPU backend ## Purpose The native `deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup` was a no-op on nvidia GPU (CUDA) models because `_find_first_mhc_layer` required `hc_pre`/`hc_post` CustomOp attributes that the nvidia `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` does not have — it calls tilelang functions (`mhc_pre_tilelang`, `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang`, `mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang`, `mhc_post_tilelang`, `hc_head_fused_kernel_tilelang`) directly instead of going through CustomOp wrappers. This caused TileLang JIT compilations during inference, creating ~6 second latency spikes on every new token count (up to ~40 minutes of cumulative compilations on a cold start). Fixes #51790. Extends #51802 with full grid coverage. ## Changes 1. **`_find_first_mhc_layer`**: Added dual detection — checks for `hc_pre`/`hc_post` (AMD/XPU CustomOp path) OR `attn_norm`/`ffn_norm` (nvidia tilelang path). Both backends are recognized. 2. **`_warmup_nvidia_layer_mhc`** (new): Warmup path for nvidia models. Calls the same five tilelang functions (`mhc_pre_tilelang`, `mhc_pre_broadcast_tilelang`, `mhc_fused_post_pre_tilelang`, `mhc_post_tilelang`, `hc_head_fused_kernel_tilelang`) that the real `forward()` uses, with actual layer parameters (attention/FFN weights, normalization params, broadcast weights). 3. **`_warmup_hc_head`**: When `hc_head_op` CustomOp is absent (nvidia), falls back to the underlying tilelang function via `_get_tilelang_mhc_ops()`. 4. **Expanded `_DEFAULT_TOKEN_SIZE_CANDIDATES`**: Increased from 15 (powers of 2 only) to 42 values covering all unique grid thresholds for both broadcast (21) and fused (26) n_splits kernels. This ensures every kernel variant is pre-compiled during startup, eliminating runtime TileLang JIT compilations. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup.py ruff check vllm/model_executor/warmup/deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup.py tests/model_executor/test_deepseek_v4_mhc_warmup.py ``` ## Test Result - `pytest` — 6 passed - `ruff check` — passed - **End-to-end validation on NVIDIA GPU:** - Built Docker image with fix, deployed vLLM server (TP=4, EP=4) - Native warmup at startup compiled all 42 token-size variants covering all 21 broadcast + 26 fused n_splits thresholds (previously 0 compilations on nvidia) - After warmup, sent real inference requests (`thinking_token_budget=16000`, `max_tokens=16000`) - **Zero TileLang JIT compilations during inference** — confirmed via `jit_monitor` logs --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR: fix DeepSeek V4 mHC TileLang warmup being a no-op on nvidia GPU backend, causing ~6s latency spikes during inference - [x] The test plan: pre-commit ruff check, pytest - [x] The test results: ruff passes, all 6 tests pass, all TileLang kernels compile during startup, zero compilations during inference - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update: N/A </details>

signal.title: [Security] Fix remote DoS from grammar-rejected spec tokens padded with -1
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-55m4-88pw-2875 When structured output invalidates speculative draft slots, the scheduler pads them with -1 for bitmask layout. This allows invalid token IDs (-1) to reach GPU embeddings, causing a remote denial of service. **Fix:** - Cap accepted tokens to the grammar-valid prefix in `update_from_output` - Sanitize -1 before writing spec tokens to `token_ids_cpu` so invalid IDs cannot reach GPU embeddings ## Test plan - Added regression tests in `tests/v1/core/test_ghsa_invalid_spec_tokens.py` - Added unit test in `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_input_batch.py` - Verified the fix prevents invalid token IDs from reaching the GPU embedding layer ## Notes - AI assistance was used in developing this fix (per AGENTS.md) - This fix was developed in the GHSA private fork and is now submitted for public review Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

The exact failing test did not run before merge. ## Validation - `uvx ruff check` on all changed Python files: passed - `git diff --cached --check` before commit: passed - [Exact H100 MoE Refactor targeted Buildkite #84570](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/84570): passed at exact head `fe30af71ea2a5fcc1e03dab6b3c3495ed10e26f0` - The formerly failing `Qwen3-30B-A3B-Fp8-CT-Block-marlin` configuration passed. - The complete selected GSM8K inventory passed: 12 passed / 0 failed in 47m14s. ## Model evaluation No separate local model evaluation was run. Targeted #84570 ran the exact H100 GSM8K integration inventory at the PR head and passed all 12 configurations, including the regression case. ## Duplicate-work check Searched open issues and pull requests for `weight_scale_inv QKVParallelLinear marlin`, `#52182`, and Marlin backend regressions. signal.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] DFlash2: accept unquantized linear LM heads in the candidate selector
signal.text: ## Purpose Stacked on **#52816** — this branch is `19c93519` plus one commit, so the diff above includes that PR's changes. Retarget to `main` once #52816 merges; the diff then collapses to the single fix commit. `DFlash2Qwen3ForCausalLM.compute_candidates` guards the LM head with `isinstance(self.lm_head.quant_method, UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod)`, but that class only appears when the model has no quant config at all. A quantization config that leaves the head unquantized — INC, ModelOpt, fp8 with excluded layers, ... — returns `UnquantizedLinearMethod` for a `ParallelLMHead` (the same class it returns for any unquantized linear). A quantized-body target with an unquantized head therefore fails to start: ``` ValueError: DFlash2 requires an unquantized target LM head for candidate TopK. ``` Reproduced with `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B` (INC-int4, head unquantized) as target and `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` as drafter, TP2 on dual RTX 3090. Both classes are unquantized and their `apply()` dispatches the same unquantized GEMM, so the guard now accepts either, and the error names the offending method. Also types the `config` parameter as `Qwen3Config` to match the base class signature. ## Why this is not a duplicate #52816 introduces the DFlash2 architecture; this PR only fixes the LM-head guard in the code that PR adds, on top of its head. No other open PR touches this path. ## Test plan - `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on the touched file → clean. - Startup with the INC-int4 target above; drafts k=7, measure acceptance. - (to be filled with exact commands + results) ## Test Result (to be filled) ## Note AI assistance (pi coding agent) was used for the fix and this description; every changed line was reviewed and tested by the submitter.

signal.title: fix(kv_cache): domain-tag LoRA and cache_salt prefix-cache keys to prevent collision (#44701)
signal.text: ## Summary `generate_block_hash_extra_keys` appends LoRA names and `cache_salt` into the **same** `extra_keys` tuple as bare strings, with no domain separation: ```python lora_extra_keys: list[str] = _gen_lora_extra_hash_keys(request) # [lora_name] cache_salt_keys: list[str] = [request.cache_salt] if ... else [] # [cache_salt] extra_keys = lora_extra_keys + mm_extra_keys + cache_salt_keys + prompt_embeds_keys ``` Because both are untagged single strings, a **LoRA request** with `lora_name == "X"` and no `cache_salt` produces the **same** first-block hash as a **base-model request** with `cache_salt == "X"` and no LoRA, for identical prompt tokens. Reported and dynamically reproduced in #44701. This is a correctness/isolation problem: - `cache_salt` exists specifically to **isolate** prefix-cache entries between callers. A LoRA adapter whose name equals someone's salt silently defeats that isolation. - A base-model request can receive a prefix-cache hit on a block whose KV was computed under **LoRA weights**, yielding wrong outputs. ## Fix Domain-tag the two sources so their keys live in distinct namespaces and can no longer collide: ```python return [("lora", request.lora_request.lora_name)] ... [("cache_salt", request.cache_salt)] ``` `mm_extra_keys` already use `(identifier, offset)` tuples and prompt-embeds keys are raw `bytes`, so all four sources are now mutually distinguishable. The change is confined to key construction; hashing logic is untouched. ## Test plan - [x] Updated existing assertions in `test_kv_cache_utils.py` to the new tagged shape (`("cache_salt", "salt")`, `("lora", "test_lora_adapter")`). - [x] Added `test_generate_block_hash_extra_keys_lora_cache_salt_no_collision` — a LoRA adapter and a base request sharing the string `"COLLIDE"` must now produce different extra keys. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: [Bugfix][Parser] Fix DeepSeek V4 and V3.2 tool argument streaming (#52846)
signal.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52846. In DeepSeek V4 and DeepSeek V3.2 parsers (`vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py` and `vllm/parser/deepseek_v32.py`), `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")` was configured. During streaming tool calls, when generating a long string parameter body (e.g. `{"text": "..."}`), the incoming token chunks do not contain `>`. As a result, `ParserEngine._compute_arg_delta()` returned `None` for every single body chunk because `self._arg_structural_chars.isdisjoint(raw_delta)` evaluated to `True`. The entire string parameter body was withheld and buffered until the closing `</parameter>` tag arrived, at which point all accumulated characters were emitted in one large delta. While `_safe_arg_prefix()` was added in #46351 specifically to stream prefix-stable string values for schema-typed properties, it never executed for parameter body chunks because the `arg_structural_chars` check discarded them beforehand. This PR removes `arg_structural_chars=frozenset(">")` from `deepseek_v4_config()` and `deepseek_v32_config()`, allowing `_dsml_arg_converter` and `_safe_arg_prefix` to stream string argument deltas incrementally in real time as tokens are generated. cc @thegoldenflow @flexwang @keivenchang @YilongL @QwertyJack ### Duplicate Work Check - Verified open and unassigned on #52846 (`gh issue view 52846 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments`). - Verified 0 open PRs for issue #52846 (`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "52846 in:body"`). - Verified no open PRs addressing DeepSeek tool-argument streaming (`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "deepseek v4 tool"`). ## Test Plan - Added regression test `TestLongStringParameterStreaming::test_long_string_parameter_incremental_streaming` in `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py`. - Verified that a long string argument (4096 characters) streams incrementally across chunks before the closing tag, with exact JSON reconstruction. - Verified that all 3,791 parser engine tests pass. Commands run: ```bash pytest tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py -v pytest tests/parser/engine/ -v ruff check vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py vllm/parser/deepseek_v32.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py ruff format --check vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py vllm/parser/deepseek_v32.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py ``` ## Test Result ```text tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py ... 65 passed in 1.07s ============================ 3791 passed in 25.18s ============================ ruff check vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py vllm/parser/deepseek_v32.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py All checks passed! ruff format --check vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py vllm/parser/deepseek_v32.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py 3 files already formatted ``` --- *AI Assistance Disclosure: AI assistance was used in analyzing the parser regression, adding regression tests, and formatting the PR description per AGENTS.md.*

signal.title: [XPU] Add block FP8 AsyncTP all-gather collective fusion
signal.text: ## Purpose This PR extends AsyncTP (asynchronous tensor-parallel collective fusion, added for per-channel static-scale FP8 in #52683) on XPU to **block-quantized** W8A8 FP8 GEMM — i.e. models with a 2D `weight_scale_inv` tensor (`block_structure=[128,128]`, e.g. DeepSeek-style block-FP8 checkpoints), building on top of the existing block-FP8 SP support (#49009). The pattern matcher and replacement in `collective_fusion.py` now recognize block-FP8's 2D per-block scale GEMM alongside the existing per-channel static-scale GEMM, fusing GEMM + its surrounding reduce-scatter/all-gather collectives into a single kernel once a prefill batch clears the SP token threshold. Validation uses `RedHatAI/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-block`, the same Llama-3.1-8B architecture and SP threshold as the static-FP8 8B case (`../w8a8-fp8-static-8b/pr.md`), to confirm block-FP8's 2D weight-scale tensor works correctly with AsyncTP and quantify any difference in gains versus the per-channel static-scale variant. This is a re-run with the previously-missing `asynctp_off` (SP-only) arm and GSM8K accuracy added for all four arms, to isolate whether the mixed prefill+decode regression seen in the first pass comes from SP or from the GEMM-comm fusion (AsyncTP) on top of it. --- ## Test Setup **Model**: `RedHatAI/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-block` **Hardware**: 4× Intel Arc Pro B60 (TP=4) **SP threshold**: `(8 MiB × TP=4) / (hidden=4096 × 2 bytes)` = **4096 tokens** (identical to the static-FP8 8B case, since architecture/hidden_size match). Four arms are compared: | Arm | Server command suffix | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `eager` | `--enforce-eager` | no-compile baseline | | `compile_nosp` | `--compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":false},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}'` | plain-compile baseline | | `asynctp_off` | `--compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":true},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}'` | SP only (AsyncTP off) | | `asynctp_on` | `--compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":true,"fuse_gemm_comms":true},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}'` | SP + AsyncTP | --- ## Commands ### Server (replace `<COMPILATION_CONFIG>` with one of the configs above) ```bash VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \ python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model RedHatAI/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-block \ --trust-remote-code \ --dtype bfloat16 \ -tp 4 \ --gpu-memory-util 0.9 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --max-model-len 8192 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ <COMPILATION_CONFIG> ``` ### Benchmark ```bash python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench serve \ --model RedHatAI/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-block \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 4096 \ --random-output-len 1 \ --num-prompt 16 \ --request-rate inf \ --backend vllm \ --ignore-eos \ --trust-remote-code \ --temperature 0 ``` For the mixed prefill+decode shapes, use `--random-input-len 256 --random-output-len 128 --num-prompt 16` or `--random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 64 --num-prompt 32`. ### Accuracy (GSM8K, 250 questions) Accuracy is measured per arm. Start the server with the arm's compilation config, then run lm_eval while the server is running. Repeat for each arm. **Step 1 — start server** (shown for `asynctp_on`; substitute config for other arms): ```bash VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \ python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model RedHatAI/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-block \ --trust-remote-code --dtype bfloat16 -tp 4 \ --gpu-memory-util 0.9 --max-model-len 8192 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --compilation-config '{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":true,"fuse_gemm_comms":true},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}' ``` | Arm | `--compilation-config` / flag | |---|---| | `asynctp_on` | `{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":true,"fuse_gemm_comms":true},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}` | | `asynctp_off` | `{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":true},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}` | | `compile_nosp` | `{"pass_config":{"enable_sp":false},"use_inductor_graph_partition":true}` | | `eager` | `--enforce-eager` (no `--compilation-config`) | **Step 2 — evaluate** (same command for all arms): ```bash python3 -m lm_eval --model local-completions \ --model_args "model=RedHatAI/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-block,base_url=http://localhost:8073/v1,tokenized_requests=False,num_concurrent=1" \ --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --limit 250 ``` --- ## Performance Results ### Pure prefill — `output_len=1`, mean TTFT (ms), mean of 2 runs Gain = (compile_nosp − X) / compile_nosp; positive = X is faster. | Shape | asynctp_on | asynctp_off | compile_nosp | eager | **on vs nosp** | **off vs nosp (SP only)** | **on vs off (AsyncTP-only)** | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 16 prompts × 4096 in | 8879 | 9364 | 10323 | 10653 | **+14.0%** | +9.3% | +5.2% | | 16 prompts × 512 in | 1554 | 1561 | 1756 | 1806 | **+11.5%** | +11.1% | +0.5% | | 2 prompts × 4096 in | 1265 | 1304 | 1509 | 1558 | **+16.2%** | +13.6% | +3.0% | Consistent with the static-FP8 8B case: SP alone captures most of the gain (+9–14%), and AsyncTP's GEMM-comm fusion adds a further +0.5–5.2% on top. ### Mixed prefill + decode — mean of 2 runs Gain = (compile_nosp − X) / compile_nosp for Duration/TPOT/TTFT (positive = X faster); (X − compile_nosp) / compile_nosp for tok/s (positive = X higher throughput). | Shape | asynctp_on | asynctp_off | compile_nosp | eager | **on vs nosp** | **off vs nosp (SP only)** | **on vs off (AsyncTP-only)** | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | **Duration (s)** ↓ lower is better | | | | | | | | | 16 prompts × 256 in × 128 out | 4.13 | 3.38 | 3.76 | 4.30 | −9.7% | **+10.1%** | −22.2% | | 32 prompts × 128 in × 64 out | 2.67 | 2.10 | 2.42 | 3.07 | −10.4% | **+13.0%** | −27.1% | | **Output tok/s** ↑ higher is better | | | | | | | | | 16 prompts × 256 in × 128 out | 502 | 608 | 549 | 477 | −8.6% | **+10.7%** | −17.4% | | 32 prompts × 128 in × 64 out | 769 | 977 | 848 | 672 | −9.3% | **+15.3%** | −21.3% | | **TPOT (ms)** ↓ lower is better | | | | | | | | | 16 prompts × 256 in × 128 out | 25.7 | 19.4 | 21.1 | 26.5 | −21.7% | **+8.3%** | −32.6% | | 32 prompts × 128 in × 64 out | 31.1 | 22.6 | 25.4 | 35.1 | −22.7% | **+11.0%** | −37.6% | | **Mean TTFT (ms)** ↓ lower is better | | | | | | | | | 16 prompts × 256 in × 128 out | 838.5 | 904.1 | 1072.6 | 894.9 | **+21.8%** | +15.7% | +7.3% | | 32 prompts × 128 in × 64 out | 677.2 | 650.1 | 801.7 | 832.8 | **+15.5%** | +18.9% | −4.2% | --- ## Accuracy (GSM8K, 250 questions) | Arm | Accuracy | |---|---:| | asynctp_on (SP + AsyncTP) | 0.784 | | compile_nosp | 0.776 | | eager | 0.772 | | asynctp_off (SP only) | 0.768 | --- ## Summary - **Pure prefill**: SP alone gives +9–14% TTFT; AsyncTP's GEMM-comm fusion adds +0.5–5.2% on top. Clean win, consistent with the static-FP8 8B case, and no accuracy regression. - **Mixed prefill+decode**: SP alone (`asynctp_off`) is still a clean win (+8–15% duration/tok/s/TPOT). But AsyncTP (`asynctp_on`, `fuse_gemm_comms=True`) turns that into a ~9–10% net *loss* vs. `compile_nosp` — a real, repeatable ~20–27pp swing (confirmed stable across both runs on the 32:128:64 shape). **The regression is caused by AsyncTP's GEMM-comm fusion specifically, not by SP.** (Mean TTFT is a queueing artifact on these two shapes and should be ignored — duration/tok/s/TPOT are authoritative.) - **Accuracy**: no statistically significant regression from either SP or AsyncTP (0.768–0.784 across all four arms, well within ±2.6pp SE). - **Recommendation**: enable SP (`enable_sp=true`) for this model/workload without reservation. Do **not** enable `fuse_gemm_comms` unconditionally for block-FP8 8B until the mixed-shape regression is root-caused (likely the fused GEMM-comm collective's overhead isn't hidden by the small per-rank compute chunk in these batch/output-length combos) — either gate it more precisely or scope this case's recommendation to pure-prefill-dominated deployments only.
